research.scope: Celonis — market leader in process mining / process intelligence; primary source of FlowMiner lost deals. Covers: Process Copilot/AI, EMS/Execution Management, PQL, Action Flows, Studio, onboarding, time-to-value, consulting/SI dependency, pricing opacity, data pipeline complexity, lock-in. Research based on G2, PeerSpot, Gartner Peer Insights, TrustRadius, Capterra, Findstack, SelectHub, SpendHound, Vendr, Celonis Community forums, TechTarget, ProcessExcellenceNetwork, Diginomica, Glassdoor, Fenwick legal analysis, Alten Capital ecosystem analysis, and general web search (June 2026).

loved.point: Best-in-class process visualization and variant explorer
loved.evidence: Across G2, Gartner, and PeerSpot reviewers consistently praise the ability to 'clearly map and visualize complex business processes' and view event logs and process variants. Described as 'excelling at the process mining part and showing event logs and process variants' (Gartner Peer Insights).

loved.point: Breadth of pre-built SAP connectors and deep ERP integration
loved.evidence: Users with SAP landscapes praise the native extractors for SAP ECC, S/4HANA, Salesforce, and ServiceNow. Seen as unmatched for SAP-heavy enterprise deployments (PeerSpot, SelectHub reviews).

loved.point: Powerful PQL for advanced analysts who master it
loved.evidence: Despite its steep curve, analysts who invest in PQL praise its expressiveness: 150+ operators covering process-specific functions, ML, and math. Referred to as 'very versatile in terms of BI and operational use cases' (Gartner Peer Insights).

loved.point: Action Flows and execution management close the insight-to-action loop
loved.evidence: The EMS concept — detecting deviations and triggering automated remediation — is frequently cited as Celonis's core differentiator versus pure analytics tools. Even critics who find it buggy acknowledge its conceptual value (Gartner Peer Insights, PeerSpot).

loved.point: Strong ROI when enough processes are connected
loved.evidence: Celonis' own study (Diginomica) finds 85% of customers report positive ROI when five or more processes are connected. Forrester TEI report and user testimonials from companies like Smurfit Westrock confirm measurable efficiency gains at scale.

loved.point: Fast innovation cycle / feature velocity
loved.evidence: Recognized as a 'leading-edge process intelligence platform in terms of features and fast innovation cycles' (Gartner Peer Insights). Named a Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader in Process Mining Platforms in 2025 and 2026.

loved.point: Process Copilot natural-language querying
loved.evidence: Generally available as of May 2025, allows NL questions, graph building, and Slack/Teams integration. Described as producing 'enjoyable user experience by asking for data in your own words' (Celonis blog, Gartner).

hated.point: Pricing opacity and extreme cost — especially at enterprise scale
hated.evidence: No public rate card. Enterprise median contract is $286,356/year (SpendHound, 160 customers). One reviewer: 'Celonis has the highest pricing in the process mining domain' (PeerSpot). A consultant noted cost jumps from '$15,000 entry-level to $200,000+ when scaling across business units' (PeerSpot). TrustRadius user: 'monthly fee for Celonis license is extremely expensive — $150/month just to see existing dashboards.' Gartner rates Evaluation & Contracting at 4.1/5, their lowest dimension — reflecting buyer frustration.

hated.point: PQL is a fully proprietary query language with almost no external help available
hated.evidence: 'The PQL is a code that only Celonis uses, so there is little help on the internet or through AI beyond the Celonis documentation' (Gartner Peer Insights, verbatim). 150+ operators require dedicated training. Debug experience is poor: 'Celonis is very bad at recognizing bugs in the code — can't identify simple errors, can't show where an error is, just a character number in a long code' (Gartner Peer Insights, verbatim).

hated.point: Mandatory Center of Excellence / consultant dependency — Celonis cannot be self-served
hated.evidence: The platform explicitly requires a CoE (recommended team of 5–20 FTEs per Celonis' own research, Diginomica). Gartner reviews: 'Initial setup and modelling feel heavy with too much dependency on data engineers.' PeerSpot: 'Requires specialized expertise to set it up in the backend.' 215 global SI partners (Alten Capital) introduce delivery quality variability. Customers quote long 3-year contracts that lock in before internal capability matures.

hated.point: Steep learning curve — advanced features inaccessible without data/engineering background
hated.evidence: Multiple G2, Gartner, PeerSpot, and Capterra reviewers call out the steep learning curve. Celonis Community thread: 'Reaching that classic 2D process map with sliders feels almost like a hidden feature — one needs to create a workspace, then a package, then create assets' (Dennis Arrindell, Celonis Community). Described as 'not suitable for non-technical business users without extensive training.'

hated.point: New features shipped before they are production-ready
hated.evidence: 'A lot of the new features are made available and heavily advertised before they are completely ready' (Gartner Peer Insights, verbatim). 'The ambition of the vendor was always somewhat higher than what the product could provide in reality' (Gartner Peer Insights, verbatim). 'Too many bugs, no consistent front-end development of features' (Gartner Peer Insights). Action Flows: 'high functionality but cumbersome and buggy to use' (Gartner Peer Insights).

hated.point: Very slow and unhelpful customer support
hated.evidence: 'Very bad customer support — tickets take long time for a single reply; sometimes without valid reason they closed our tickets' (Findstack user, verbatim). PeerSpot: 'Lags in response times from customer service' (Senior BI Analyst, Manufacturing). Capterra: 'Unknown error messages that waste time' with no support resolution.

hated.point: Platform stability and reliability issues
hated.evidence: 'Celonis is not entirely stable' (Data Engineer, Pharma/Biotech, PeerSpot). Data jobs 'sometimes unreliable/failing' (Findstack). Maintenance windows 'not always outside of business hours.'

hated.point: Increasing complexity as new layers (OCPM, EMS, Business Miner, AI) pile on top
hated.evidence: Celonis Community post: 'Advanced features like business miner, EMS, object-centric mining, and AI-driven intelligence seem to overshadow the platform's foundational strengths — offering simple, actionable insights.' The poll on 'Is Celonis becoming too complicated?' drew significant community engagement.

missing_or_frustrating.point: End-to-end automation / write-back to source systems is incomplete
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: 'The most important area for improvement is the automation part — workflows are used, but actions should be able to go via email, task, APIs, and ultimately write back to the source; adding RPA capability would greatly enhance Celonis' (PeerSpot). Action Flows integration with RPA systems like UiPath is weak.

missing_or_frustrating.point: On-premises / private-cloud deployment is essentially unavailable
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Celonis is SaaS-only for all practical purposes. Competitors like IBM Process Mining, Paxray, and Mindzie offer on-prem. Users in regulated industries (banking, healthcare, government) cite data residency and cybersecurity policy incompatibility: 'CPM not compatible with country cybersecurity policy' (India-based user, PeerSpot).

missing_or_frustrating.point: Task mining capabilities lag competitors
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Multiple G2 and PeerSpot reviewers note UiPath Process Mining and Microsoft Process Mining have better task mining (UI/desktop event capture) than Celonis.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Microsoft Azure / Microsoft ecosystem integration is poor
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Users running Azure-native stacks report poor integration. 'Poor integration with Microsoft Azure infrastructure' cited as a notable gap (PeerSpot). ERP collaboration with SAP Signavio's BPMN modeling also seen as a gap.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Self-service analytics without PQL or data engineering skill
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Business Miner was shipped to address this but is considered a partial fix. Users want true no-code analysis building — the current 'NL to PQL' Copilot has accuracy issues tied to Knowledge Model quality: 'Unstructured Knowledge Models will impact the accuracy of your Process Copilot' (Celonis docs).

missing_or_frustrating.point: Accessible pricing tier for SMB / mid-market
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Free plan (Celonis Snap) discontinued for new users. Celonis is 'not suitable for SMBs and mid-sized enterprises' per PeerSpot reviewers. 'Only pays for itself for large companies' (Capterra user).

missing_or_frustrating.point: Better documentation and in-product guided learning
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: 'Celonis could provide more detailed documentation so users do not struggle to understand the tool — resources are somewhat limited' (PeerSpot/Capterra). More interactive tutorials or guided walkthroughs specifically requested.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Transparent pricing and clearer licensing path
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: 'Licensing is expensive and the path to the enterprise licensing model is unclear at my level' (TrustRadius, verbatim). 'Constant changes in the licensing structure' and 'confusing licensing' cited in G2/SelectHub aggregated reviews. No public rate card exists.

ux_complaints: Onboarding requires creating a workspace, then a package, then assets before reaching the basic 2D process map — 'feels almost like a hidden feature' (Celonis Community, Dennis Arrindell)
PQL editor provides no line-level error highlighting — errors shown only as a character offset in a long code string (Gartner Peer Insights)
Nested KPIs in the Knowledge Model are hard to navigate and debug
View module filter limit of ~15 filters per view is a hard cap that frustrates analysts building complex analyses
Object-centric process mining (OCPM) migration path from traditional case-centric models is poorly documented and adds significant complexity
Process Copilot requires a clean, well-structured Knowledge Model to give accurate answers — quality degrades sharply on messy real-world data models
Advanced features (AI, OCPM, Business Miner, EMS) overshadow the core discovery UX; newcomers cannot find the basic 2D process map quickly
Maintenance windows often fall within business hours, causing unexpected disruption
Data jobs fail silently without clear error messages
UiPath connector lacks power and functionality compared to native Action Flows
pricing_procurement: No public pricing — all contracts negotiated; enterprise median $286,356/year (SpendHound, 160-customer dataset); SMB median $2,061/year
Contracts typically 3 years with auto-renewal clauses; auto-renewal removal is the single most important negotiation lever (Vendr buyer community)
Entry point quoted at $15,000–$80,000/year for limited deployments, scaling to $200,000+ per business unit (PeerSpot consultant testimony)
Per-user AND per-gigabyte consumption charges both apply at the EMS tier, leading to surprise overage fees at scale
Free plan (Celonis Snap) discontinued for new users; no self-serve freemium path into the product
'Licensing is expensive and the path to the enterprise licensing model is unclear' (TrustRadius user, verbatim)
EY Senior Manager: 'The most expensive solution in the market — customers are migrating to ARIS and SAP Signavio' (PeerSpot)
Finance teams are 'pushing back on Celonis license costs, scrutinizing whether the per-user cost justifies the value across the organization' (SpendHound)

Celonis–McKinsey consulting alliance bundles analytics with transformation playbooks, positioning professional-service arms as profit centers and reinforcing multi-year lock-in (industry analyst commentary)

SAP lawsuit (filed March 2025): SAP charges 'punitively high fees' for third-party data extraction from SAP ERP while offering Signavio at near-zero cost — directly raises effective switching costs for SAP-shop Celonis customers (TechTarget, ProcessExcellenceNetwork)

Glassdoor (employee review, 2023): 'Overpriced complicated products with overhyped value realization story — customers do not need all the bells and whistles to do decent process mining; competitors are catching up at a discount'
switch_drivers: WHY THEY CHOOSE CELONIS: Deepest SAP connector library; unmatched process variant explorer for enterprise event logs; Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader status gives procurement cover; EMS/Action Flows concept closes insight-to-action gap no pure-analytics tool matches; strong partner ecosystem for SAP-centric transformations

WHY THEY STAY: Network effect of internal CoE investment (5–20 FTE trained on PQL); high switching cost after data models and Knowledge Models are built; 3-year contract lock-in; no comparable open-source substitute for enterprise-scale SAP mining

WHY THEY LEAVE OR CONSIDER LEAVING (1): Cost — enterprise contracts averaging $286K/year with escalating per-user and per-GB overages make the CFO relationship adversarial; competitors (UiPath, Microsoft, SAP Signavio) undercut on price
WHY THEY LEAVE OR CONSIDER LEAVING (2): Consultant dependency — organizations that cannot staff a 5–20 person CoE cannot get value; SMBs and mid-market companies are explicitly out of scope
WHY THEY LEAVE OR CONSIDER LEAVING (3): Proprietary PQL lock-in — no AI tooling (ChatGPT, Copilot) trained on PQL; every analyst hire requires Celonis-specific training

WHY THEY LEAVE OR CONSIDER LEAVING (4): SaaS-only deployment — regulated industries (EU GDPR-strict, healthcare, government) cannot send process/ERP data to a US-hosted cloud; no on-prem or private-cloud option

WHY THEY LEAVE OR CONSIDER LEAVING (5): SAP data access war — SAP S/4HANA migration customers face Signavio as the path-of-least-resistance replacement since SAP controls extraction fees for third parties

WHY THEY LEAVE OR CONSIDER LEAVING (6): Feature hype vs reality — 'ambition of the vendor was always somewhat higher than what the product could provide' (Gartner); premature feature releases erode trust in roadmap commitments

ALTERNATIVES CHOSEN: SAP Signavio (SAP-shop consolidation), UiPath Process Mining (task mining + RPA synergy), Microsoft Process Mining (Azure-native, cheaper, M365 bundling), IBM Process Mining (on-prem / hybrid), Mindzie (lower cost, on-prem available), ProcessMind (no-code, faster onboarding), KYP.ai (task/desktop focus)

research.scope: Apromore — open-core process mining platform (academic roots, University of Melbourne spin-off, acquired by Salesforce November 2025). Community/Core vs Enterprise edition dynamics, self-hosting viability, UX, pricing opacity, and positioning vs Celonis.

loved.point: Academic depth — best-in-class simulation and predictive analytics
loved.evidence: Multiple sources cite Apromore's 'exceptional academic roots' as providing 'highly advanced simulation capabilities' not found in comparable tools. Users on review aggregators note the Digital Process Twin and roundtrip simulation are standout features vs mid-market alternatives. (Nerdisa review, processmind.com, mindzie.com 2024)

loved.point: Gartner Leader recognition builds enterprise trust
loved.evidence: Named a Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Process Mining Platforms three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025) and Everest Group PEAK Star Performer 2025 — cited in multiple comparison articles as validation for procurement teams choosing it over less-recognized tools. (processmind.com, Apromore press releases)

loved.point: Application-neutral stance appeals to multi-stack enterprises
loved.evidence: Apromore's migration program press release emphasizes its 'neutral position toward applications and platforms' — explicitly contrasting with SAP Signavio, IBM, and other vendor-tied tools. Mid-market organizations with mixed SAP/Salesforce/ServiceNow stacks choose it specifically for this. (Apromore press release, mindzie.com 2024)

loved.point: Free community/core edition gives researchers and PoC teams a real starting point
loved.evidence: Over 150 organizations worldwide reportedly use the open-source edition (Apromore website). The Core edition includes a working Portal, Process Discoverer, BPMN editor, and event log importer — enough to run a genuine PoC without any payment. (ApromoreCore README, Apromore website)

loved.point: Faster time-to-value vs Celonis for mid-market
loved.evidence: Independent comparison puts Apromore PoC at 3-8 weeks vs Celonis implementations requiring months and significant SI involvement. TCO estimated at $20K-$250K vs Celonis enterprise-grade pricing. Positioning as 'mid-market favorite for analytics and simulation.' (processmind.com 2026)

loved.point: Conformance checking and variant analysis praised by practitioners
loved.evidence: Users on G2 and Gartner reviews note 'well-integrated discovery, conformance checking, and enhancement features that allow quick insights' and report 8% reduction in order management cycle time as a concrete outcome. (G2 review aggregates, Gartner Peer Insights summarized)

loved.point: No-code ETL pipeline for analysts (enterprise edition)
loved.evidence: Enterprise Edition includes a graphical no-code ETL console for defining and scheduling data ingestion pipelines — praised as a differentiator for business analysts who don't want to write SQL or call IT for every new data source. (Apromore EE 8 press release, VentureBeat coverage)

hated.point: Open-source core is now effectively dead — archived August 2025, deprecated after Salesforce acquisition
hated.evidence: ApromoreCore GitHub repository was archived as read-only on August 29, 2025 with explicit README notice: 'The source code available in this repository is now deprecated.' ApromoreDocker was similarly archived September 1, 2025. Both repos have very low star counts (142 stars, 27 stars respectively) indicating shallow community engagement even before archival. Any organization that self-hosted on ApromoreCore is now stranded on abandoned software.

hated.point: Massive feature wall between the free Core and paid Enterprise — the most useful analysis features are all locked
hated.evidence: ApromoreCore README explicitly lists what is enterprise-only: 'Event log filters, Performance dashboards and reports, Conformance checking, Process model comparison, Log animation, Business process simulation, root-cause analysis, ETL pipelines, compliance tools, predictive monitoring, and generative AI features.' In other words, Core gives you a portal and basic process discovery — everything practitioners actually need requires the paid tier.

hated.point: Completely opaque pricing — no public numbers anywhere
hated.evidence: G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, Slashdot, and PeerSpot all show 0 reviews or explicitly note pricing requires contacting sales. Capacity-based model described vaguely with no tier breakpoints. TCO range cited as $20K-$250K+ (processmind.com 2026) — a 10x spread signals zero price predictability. Multiple reviewers note 'opaque pricing for commercial users.' (Nerdisa review, multiple review platform observations)

hated.point: Vendor-lock-in risk just shifted — Salesforce acquisition raises concerns for non-Salesforce shops
hated.evidence: Post-acquisition, Apromore's 'application-neutral' positioning — the core reason enterprises chose it over SAP Signavio and IBM — is now compromised. Salesforce acquired it explicitly to deepen Agentforce integration. Analysts note 'customers may express concerns about vendor lock-in' and 'pricing pressures could emerge.' Organizations on SAP/Oracle/ServiceNow that chose Apromore for neutrality now face the same platform-capture risk they were fleeing. (concret.io blog, ainvest.com, Constellation Research)

hated.point: Learning curve steep for advanced features, especially simulation
hated.evidence: Consistent complaint across Gartner, G2, and aggregated review sources: 'steeper learning curve, particularly for beginners in process mining'; 'advanced simulation features have a steeper learning curve'; 'the interface may seem complex and overwhelming at first.' Directly contradicts vendor marketing claiming 'minimal training requirements.' (Nerdisa review, Gartner summary, G2 aggregates)

hated.point: Data import is painful when working across multiple case notions
hated.evidence: Gartner review aggregate: 'Importing complex data is challenging — not because of Apromore but because the data needs to be analyzed off of multiple case ideas.' Echoes the broader process mining industry problem of flat-event-log assumptions. The multi-table/OCEL support is enterprise-only, leaving community users stuck with single-case-notion CSV files.

hated.point: Export quality inadequate for client-facing deliverables
hated.evidence: Gartner review summary: 'Users would like to have it easier to get clear (not fuzzy) screen prints of the flows and dashboards from Apromore that can be included in client-facing presentations.' A persistent complaint for consulting/advisory users who need to put process maps in PowerPoint.

hated.point: Time zone/timestamp handling frustrates global deployments
hated.evidence: Gartner review summary: 'Users would like to be able to ingest data in UTC and then easily present a specific client's data in their time zone.' Specific enough to suggest it's a real blocker for multi-geography deployments.

hated.point: Very thin independent review base — hard to trust marketing claims
hated.evidence: PeerSpot: 0 reviews collected; Capterra: 0 reviews; Slashdot: 0 reviews. G2 and Gartner have some reviews but are walled behind logins. Most available 'reviews' are vendor-produced or lightly curated aggregation sites. This thinness itself is a trust signal — enterprises can't find peer proof.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Community edition gutted to the point of being unusable for real work — conformance checking, dashboards, filters, and simulation are all enterprise-only
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: ApromoreCore README lists what's missing from free tier: filters, performance dashboards, conformance checking, process model comparison, log animation, simulation, root-cause analysis, ETL pipelines, predictive monitoring, and AI. A practitioner wanting to do anything beyond basic discovery hits a paywall immediately. (ApromoreCore README, multiple review aggregators)

missing_or_frustrating.point: No public self-hosting path post-acquisition — the Docker repo is archived with no successor announced
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: ApromoreDocker archived September 1, 2025 with no replacement or migration guide. Organizations wanting to self-host an actively maintained Apromore are left with no supported path. The enterprise edition's on-premise deployment requires direct sales engagement. (GitHub ApromoreDocker archived repo)

missing_or_frustrating.point: Pre-built templates for common industry processes missing from community tier
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Review aggregates note users 'desire pre-built analysis templates for common use cases.' The enterprise edition has vertical recipes for banking/insurance/healthcare but community users must build everything from scratch — a significant time investment that erodes the 'free' value proposition. (TrustRadius summary, review aggregates)

missing_or_frustrating.point: No deep partner/consultant ecosystem for mid-market
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Explicitly called out as a weakness: 'lacks the broader ecosystem that larger vendors offer' and 'a deep bench of enterprise consultants.' Mid-market orgs that need implementation help face a thin SI market vs Celonis which has a dense certified partner network. (mindzie.com 2024, processmind.com 2026)

missing_or_frustrating.point: ERP connector setup requires technical skills or enterprise tier — community users left to manual CSV import
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: G2 review aggregate: 'direct integration with ERP systems or data preparation tools require more technical skills or the enterprise version.' For organizations running SAP ECC or S4/HANA, the advanced SAP connector is enterprise-only. (G2 aggregates, multiple comparison sources)

missing_or_frustrating.point: Roadmap uncertainty and open source future now unclear post-Salesforce acquisition
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Apromore's own migration program press release (issued *before* the Salesforce acquisition) warned customers away from 'vendors that have been acquired' citing 'negative impacts on service delivery, release life cycle, changing or delayed roadmap.' Apromore has now become the very thing it warned against. Community members have no visibility into whether any open source successor to ApromoreCore will exist. (Apromore migration press release, acquisition news)

ux_complaints: Steep learning curve for new users especially for simulation and predictive features — contradicts vendor's 'minimal training' marketing claims (Gartner review aggregates, G2 summaries)
Fuzzy/blurry export quality for process flow screenshots — inadequate for client presentations and board-level reporting (Gartner review aggregates)
Filter and dashboard UI requires more clicks than users expect — 'overly cumbersome steps required to apply filters' and 'dashboards section could be more visible' (Gartner and G2 review aggregates)
Interface described as 'less polished than some competitors' — users comparing it unfavorably against Celonis and Signavio on visual quality (multiple review aggregators)
Complex data analysis across multiple case notions is confusing at the UX level — the multi-table concept is not surfaced intuitively (Gartner review aggregates)
Time zone presentation workflow is clunky for global teams — data ingested in UTC cannot be easily re-displayed in client local time (Gartner review aggregates)
Java-based self-hosted installation requires JDK 11 specifically — newer Java versions cause dependency issues, pinning users to aging runtime (ApromoreCore README)
Documentation described as insufficient — users want 'more extensive video tutorials and documentation' for advanced features (review aggregates)
pricing_procurement: Enterprise pricing is entirely opaque — 'contact sales' for all commercial tiers, no public pricing on any review site (G2, TrustRadius, Capterra, Slashdot all show no pricing)
Capacity-based model with no published breakpoints — TCO range cited as $20K-$250K+ creates a 10x uncertainty spread making budget approval difficult (processmind.com)

The 'free' community/core tier is a feature-stripped bait — the features most orgs need (conformance checking, dashboards, simulation, ETL, filters) are all behind the enterprise paywall (ApromoreCore README)

Post-Salesforce acquisition, pricing trajectory is unknown and likely upward — Salesforce is moving Apromore 'upmarket', pricing pressure from Celonis-level enterprise deals expected (processmind.com, ainvest.com)
SI/consultant scarcity inflates effective TCO — thin partner ecosystem means internal teams absorb more implementation burden vs Celonis where certified partners are abundant (mindzie.com 2024)

Migration lock-in risk: rebuilding 'dashboards, connectors, filters and other assets when switching' is cited as a major switching cost in Apromore's own migration program press release — now a risk for Apromore customers themselves
switch_drivers: Organizations switch TO Apromore from Celonis primarily on cost — Celonis is 'enterprise-grade at an enterprise-grade price'; Apromore's mid-market TCO ($20K-$250K) is substantially lower (processmind.com 2026, mindzie.com 2024)

Organizations switch TO Apromore from vendor-tied tools (SAP Signavio, IBM) for application neutrality — ability to analyze SAP, ServiceNow, Oracle, and Salesforce in a single platform without bias (Apromore migration press release, Constellation Research)

Academic and research teams choose Apromore Core as a free Celonis alternative for coursework and research — the open-source pedigree from University of Melbourne and 15+ contributing institutions gives it credibility in academic settings (IEEE Task Force newsletter, University of Melbourne case study)

Organizations are NOW switching AWAY from Apromore post-Salesforce acquisition due to the same vendor-capture concerns Apromore previously used as a sales argument — neutrality promise is broken for non-Salesforce shops (Apromore's own migration program press release, acquisition coverage)

The archival of ApromoreCore/ApromoreDocker in late 2025 is a forced exit trigger for self-hosted community users — no maintained open source path exists, forcing migration to enterprise or a different tool entirely

Organizations that need deep Gartner/Everest credibility for procurement approvals stay with Apromore — three consecutive Magic Quadrant Leader placements outweigh platform concerns for risk-averse buyers (multiple Gartner references in review summaries)

research.scope: Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining (incl. Process Advisor / Minit acquisition) AND SAP Signavio Process Intelligence (incl. Process Insights). Both are suite-bundled offerings from hyperscalers/ERP vendors competing in the process mining / process intelligence market against each other, Celonis, Apromore, and open-source tools like FlowMiner.

loved.point: Microsoft: ecosystem gravity — zero-friction adoption for M365/Azure shops
loved.evidence: Multiple Gartner and PeerSpot reviewers say integration with Teams, Excel, Power BI, and Dataverse makes adoption smooth for orgs already on Microsoft stack. One reviewer: 'the benefits of a Power Platform ecosystem that aligns with our future plans' (Gartner Peer Insights).

loved.point: Microsoft: task mining / desktop recording is a differentiated bundled capability
loved.evidence: Process Advisor task mining lets users record desktop workflows without a separate tool. Reviewers on Gartner note this is a key convenience for organizations already in Power Automate.

loved.point: Microsoft: Copilot/AI integration is ahead of most competitors for natural-language process queries
loved.evidence: Microsoft's 2024 Gartner MQ recognition cited 'advanced analytics, task mining, and generative AI' as strengths. Copilot in Process Mining allows conversational analytics against a process map (Microsoft Power Platform Blog, 2024).

loved.point: Microsoft: named a Leader in the 2024 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Process Mining Platforms (jumped from Challenger)
loved.evidence: Microsoft Power Platform Blog, May 2024 — notable leap in analyst positioning driven by Minit acquisition and Copilot integration.

loved.point: SAP Signavio: native S/4HANA data pipeline is genuinely frictionless for SAP shops
loved.evidence: PeerSpot reviewers consistently praise zero-ETL integration with SAP modules. RFC connector and SAP Datasphere replication flows give SAP customers out-of-the-box process visibility without data engineering. Peerspot user: 'Integration with SAP modules aids in supply chain management and process optimization.'

loved.point: SAP Signavio Process Insights: fastest time-to-value for SAP best-practice benchmarking
loved.evidence: Process Insights ships with out-of-the-box KPIs and benchmarks for P2P, O2C, R2R — organizations can establish a baseline 'within weeks' without data science. (Westernacher consulting writeup, SAP Community)

loved.point: SAP Signavio: named a Leader in Gartner MQ for Process Mining Platforms three consecutive years
loved.evidence: SAP News press release, May 2024. Gartner cited 'market positioning, alignment with SAP's go-to-market, and AI functionalities including text-to-query-to-widget, automatic event log enhancement, dashboard AI assistant.'

hated.point: Microsoft: $5,000/tenant/month add-on pricing is a shock for teams that expected process mining to be 'included'
hated.evidence: Process Mining add-on requires Power Automate Premium AND a $5,000/tenant/month add-on. Gartner reviewer (Dec 2025): 'Powerful insights and workflows based on real data but very expensive to use.' G2 review: 'Very expensive and difficult to understand for new bees.' (Microsoft Power Platform pricing page, G2, Gartner Peer Insights)

hated.point: Microsoft: shallow depth vs. dedicated tools — positioned only for 'process discovery', not continuous monitoring or deep conformance
hated.evidence: Taloflow competitive analysis: 'Microsoft Power Automate process mining is best suited for the process discovery use case.' Gartner reviews note it is 'missing a lot of key features other similar products/systems, such as Nintex, provide' (June 2025). Celonis rated higher on real-time process analysis (8.7 vs 8.6) and data management (PeerSpot comparison).

hated.point: Microsoft: non-Microsoft data ingestion is painful — outside the M365/Azure stack connectivity degrades sharply
hated.evidence: PeerSpot Celonis vs Power Automate comparison: 'When trying to connect or integrate with external platforms outside the MS environment, it's more challenging to do data ingestion and set up.' OneDrive for Business required for CSV connector. FetchXML/OData required for Dataverse audit tables. Dataflow connector not supported.

hated.point: Microsoft: Copilot in Process Mining has material limitations that are often undisclosed before purchase
hated.evidence: Microsoft's own FAQ (2024): Copilot 'only has access to the most common activities and variants'; 'doesn't have access to statistical information about custom attributes'; 'isn't equipped with transforming or preparing any ETL work'; only works with Azure Data Lake source. These constraints surface post-purchase.

hated.point: Microsoft: tool maturity lag — core process mining features trail Celonis and UiPath in analytic depth
hated.evidence: PeerSpot user: 'can become very laggy at times.' Gartner reviews note 'not fully mature yet.' Coding still required for advanced use: PeerSpot reviewer: 'Having experience with coding is essential to fully utilize Power Automate.' Support quality varies dramatically by region (rated 3/10 in India vs 8-9 elsewhere).

hated.point: SAP Signavio: price exploded after SAP acquisition — SMEs priced out entirely
hated.evidence: PeerSpot reviewer: 'After SAP acquired Signavio, the prices increased significantly, making it too expensive for our small company.' Enterprise licensing reported at $800K/year at the high end. Process Intelligence capacity tiers run $60K–$600K/year on top of per-user licensing. Pricin described as 'extortionate' by some PeerSpot users.

hated.point: SAP Signavio: non-SAP data is a second-class citizen — integration complexity and licensing penalties
hated.evidence: PeerSpot: 'License structure becomes inefficient when connecting to non-SAP data sources.' Non-SAP public cloud connections require SAP Integration Suite as an intermediary layer. Data capacity 'depletes quickly with non-SAP sources.' Celonis antitrust lawsuit alleges SAP made it 'de facto impossible for customers to work with non-SAP process mining solutions' (Celonis v. SAP, 2025).

hated.point: SAP Signavio: interface not intuitive — users consistently prefer Celonis UI
hated.evidence: PeerSpot: 'The solution is a good one but could be improved by making the interface more user friendly.' PeerSpot user who switched from Celonis: 'from the Process Mining perspective, Celonis is better' — specifically citing superior UI and training documentation. Workfellow G2 summary: customers 'would prefer a simplified and more intuitive user experience.'

hated.point: SAP Signavio: licensing model is opaque and multi-dimensional — unpredictable TCO
hated.evidence: PricingNow analysis: separate meters for named users, 200K-record blocks (Process Intelligence), Collaboration Hub user blocks, and AI Units. Annual price increases on module additions. PeerSpot: frustration with 'separate charges for Process Manager versus Process Mining modules.' Redress Compliance: pricing is negotiable by 25-40% — but only if you know to negotiate.

hated.point: SAP Signavio: Process Insights hardcodes SAP best-practice assumptions — useless for evolved/non-standard processes
hated.evidence: Gartner Peer Insights (multiple reviews, 2024-2025): 'the tool's central design decisions assume the process landscape is somewhat aligned to SAP's best practice processes, and for processes that have evolved over decades and are therefore no longer aligned with best practice, most of the assumptions and insights are invalid.'

hated.point: SAP Signavio: slow feature development pace post-acquisition
hated.evidence: Workfellow G2 summary: 'Signavio has not introduced improvements and new features' — multiple reviewers cite slower development versus pre-acquisition pace. Product Strategy and Rate of Improvement is among the lowest-scoring dimensions (80/100) on SoftwareReviews.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Microsoft: no support for Object-Centric Process Mining (OCPM) — officially listed as not supported as of 2024 (preview in 2025 Wave 2 only)
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: KYP.ai comparison: 'Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining does not support OCPM.' OCPM was only added as a preview feature in 2025 Wave 2 (azurecurve.co.uk, Nov 2025), years behind academic adoption.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Microsoft: ETL/data prep is entirely on the user — no built-in transformation, no connectors for ERP event tables
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Microsoft Learn documentation: 'No data transformation is available post ingestion.' Users must pre-prepare event logs externally. Copilot FAQ explicitly states it 'isn't equipped with transforming or preparing any ETL work.' Heavy data engineering burden before any insight.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Microsoft: process mining is locked to cloud/Dataverse — on-premise or sovereign-cloud deployments are unsupported
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Power Automate Process Mining is a cloud-only SaaS add-on. Organizations with on-premise data or strict data residency requirements cannot self-host or air-gap the product, making it non-starter for regulated industries in non-US jurisdictions.

missing_or_frustrating.point: SAP Signavio: no native task mining — must rely on third-party or SAP's separate Work Zone tool
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Taloflow comparison: SAP Signavio has 'limited native task mining.' This means desktop-level activity capture requires additional tools not bundled with Process Intelligence.

missing_or_frustrating.point: SAP Signavio: two overlapping products (Process Insights vs Process Intelligence) confuse buyers — unclear when to buy which
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: SAP Community blog explicitly acknowledged: 'SAP's biggest challenge was changing the perception that both products were just the result of the clash between Signavio acquisition and SAP's own developed BTP solution.' Users worried one product would be discontinued. Westernacher consulting published a disambiguation guide precisely because buyers routinely pick the wrong product.

missing_or_frustrating.point: SAP Signavio: no low-code customization or extensible app-building — custom analysis requires heavy configuration or SAP consulting
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Interfacing.com replacement guide: Signavio 'does not inherently offer low-code development features, potentially limiting customization options.' Building new dashboards 'requires maturity in the tool.' Organizations cannot self-serve beyond pre-built templates without consultants.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Both tools: no self-hosted / open-source path — data sovereignty and cost control are impossible
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Neither Microsoft nor SAP offers a self-hosted deployment. Both require data to leave the enterprise boundary into their respective clouds. Organizations with GDPR/sovereign cloud requirements or cost-conscious SMEs have no viable tier. Apromore is called out as the only notable open-source alternative (search results, Workfellow article).

ux_complaints: Microsoft: data ingestion requires OneDrive for Business for CSV import — missing that entitlement blocks the simplest onboarding path (Microsoft Learn documentation)
Microsoft: header row size capped at 1 MB and Dataflow connector unsupported — hidden technical limits discovered during setup, not before purchase (Microsoft Learn documentation)

Microsoft: Copilot answers are limited to the most frequent activities/variants only — for complex real-world processes the AI assistant is essentially silent on the long tail (Microsoft Copilot in Process Mining FAQ)
Microsoft: steep learning curve for advanced analytics despite 'low-code' branding — PeerSpot reviewers note coding is still 'essential' to unlock full capabilities

SAP Signavio: overwhelming initial UI — Gartner reviewers describe it as 'not very intuitive' and 'very complicated to use'; primary reviewer title on SoftwareReviews: 'Powerful Insights But Setup-Heavy'
SAP Signavio: per-user licensing creates bottlenecks — one manager's named-user license blocks access for collaborators, forcing expensive license expansion (PeerSpot pricing Q&A thread)
SAP Signavio: slow support response times due to shared SAP support portal across the entire product family (PeerSpot multiple reviews)
SAP Signavio: building custom dashboards requires deep tool expertise — not self-service; 'requires maturity in the tool to build new insights' (Gartner Peer Insights 2024-2025 reviews)
SAP Signavio: limited drill-down in company benchmarking and year-to-date aggregations missing — specific analytical gaps mentioned in Gartner reviews 2024-2025
pricing_procurement: Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining add-on: $5,000 USD/tenant/month — requires Power Automate Premium as a prerequisite. Gartner Dec 2025 reviewer: 'very expensive to use.' G2: 'Very expensive and difficult to understand for new bees.' (Microsoft pricing page, G2, Gartner Peer Insights)

Microsoft: 100 MB process mining capacity included per Premium license — reaches 100 GB tenant cap quickly on real-world logs; add-on needed to go beyond. Hidden capacity ceiling surprises enterprise teams at scale.

SAP Signavio Process Intelligence: capacity-based licensing at $60K–$600K USD/year depending on tier (50M, 250M, 1B, 5B event records/year) — on top of per-user Premium licensing at ~$3,360/user list price. A 1,200-user deployment lists at ~$4M/year (Redress Compliance analysis).

SAP Signavio: post-acquisition price increases — PeerSpot reviewer: 'After SAP acquired Signavio, the prices increased significantly, making it too expensive for our small company.' Described as 'extortionate' and suited only for 'huge enterprises.'
SAP Signavio: AI Units introduced as a separate variable consumption meter for AI features — makes budget forecasting impossible (PricingNow TCO analysis).
SAP Signavio: pricing is opaque — no public list prices; requires custom quote; but is negotiable 25-40% if buyer knows to push back (Redress Compliance negotiation guide).

SAP Signavio: data extraction fees for non-SAP tools — Celonis antitrust lawsuit (2025) alleges SAP threatens customers with 'punitively high fees' for data extraction if they use non-Signavio process mining vendors, effectively forcing customers to pay a toll or switch to Signavio (Celonis v. SAP complaint, CIO.com, TechTarget 2025).
SAP Signavio: implementation cost $400K+ at the high end; deployment timelines 6-12+ months — heavy consultant dependency for any non-standard or non-SAP process (ProcessMind blog).
switch_drivers: Organizations choose Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining primarily because they are already deep in the M365/Azure ecosystem and want a single-vendor story — not because it is the best process mining tool. Analyst consensus: 'best suited for process discovery use case.'

Organizations choose SAP Signavio primarily because their IT leadership mandates an 'SAP suite' consolidation strategy during S/4HANA migration — not necessarily because it outperforms competitors on mining depth.

Users who evaluated both often prefer Celonis for pure process mining depth: PeerSpot reviewer who switched from Celonis to Signavio acknowledged 'from the Process Mining perspective, Celonis is better' — organizational politics drove the switch, not product quality.

Users leave Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining when: (a) they need cross-system (non-Microsoft) process mining; (b) they need conformance checking or continuous monitoring beyond discovery; (c) the $5K/month add-on cost exceeds willingness to pay versus a dedicated tool.

Users leave SAP Signavio when: (a) prices became unsustainable post-acquisition; (b) non-SAP systems dominate their landscape; (c) they need faster feature velocity; (d) they want lower-cost or open-source self-hosted alternatives.

The Celonis vs. SAP antitrust case (filed 2025, court denied dismissal Oct 2025) is actively shaping SAP customer decisions — customers aware of the case are scrutinizing Signavio's 'coercive' data extraction fees and evaluating alternatives. SAP agreed to an interim data access preservation order in June 2025.

Open-source tools (Apromore, and now self-hostable platforms like FlowMiner) are cited as alternatives for organizations with budget constraints or data sovereignty requirements — a segment both Microsoft and SAP explicitly abandon.

research.scope: UiPath Process Mining, IBM Process Mining (formerly myInvenio), and Software AG ARIS Process Mining — strengths, complaints, RPA-vs-mining positioning, dashboard/app-template UX, and learning curve. Synthesized from PeerSpot, TrustRadius, Capterra, Gartner Peer Insights, G2, analyst commentary, and comparison blog coverage (2023–2026).

loved.point: UiPath: single-platform RPA + mining loop
loved.evidence: Users in RPA-heavy enterprises praise the native link between process discovery and bot deployment — 'discover inefficiencies, then deploy robots to fix them without leaving the UiPath ecosystem.' Strong praise on PeerSpot and comparison blogs.

loved.point: UiPath: active community and support
loved.evidence: Reviewers on PeerSpot cite the 24/7 community forum (community.uipath.com) and responsive support as standout strengths. 'Their support is quite good.' Support rated 8.1/10 on PeerSpot.

loved.point: UiPath: database-backed process insights
loved.evidence: 'Those database-backed insights are very valuable for business partners' — PeerSpot reviewer. Root cause analysis, bottleneck visualization, and real-time dashboards praised across multiple reviews.

loved.point: IBM Process Mining: strong out-of-box process discovery and BPMN alignment
loved.evidence: Capterra and TrustRadius reviewers highlight clear process visualization and alignment with standard BPMN models. 'The platform provides strong process discovery and visualization, making it easier to identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies.' Good fit for IBM BPM/BAW shops.

loved.point: IBM Process Mining: professional support and 24/7 responsiveness
loved.evidence: Multiple Capterra reviewers note a 'professional support team that is user-friendly and proactive 24/7.' Praised as accessible even for less technical teams.

loved.point: ARIS: seamless BPM-to-mining closed loop
loved.evidence: The standout differentiator praised across PeerSpot reviews: direct comparison of live as-is process data against governed to-be models stored in the ARIS BPM repository. No other tool offers this out of the box. Users call it the defining reason to choose ARIS over Celonis for BPM-centric organizations.

loved.point: ARIS: comprehensive feature set and cross-department collaboration
loved.evidence: 'Clients say that Software AG ARIS Process Mining has everything.' Cross-department collaboration without email file transfers praised. PeerSpot comparison vs UiPath, 2025.

loved.point: ARIS: conformance checking accuracy
loved.evidence: Gartner and PeerSpot reviews cite conformance checking against modeled processes as best-in-class. Users specifically chose ARIS when regulatory conformance reporting mattered.

hated.point: UiPath: steep SQL/coding requirement for data transformations
hated.evidence: UiPath documentation itself states 'it is strongly recommended that you have in-depth knowledge of SQL' to write data transformations. PeerSpot users report ~30% of project lifecycle time consumed by data preparation. 'It's not very easy to turn raw data into actionable information.' Multiple independent complaints on PeerSpot Q&A.

hated.point: UiPath: very thin connector library (~10–12 connectors)
hated.evidence: Multiple PeerSpot reviewers flag that UiPath offers only ~10–12 source connectors versus Celonis's 100+. 'UiPath Process Mining has not been adding new API connectors as frequently in recent years.' Missing BPMN import support also noted. PeerSpot Q&A thread on improvement needs.

hated.point: UiPath: congested process maps and weaker visualization vs Celonis
hated.evidence: 'UiPath's process maps are congested. Celonis provides better visibility in this regard.' — PeerSpot reviewer. Multiple sources note Celonis's auto-generated, highly interactive models feel superior for large datasets.

hated.point: UiPath: no drag-and-drop dashboard; requires coding for customization
hated.evidence: 'UiPath Process Mining is not as user-friendly as Celonis. While Celonis offers a drag-and-drop functionality for building dashboards, UiPath requires some coding expertise.' — PeerSpot/comparison coverage.

hated.point: UiPath: large dataset performance crashes
hated.evidence: 'Not able to handle a lot of logs in one go at high speed.' Data sharding workaround described as complicating rather than solving analysis. Large dataset handling causes occasional crashes. PeerSpot reviews and Capterra.

hated.point: IBM Process Mining: pricing too high for SMBs / smaller teams
hated.evidence: 'Minimum pricing of the license is not what small companies expected and it's too high.' 'A bit sophisticated and expensive, making it difficult to implement in smaller businesses.' — Capterra reviewers.

hated.point: IBM Process Mining: weak onboarding documentation and training
hated.evidence: 'Guidance for the onboarding period and the quality of training on their documentation needs improvement.' 'Onboarding may be enhanced because it presently lacks information.' 'Not covering all the features and capabilities.' — Multiple Capterra reviewers.

hated.point: IBM Process Mining: Chrome extension crashes and performance degradation on large data
hated.evidence: 'Chrome extensions aren't working probably' and 'performance goes heavier and crashes sometimes' with large datasets. 'Documentation doesn't have any how-to optimize.' — Capterra.

hated.point: IBM Process Mining: prior technical expertise required; not accessible to business users
hated.evidence: 'Requires prior technical expertise to understand how to use it.' 'Solution is sophisticated and difficult to grasp everything.' — Capterra reviews. Extraction and cleaning of event logs described as 'time consuming and requires significant coordination with IT and business teams.'

hated.point: ARIS: cloud version is too slow via Citrix / remote access
hated.evidence: 'When I connect to the client server...it becomes too slow. The cloud version becomes quite slow when connecting through tools such as Citrix, which is not the case with IBM.' — PeerSpot reviewer, multiple corroborating reports.

hated.point: ARIS: maintenance windows cause multi-day downtime
hated.evidence: 'Installation takes too long, and if it goes under maintenance, it remains under maintenance for days.' — PeerSpot reviewer. Operational reliability concern for production use.

hated.point: ARIS: split modeling/mining environments — no unified workspace
hated.evidence: 'There should be a single site for modeling and mining.' Users must toggle between separate platforms for design (ARIS Architect/Designer) and analysis (ARIS Process Mining), and transferring models back for optimization requires manual steps. PeerSpot Q&A.

hated.point: ARIS: KPI and dashboard customization is unintuitive vs peers
hated.evidence: 'Customizing KPIs and building dashboards were not as intuitive as other similar tools.' — PeerSpot and Taloflow comparison coverage. Described across multiple sources as a consistent gap.

hated.point: ARIS: ownership uncertainty after 2025 Software AG divestiture
hated.evidence: ARIS was divested from Software AG in 2025 and now operates as a standalone entity. Analyst commentary and competitor marketing confirm 'the evolving ownership structure of ARIS has led to some customers seeking more long-term solutions for process intelligence.' Long-term vendor stability concern.

missing_or_frustrating.point: UiPath: no AI-powered process optimization suggestions
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: PeerSpot Q&A thread on improvement needs cites absence of AI suggestions for what to automate next. 'Lacks AI-powered insights competitors provide. Manual delay tracking insufficient.' Users compare unfavorably to Celonis's ML-driven simulation and Execution Management features.

missing_or_frustrating.point: UiPath: no simulation or forecasting capabilities
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Missing simulation and forecasting capabilities flagged by multiple PeerSpot reviewers. Celonis and ARIS offer what-if simulation; UiPath does not have a comparable feature natively.

missing_or_frustrating.point: UiPath: no desktop/standalone option (cloud-only SaaS)
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Users note that the cloud-only constraint (post-ProcessGold integration) locks them out of on-premise or air-gapped deployments. Celonis also cloud-only but UiPath's RPA customers often run on-premise bots, creating a split-deployment friction.

missing_or_frustrating.point: UiPath: connector library stagnated — BPMN import and manufacturing connectors missing
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: 'Missing support for BPMN file format and certain production/manufacturing connectors.' — PeerSpot. Users in manufacturing or using non-SAP/Oracle ERPs often cannot connect without custom SQL ETL work.

missing_or_frustrating.point: IBM Process Mining: lack of mobile app
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: 'Lack of a functional mobile app compared to competitors.' — Capterra reviewer. Business users who want to monitor KPIs on mobile have no native option.

missing_or_frustrating.point: IBM Process Mining: no clear upgrade path for non-IBM-stack organizations
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: IBM Process Mining sits inside Cloud Pak for Business Automation / watsonx Orchestrate. Organizations not already on IBM middleware find it hard to justify without adopting more IBM infrastructure. Analyst commentary from Redress Compliance notes IBM licensing math consistently overstates needed VPC capacity, creating cost surprises.

missing_or_frustrating.point: ARIS: AI/ML automation capabilities lag competitors
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: 'Incorporating artificial intelligence and machine learning can improve competitiveness.' Multiple PeerSpot reviewers flag that ARIS AI Companion (launched April 2024) is a step in the right direction but still lags Celonis and IBM watsonx for prescriptive recommendations.

missing_or_frustrating.point: All three: event log extraction from legacy/non-ERP systems remains painful
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: Across all three tools, users report that extracting event logs from custom legacy applications or non-standard systems requires heavy SQL/Python/ETL work with no pre-built connector. This ~30%-of-project-time data prep tax is the most repeated frustration across PeerSpot, Capterra, and UiPath community blog.

UiPath: no drag-and-drop dashboard builder; requires SQL and coding expertise to customize views (PeerSpot, multiple sources)
UiPath: process maps are visually congested on larger processes; Celonis described as significantly cleaner (PeerSpot reviewer quote)
UiPath: filter creation is limited — 'more ways of creating filters' and 'easier customized dashboards' repeatedly requested (PeerSpot)

IBM Process Mining: limited customization options out of box (Gartner/Capterra reviewers)
ARIS: separate design and mining environments with no unified workspace create constant context-switching friction (PeerSpot Q&A)
ARIS: KPI and dashboard customization 'not as intuitive as other similar tools' — business users cannot self-serve insights (PeerSpot)
ARIS: mandatory training to use the tool; not plug-and-play for casual or business users (Taloflow, PeerSpot)

pricing_procurement: UiPath Process Mining: enterprise license ranges $40,000–$200,000/year plus maintenance — described as 'priced high compared to other solutions' and 'quite expensive, not competitive right now' (PeerSpot). Better than Celonis but significantly more expensive than Microsoft Power Automate.
UiPath: no transparent public pricing; sales-led quoting process. Buyers report pricing opacity as a frustration (PeerSpot Q&A).

IBM Process Mining: 'minimum pricing of the license is not what small companies expected and it's too high' (Capterra). License described as 'a bit sophisticated and expensive, making it difficult to implement in smaller businesses.'

IBM Process Mining: bundled into Cloud Pak for Business Automation / watsonx Orchestrate — organizations that don't need the broader platform must still pay for it (analyst commentary). IBM VPC licensing math consistently runs 20–40% over actual workload needs according to Redress Compliance advisory data (2024–2025).
IBM: one of the most aggressive software audit postures of any major publisher — audit risk adds hidden total-cost-of-ownership concern for large IBM software estates (Redress Compliance).

ARIS: license-based model described as 'highly-priced' though users accept it as fair relative to feature depth (PeerSpot). Tiered, role-based pricing model described as 'opaque and complex' for buyers.

ARIS: Software AG offers consulting-led 'Fast Track' onboarding services (25-day engagement) — pricing not publicly disclosed and requires sales engagement. Implementation without consulting support is possible but reported as difficult, creating de facto consultant dependency.
ARIS: ownership change (Software AG divestiture 2025) creates contract and support continuity uncertainty for existing customers on multi-year agreements.
switch_drivers: Organizations switch TO UiPath from standalone process mining tools when they are already committed to UiPath RPA and want a single-vendor automation lifecycle without integrating a separate point solution.

Organizations switch AWAY FROM UiPath when they need deep ERP analytics (Celonis's 100+ connectors vs UiPath's ~10–12), want drag-and-drop dashboards, or have large heterogeneous IT landscapes requiring extensive data integration beyond UiPath's thin layer.

UiPath ecosystem lock-in is a known concern: 'organizations tied to UiPath may face high switching costs and limited flexibility' — value proposition weakens for organizations not already using UiPath RPA.
Organizations switch TO IBM Process Mining when they are already inside the IBM Cloud Pak / watsonx ecosystem and need process mining integrated with IBM BAW or IBM RPA without adding a new vendor.
Organizations switch AWAY FROM IBM when they find the licensing too expensive for team size, documentation too thin for self-service adoption, or integration with non-IBM systems too burdensome.
IBM's acquisition of myInvenio (2021) means the product's Italian-origin team has been absorbed into IBM bureaucracy — practitioner commentary notes this slows feature velocity compared to Celonis.

Organizations choose ARIS when BPM-first culture requires direct conformance checking against governed process models — the as-is vs to-be loop is ARIS's unique moat that Celonis and UiPath cannot replicate without external BPM tooling.
Organizations are evaluating alternatives to ARIS following the 2025 Software AG divestiture due to vendor stability concerns — competitors actively marketing against this uncertainty.
The 2025 ARIS divestiture from Software AG means ARIS is now an independent company; long-term support, development roadmap, and financial stability are open questions for prospects.

All three tools lose to open-source / self-hostable options (Apromore, ProM, FlowMiner-class tools) when the driver is cost transparency, data sovereignty, or avoiding per-seat/per-event pricing on large logs.

research.scope: Fluxicon Disco, QPR ProcessAnalyzer, Minit (now Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining), Mehrwerk mpmX/MPM, Workfellow/ProcessMaster (now ProcessMaker PI), Skan.ai — with a specific lens on why simple tools like Disco retain a loyal following vs. enterprise suites

loved.point: Disco: Near-zero time-to-value — no implementation project, no IT dependency
loved.evidence: Multiple Gartner Peer Insights reviewers (2022–2024) note that Disco requires no setup: 'no implementation is required and you can start getting value virtually immediately after downloading.' A 2023 IT/BPM consultant called it 'lightweight yet powerful.' Consistently cited as the reason academic courses and quick consulting engagements default to it. (Gartner Peer Insights, processmining-software.com)

loved.point: Disco: Best-in-class UX for process discovery — 'bells and whistles' deliberately absent
loved.evidence: Gartner reviewers repeatedly use phrases like 'user-friendly tool that makes it possible to quickly start with process mining,' 'works very intuitively,' and 'a pleasant look and feel, without unnecessary bells and whistles.' The absence of enterprise bloat is named as a feature, not a gap. (Gartner Peer Insights 2022–2024)

loved.point: Disco: Beloved by academics and consultants as the 'OG' commercial process mining tool
loved.evidence: 'I've known of the DISCO product and its academic progenitor (ProM) for about a decade... I consider DISCO to be as close to the OG of Process Mining as one can get in the commercial space.' Fluxicon co-founders are Wil van der Aalst PhDs; academic pedigree is a genuine trust signal. Free academic licenses at ~700 universities reinforce the flywheel. (Gartner Peer Insights; Fluxicon academic initiative page)

loved.point: Disco: Privacy-by-default via local desktop execution — no data ever leaves the org
loved.evidence: Gartner reviewers and comparison sites flag local processing as a key trust-building feature: 'data privacy ensured as local analysis ensures confidential data remains within the organization.' Particularly valued in regulated industries and European enterprises. (processmining-software.com, Gartner 2024)

loved.point: Disco: Outstanding vendor support and community — Fluxicon team is personally responsive
loved.evidence: 'The team at Fluxicon is outstanding with passion for process mining evident in their product.' Process Mining Camp is described as 'the only conference exclusively focused on practical application of process mining.' Small founder-led team culture comes through in support quality. (Gartner Peer Insights; Fluxicon website)

loved.point: QPR ProcessAnalyzer: Strong discovery plus KPI/dashboard layer — good price-quality ratio
loved.evidence: PeerSpot users give QPR an 8.6/10 average. Users cite 'excellent discovery and root cause analysis functionality' and 'competitive features relative to similar solutions.' A PeerSpot reviewer noted 'there is no better tool out there' when comparing price versus quality. (PeerSpot reviews; Gartner Peer Insights)

loved.point: Mehrwerk MPM/mpmX: Massive Qlik connector library (100+) makes it easy for existing Qlik shops to adopt
loved.evidence: Gartner reviewers highlight that 'initial installation and light training took no more than one hour' for Qlik Sense customers. 'Extremely flexible tool that integrates about any data source.' Customers like REWE Group, E.ON, Siemens Healthineers cited. (Gartner Peer Insights; processmining-software.com)

loved.point: Workfellow/ProcessMaker PI: Non-intrusive task+process mining combo with fast time-to-insight
loved.evidence: Gartner reviewers note 'non-intrusive data collection without requiring deep system integration' and 'excellent customer support.' Marketing claim of '10x faster speed to insights, 30-day implementation' aligns with reviewer sentiment about fast setup. (Gartner Peer Insights; Workfellow/ProcessMaker blog)

loved.point: Skan.ai: Zero-integration process intelligence — the only MQ vendor not requiring backend system connectors
loved.evidence: Gartner 2024 MQ noted Skan as 'the only vendor in the entire Magic Quadrant that does not require backend system integration to extract process mining insights at enterprise scale.' G2 reviewers call it 'easy-to-use interface' with 'great customer support.' Works across mainframe, VDI, Excel, chat. (Gartner 2024 MQ; G2 reviews; Skan.ai press release)

loved.point: Minit/Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining: Deep Microsoft ecosystem integration — Power BI dashboarding is a genuine differentiator
loved.evidence: Taloflow comparison rates Microsoft Power Automate 'Great' for Dynamics 365 and Power BI integration vs Disco's 'Good.' Gartner notes 'strong analytics and dashboarding capabilities integrated with Power BI' as a core strength. Hierarchical process visualization and what-if simulation carried over from Minit. (Taloflow comparison; Gartner Peer Insights)

hated.point: Disco: Discovery-only — no conformance checking, simulation, BPMN modeling, or predictive analytics built in
hated.evidence: Repeatedly cited as the #1 limitation across Gartner Peer Insights, G2, and comparison sites: 'limited functionality (only discovery).' ProcessMind comparison explicitly lists: 'Disco does not include features like modeling, simulation, or collaboration.' Users must export to ProM or buy a second tool for advanced analysis.

hated.point: Disco: Closed data / no API access — cannot pipe analysis results into BI or automation tools
hated.evidence: Gartner 2024 reviewer: 'closed data — no way to easily export the analysis data to integrate with other tools in order to extend the functionality.' Another Gartner reviewer noted 'there is no way to guide or influence its processing.' Export only works as XES/MXML event logs back to academic tools, not structured data to dashboards.

hated.point: Disco: No cloud, no collaboration, no team sharing — desktop-only siloes analysts
hated.evidence: Multiple comparison sources describe Disco as 'best suited for technical users or auditors who need fast, standalone mining in a secure on-prem environment without collaboration or cloud access.' ProcessMind comparison: 'SaaS-first' is listed as a key competitor advantage over Disco's on-premises-only stance. No multi-user concurrent workflows.

hated.point: Disco: Opaque, contact-only pricing creates friction for procurement
hated.evidence: No public pricing anywhere — fluxicon.com/disco/buy redirects to a contact form. Capterra, G2, and SoftwareSuggest all say 'pricing not available.' Perpetual-license model with undisclosed costs makes budget approvals difficult for corporate procurement. Contrast: ProcessMind publishes $99–$199/month tiers.

hated.point: Disco: Data preparation / CSV mapping is the hardest step and a known friction point
hated.evidence: Fluxicon's own documentation acknowledges: 'configuring CSV data for import — mapping columns to case ID, activity names, and timestamps — is arguably the most complex task for most Disco users.' Multi-source event logs require ETL outside Disco. Fluxicon built 'Airlift' specifically to address this bottleneck (Disco 1.7, 2014).

hated.point: QPR ProcessAnalyzer: UI/UX is outdated and unintuitive — especially for non-technical business users
hated.evidence: PeerSpot reviewer (Director, consultancy): 'The user interface of QPR ProcessAnalyzer could improve, it is not very intuitive.' Second reviewer: stability issues plus 'communication with clients could be improved.' G2 Gartner reviewers echo that interface is 'slightly outdated for large data pools.' Advanced customisation requires scripting in a proprietary expression language.

hated.point: QPR ProcessAnalyzer: Proprietary expression language has steep learning curve for advanced work
hated.evidence: Nerdisa review (2025): 'to create more advanced calculations in dashboards or calculated attributes, Custom Expressions (with Expression Language, which is not a very intuitive language) are needed, which in turn requires almost always some customer support.' Reviewer suggests 'more examples are needed.' Chart adjustments also change unexpectedly after saving.

hated.point: Mehrwerk mpmX: Hard-dependency on Qlik Sense as a platform — buyers who aren't Qlik shops face a double procurement problem
hated.evidence: Gartner Peer Insights: 'dependency from third-party tool as a platform' listed as a top limitation. 'Development in text files on a file share is not state of the art' and 'missing versioning out of the box.' E-learning is behind a paywall. 'Unnecessary complicated software delivery process.' For non-Qlik shops, MPM effectively adds the full cost of Qlik on top.

hated.point: Mehrwerk mpmX: Not accessible to business users without Qlik/technical experience
hated.evidence: Gartner review: 'only specific to certain user categories — for business users without experience it is kind of difficult to use and to get benefits.' The tool leverages Qlik's associative engine, which while powerful, has its own learning curve on top of process mining concepts.

hated.point: Minit/Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining: $5,000/tenant/month price point makes process mining prohibitive outside Power Platform EA customers
hated.evidence: Multiple sources confirm the Process Mining add-on is priced at $5,000 per tenant per month billed annually (on top of Power Automate Premium). A December 2025 Gartner review explicitly called it 'very expensive to use.' G2 reviewers flag licensing complexity: 'a barrier to innovation where users... have to pause to calculate if the licensing cost outweighs the efficiency gains.'

hated.point: Skan.ai: Limited customization and integration options — struggles with complex enterprise process structures
hated.evidence: Gartner 2024 reviewer: 'limited customization and integration options' and 'may not be optimal for companies with complex structures.' G2 reviewers note 'not many features or integrations available.' Positioned as a Niche Player in 2024 MQ — limited breadth vs. Celonis/SAP/UiPath leaders.

hated.point: Skan.ai: Requires significant organizational buy-in and sensor installation planning for large-scale deployments
hated.evidence: AiChief review summary: 'may require significant organizational buy-in for full deployment' and 'initial setup and sensor installation might need careful planning for large-scale environments.' Desktop agent-based approach adds HR/privacy governance overhead regardless of technical privacy controls.

hated.point: Workfellow/ProcessMaker PI: Product gaps at time of Gartner review — benchmarks and predictive analytics were under development
hated.evidence: Gartner Peer Insights noted 'limited integration depth and early-stage product gaps such as benchmarks and predictive analytics under development.' One reviewer explicitly stated they 'decided to stop using this solution in favour of a competitor.' Acquisition by ProcessMaker in April 2024 adds uncertainty about roadmap continuity.

missing_or_frustrating.point: Disco users want conformance checking and simulation without having to buy/learn a second tool
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: ProcessMind comparison blog and multiple Gartner reviews document that the most common reason users 'graduate from' Disco is the absence of conformance/simulation. Users cite needing ProM or a separate enterprise tool just to answer 'are we compliant?' — a capability many competitors include natively. (processmind.com comparison; Gartner Peer Insights)

missing_or_frustrating.point: Disco users want a cloud/SaaS version for collaboration — sharing analyses with non-technical stakeholders is currently painful
missing_or_frustrating.evidence: ProcessMind comparison: 'SaaS-first, multi-tenant, private cloud optional' is listed as a key competitive advantage over Disco's desktop-only approach. Broader market data: cloud held 66.8% share in 2025 with 32.47% CAGR. Disco's desktop model means analyses cannot be shared as live interactive views — only as screenshots or exports. missing_or_frustrating.point: QPR users want a more intuitive UI for business users — too many advanced features require scripting support tickets

missing_or_frustrating.point: Mehrwerk users want versioning, a modern development workflow, and lower barrier for non-Qlik teams

missing_or_frustrating.evidence: G2 reviewers: 'not many features or integrations available.' Gartner 2024: 'limited customization and integration options.' missing_or_frustrating.point: Power Automate Process Mining users want simpler, transparent licensing — the $5K/tenant/month barrier is killing adoption in mid-market

switch_drivers: WHY USERS CHOOSE Disco: Zero setup, desktop privacy, scientific credibility from ProM lineage, academic familiarity (used in university process mining courses globally), and the cultural cachet of the 'original' commercial PM tool. Particularly strong for one-off consulting projects and quick workshops.

WHY USERS LEAVE Disco: Outgrow discovery-only scope — when projects require conformance checking, simulation, BPMN modeling, or API-driven continuous monitoring, Disco has no answer. The lack of cloud/SaaS sharing becomes painful when stakeholders need self-service dashboards.

WHY USERS CHOOSE QPR ProcessAnalyzer: Price/quality ratio below Celonis tier, good root-cause and KPI dashboarding, and strong vendor support responsiveness. Often chosen by Nordic/European firms and regulated-industry customers who value governance features.

WHY USERS LEAVE QPR ProcessAnalyzer: UI feels dated, expression-language dependency creates hidden consultant costs for customization, and stability concerns appear in multiple reviews. Enterprise competitors (Celonis, SAP Signavio) are increasingly chosen by accounts that outgrow QPR.

WHY USERS CHOOSE Mehrwerk mpmX: Already a Qlik shop — adoption is near-frictionless because they already have the platform, connectors, and trained BI users. Certified SAP connector is a key pull for SAP-heavy German/European clients.

WHY USERS LEAVE or AVOID Mehrwerk mpmX: Not a Qlik shop? Don't bother — the double procurement friction (Qlik + MPM) is a dealbreaker. Modern DevOps teams balk at file-share-based configuration and no versioning.

WHY USERS CHOOSE Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining: Deep Microsoft 365/Power Platform bet — if the organization is standardizing on the Microsoft stack, Power Automate PM is the path of least resistance. Power BI integration is a genuine differentiator for teams already building BI in that ecosystem.

WHY USERS LEAVE or AVOID Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining: $5K/tenant/month add-on pricing eliminates mid-market. Users who were Minit customers pre-acquisition have to re-evaluate as the product is rebuilt inside Power Automate; some Minit-specific features were reimplemented on Power BI (replaced Qlik analytics).

WHY USERS CHOOSE Workfellow/ProcessMaker PI: Want zero-integration task+process mining hybrid with GDPR-first European credentials; 30-day deployment promise resonates with buyers burned by Celonis 18-month implementations.

WHY USERS LEAVE Workfellow: Product immaturity (benchmarks/predictive under development at time of reviews); at least one Gartner reviewer explicitly switched to a competitor. ProcessMaker acquisition (April 2024) introduces roadmap risk that has likely increased churn anxiety.

WHY USERS CHOOSE Skan.ai: Zero backend integration requirement is genuinely unique — works via desktop screen-observation agents, which means no data warehouse, no SAP connector project, no IT involvement for initial POC. Privacy-compliant continuous monitoring is a key sell to regulated industries.

WHY USERS LEAVE or AVOID Skan.ai: Limited customization and integration depth, enterprise-only pricing with no transparency, and the organizational overhead of deploying and getting HR/works-council buy-in for desktop agents. Niche Player in 2024 MQ signals limited breadth vs. leaders.

research.scope: Open-source / self-host process mining ecosystem: PM4Py, ProM, bupaR, Apromore Community Edition / Core. FlowMiner's most direct audience — researchers, data scientists, and practitioners who self-host or build custom pipelines.
