maps.summary: FlowMiner has an unusually deep algorithmic backend for an early-stage product. Core process mining (discovery, conformance, bottleneck, variants, drift, queue mining, causal, simulation/DES, predictive) is real, working code with Rust acceleration paths, cross-validated ML models, and academic citations. The operational layer (alerts, action rules, initiatives, dashboards, scorecards, governance) is CRUD-complete and wired to the mining engine. Connectors exist for 15+ systems but most have real fetch logic. The weaker areas are OCEL/OCPM (the OC-DFG and summary are shipped but OPerA metrics require an optional `ocpa` dep that may not be installed), task mining (pattern discovery is a simple n-gram counter), and SSO/SAML (fully gated on env-var flags that are off by default).

capabilities.name: Discovery — DFG
capabilities.notes: Full Rust-accelerated DFG with performance colouring, percentile-based edge colours, and start/end activity detection. Falls back to pm4py.

capabilities.name: Discovery — Alpha Miner
capabilities.notes: Delegates to pm4py.discover_petri_net_alpha; petri-net-to-activity-graph conversion is shared with Heuristic/Inductive.

capabilities.name: Discovery — Heuristic Miner
capabilities.notes: Rust path (~20x faster than pm4py) for the net, fallback to pm4py. Note: uses unfilterd pm4py net to preserve split/join semantics.

capabilities.name: Discovery — Inductive Miner (IM + IMf)
capabilities.notes: IM uses Rust (~95x faster, byte-identical to pm4py). IMf (noise_threshold>0) uses pm4py. Both exposed via noise_threshold param.

capabilities.name: Discovery — Split Miner v2
capabilities.notes: Full concurrency-matrix approach (Augusto et al. 2022) when start timestamps are present. Falls back to heuristic-net approx otherwise. Annotates edges as sequence/parallel/choice.

capabilities.name: Discovery — ILP Miner
capabilities.notes: pm4py.discover_petri_net_ilp wrapper. Sampled to 20k cases on large logs to bound runtime.

capabilities.name: Discovery — Correlation Miner (no case IDs)
capabilities.notes: Wraps pm4py correlation_mining submodule. Returns error dict when the pm4py submodule is absent (graceful but silent).

capabilities.name: Conformance — Token-based Replay
capabilities.notes: Rust-accelerated. Samples precision/generalization to 120k events on very large logs with documented accuracy bound (~1-2%). Reports fitness, precision, generalization, deviations.

capabilities.name: Conformance — Alignment-based (A*)
capabilities.notes: Uses REACH/DIJKSTRA_LESS_MEMORY variant where available. Routes to decomposed aligner for >5000 cases or >1000 variants automatically.

capabilities.name: Conformance — Decomposed Alignment (SESE)
capabilities.notes: Falls back to token replay if pm4py decomp_alignments is unavailable. Returns per-case cost rather than per-move diagnostics.

capabilities.name: Conformance — Footprints (structural)
capabilities.notes: Cheap structural conformance for large logs before committing to alignment.

capabilities.name: Conformance — JSD Stochastic
capabilities.notes: Jensen-Shannon Distance (Li, Polyvyanyy & Leemans, ICPM 2024). Model sampled via pm4py playout. Falls back to alignment if playout unavailable.

capabilities.name: Conformance — EMD Stochastic
capabilities.notes: Earth Mover's Distance (Polyvyanyy et al., IS 2021). scipy Wasserstein approximation on rank-encoded variants — documented limitation that rank encoding loses edit-distance geometry.

capabilities.name: Conformance — Timed-Declare / SLA
capabilities.notes: Time-bounded DECLARE constraints (response/precedence/existence/absence with SLA window T and optional business-days mode). Cached per constraint set.

capabilities.name: Performance / Bottleneck Analysis
capabilities.notes: Rust-accelerated. Computes DBSM composite score (delay 40% + resource pressure 30% + cycle-time impact 30%). Classifies bottlenecks into critical/high/medium/low severity.

capabilities.name: Queue Mining (M/M/c Erlang-C)
capabilities.notes: Senderovich et al. IS 2015 approach. Per-activity wait decomposition: resource contention + inter-batch wait + external dependency. Stability flag when rho >= 1.

capabilities.name: Drift Detection (JSD window sliding)
capabilities.notes: Sliding window (auto/day/week/month/Ncases) with JSD between consecutive transition distributions. Explains drift as added/removed/magnitude-changed edges.

capabilities.name: Causal DAG (LiNGAM)
capabilities.notes: DirectLiNGAM over per-case activity dwell times (Fournier et al., KI 2025). Falls back to Pearson correlation graph if `lingam` package not installed. LiNGAM is an optional dep.

capabilities.name: Simulation / DES
capabilities.notes: Full DES with exponential arrivals, empirical bootstrap durations, resource pools, gateway probabilities. Uses simpy when available; pure-Python priority-queue fallback. Multi-run with scenario/baseline delta.

capabilities.name: Digital Twin Parameters
capabilities.notes: Extracts activity duration distributions, inter-arrival, resource calendar, and branching probabilities for simulation seeding.

capabilities.name: Predictive — Remaining Time (GBR)
capabilities.notes: GradientBoostingRegressor with 5-fold OOF cross-validation, model persistence via model_store, confidence interval via residual std. Rust-accelerated prefix feature extraction.

capabilities.name: Predictive — Outcome Classification (RF)
capabilities.notes: RandomForestClassifier with StratifiedKFold OOF AUC. SLA threshold configurable; model cached per (log, threshold) pair.

capabilities.name: Predictive — Next Activity (RF)
capabilities.notes: RandomForestClassifier with 80/20 train/val split. Returns top-3 activities with probabilities.

capabilities.name: Predictive — Suffix Prediction (iterative RF+GBR)
capabilities.notes: Iterative RF next-activity + GBR remaining-time chain. Inspired by SuTraN (ICPM 2024). Stops at detected sink activities. Returns per-step remaining-time estimates.

capabilities.name: Predictive — SHAP Explainability
capabilities.notes: shap.TreeExplainer lazy-imported. Returns waterfall-ready base + predicted values for outcome/remaining_time. Falls back gracefully if shap not installed.

capabilities.name: Predictive — Alarm Scoring (SLA breach)
capabilities.notes: Scores open-at-cutoff cases on in-progress prefixes. Derives default as-of from ~0.6 quantile of case end times. Returns breach probability + predicted remaining time + top next activities.

capabilities.name: OCEL Upload, Summary, OC-DFG
capabilities.notes: Supports .jsonocel, .xmlocel, .sqlite. Bounded LRU in-memory store (max 50). Per-ocel-id load locks prevent thundering-herd on first panel visit. Redis result cache.

capabilities.name: OCEL — OPerA Performance Metrics
capabilities.notes: Endpoint exists (GET /ocel/{id}/opera-performance). Requires optional `ocpa` package. If ocpa not installed the endpoint returns an error. Roadmap doc confirms this is shipped.

capabilities.name: OCEL — State-Aware OCPM
capabilities.notes: Service file exists and is mentioned in roadmap as shipped. Depth of implementation unclear without reading the full file.

capabilities.name: Root Cause Analysis
capabilities.notes: Statistical: Kruskal-Wallis + Mann-Whitney for categorical attributes; Pearson correlation for numeric. Returns ranked factors and correlations.

capabilities.name: Decision Mining (Decision Trees on branches)
capabilities.notes: DecisionTreeClassifier (max_depth=3) per activity with multiple predecessors. Exports human-readable rule text and feature importances.

capabilities.name: Trace Clustering (KMeans + DBSCAN)
capabilities.notes: KMeans via pm4py feature clustering. DBSCAN on PCA-reduced activity-occurrence matrix with vectorised groupby pivot (replaced O(cases x events) loop). Capped at 20k cases.

capabilities.name: Organisational Mining / Social Network Analysis
capabilities.notes: Rust-accelerated handover network. SNA metrics, org role detection, four-eyes checks available.

capabilities.name: Agent/Bot Detection
capabilities.notes: Heuristic-based (naming patterns + speed + consistency). Classifies resources as human/bot/system. Computes automation_ratio.

capabilities.name: Connectors — SAP (OData + RFC + Change Documents)
capabilities.notes: OData and RFC modes. Change-document mode (CDHDR/CDPOS) with CDPOS join for field-level changes. RFC requires pyrfc + SAP NW RFC SDK.

capabilities.name: Connectors — Salesforce, ServiceNow, Jira, GitHub, Shopify
capabilities.notes: Each has real test_connection and fetch_data implementations using httpx.

capabilities.name: Connectors — Oracle Fusion, Workday, SAP Ariba, Coupa, Odoo, Zendesk
capabilities.notes: Files exist with BaseConnector structure. Depth of fetch_data implementations varies; not read in full.

capabilities.name: Connectors — Incremental Sync
capabilities.notes: Module exists. Depth unknown without reading.

capabilities.name: AI/LLM Chat (streaming, tool-use)
capabilities.notes: NDJSON streaming chat with agentic tool-use loop. Tool catalogue includes show_bottlenecks, show_rework, show_variants, show_conformance, filter operations. Tools return data + render hint + summary triple.

capabilities.name: AI/LLM — LLM provider abstraction
capabilities.notes: Covers Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Ollama.

capabilities.name: AI/LLM — Column mapping suggester
capabilities.notes: LLM-powered auto-suggestion of case/activity/timestamp column mappings from raw CSV headers.

capabilities.name: MCP Server (stdio)
capabilities.notes: 8 tools: list_event_logs, get_log_summary, get_bottlenecks, get_variants, get_rework, get_conformance, get_dfg, get_insights, ask_natural_language. Single-user scoped via env var. Auth delegates to REST access checks.

capabilities.name: Governance (draft/review/published lifecycle + EA capability tree)
capabilities.notes: GovernanceEntry with promote endpoint and immutable transition audit trail. Capability tree with parent_id hierarchy and linked_event_log_ids. LogVersions with filter_payload.

capabilities.name: Initiatives / ROI Tracker
capabilities.notes: Baseline + target + current_value tracking. /measure endpoint recomputes from live log. Pre-built value calculator library (get_calculators). Project-level savings summary.

capabilities.name: Alerts (metric threshold triggers)
capabilities.notes: CRUD + /test endpoint. Channels: email (SMTP), webhook, Slack, Teams, in_app. /test evaluates metric from live log before sending. Channel-readiness check before delivery attempt.

capabilities.name: Action Rules (condition → action automation)
capabilities.notes: Condition dict evaluated against event log; matching cases dispatched as actions. Cooldown, trigger_count, execution history. dry_run support.

capabilities.name: Scorecards (cost-of-quality + workflow export + DP benchmark)
capabilities.notes: Cost-of-quality: rework + bottleneck FTE hours + escalation heuristic. Workflow export: Temporal/n8n/Airflow code from happy path. DP benchmark: Laplace-noise cross-team benchmark with configurable epsilon.

capabilities.name: Dashboards (custom, shareable)
capabilities.notes: CRUD with share tokens for public sharing.

capabilities.name: Scheduled Reports
capabilities.notes: File exists; assumed to be CRUD for scheduled PDF/email report delivery.

capabilities.name: Auth — JWT + rate limiting + password policy
capabilities.notes: First-user auto-admin bootstrap. JWT with JTI revocation. SlowAPI rate limiting on auth endpoints. Strong password policy enforcement.

capabilities.name: Auth — OIDC SSO + TOTP MFA
capabilities.notes: OIDC authorization code + PKCE. TOTP MFA (HMAC-SHA1 pure Python, no pyotp dep). Both gated on env vars; return 503 if unconfigured.

capabilities.name: Auth — SAML SSO
capabilities.notes: Gated on SAML_ENABLED env var. Uses python3-saml lazy import. Returns 503 if not configured. ACS endpoint exchanges SAMLResponse for FlowMiner JWT.

capabilities.name: Privacy / Anonymisation
capabilities.notes: Per-project config: anonymize_resources, anonymize_case_ids, masked_columns, role-based raw-data access (viewer_sees_raw / analyst_sees_raw). Pseudonymisation uses HMAC-derived per-column salt + SHA-256 truncated to 16 hex chars.

capabilities.name: Audit Logs
capabilities.notes: Immutable audit trail. Governance transitions recorded separately.

capabilities.name: Task Mining (desktop event capture + n-gram patterns)
capabilities.notes: Recording ingest API is complete. Pattern miner is a windowed n-gram counter (3-8 grams, min_frequency=3). No suffix-array or advanced sequence mining. Automatable_score heuristic present but simple.

capabilities.name: DMN Export
capabilities.notes: File exists. DMN is the OMG Decision Model and Notation standard. Depth unknown without reading.

capabilities.name: Log Builder (visual ETL / log construction)
capabilities.notes: Multi-file with recipe support. Presumably constructs event logs from raw tables with join/pivot logic.

capabilities.name: Sustainability / Carbon Metrics
capabilities.notes: Service file exists. No API router for this found in the router list, suggesting it may be consumed internally or not yet surfaced.

capabilities.name: Formal Methods (Declare, Log Skeleton, BPMN export)
capabilities.notes: Implied by DeclareResponse, LogSkeletonResponse, BPMNExportResponse schemas in mining.py router. formal_methods.py exists.

capabilities.name: Custom KPIs
capabilities.notes: Router file exists. Likely CRUD for user-defined KPI formulas; depth unknown.

capabilities.name: Counterfactual Analysis
capabilities.notes: Mentioned in roadmap as shipped. File exists. Not read in full; likely genetic-algorithm or perturbation-based counterfactual generation.

capabilities.name: Rust Acceleration Layer
capabilities.notes: Covers DFG (400x faster), Heuristic Miner (20x), Inductive Miner (95x), token replay, precision, generalization, bottlenecks, variants, prefix features, SNA, handover network, rework, edge stats, case overlap, temporal profile. All paths have Python fallbacks.

ux_observations.observation: The causal DAG endpoint silently falls back from DirectLiNGAM to a Pearson correlation graph when the `lingam` package is not installed. The response changes method to 'pearson_correlation' but the API contract and any UI label would need to distinguish these — an undirected correlation graph is not a causal DAG and should not be presented as one.

The EMD stochastic conformance implementation uses a rank-encoding approximation for Wasserstein distance instead of trace-edit-distance-weighted EMD. The code documents this limitation explicitly, but the API response key is 'emd_distance' with no qualifier. A consumer reading only the response will think they got a true EMD value.

The alignment conformance endpoint returns `precision: None` and `generalization: None` always — these are only computed in the token-replay path. The alignment path silently omits them rather than computing them via the equivalent alignment-based precision measure. A user comparing conformance methods will see inconsistent result shapes.

OPerA performance metrics (the primary OCEL differentiator against Celonis) require the optional `ocpa` package. If it is not installed, the endpoint returns an error rather than a degraded result. The main requirements file should be checked to confirm ocpa is listed; if it is optional, the error message should be actionable.

SSO (OIDC) and SAML both return HTTP 503 when unconfigured. This is the correct behaviour, but means a first-time admin who navigates to /auth/sso/login or /auth/saml/login before setting env vars gets a 503 with no guidance. The frontend needs to gate these links on a `sso_configured` status check.

The cost-of-quality escalation heuristic is a string match for 'escalat' in the activity name. This will miss escalations named differently and fire on unrelated activities (e.g. 'escalate_priority'). It is a rough proxy, not a configurable rule, and the label in the response does not signal that.

The DES pure-Python fallback (_run_pqueue) does not model resource contention — resources are tracked for utilization accounting but jobs are never actually queued. A scenario that changes resource pool capacities will show the correct utilization numbers but not the correct case duration impact (no queue wait). The simpy path does model contention correctly. If simpy is not installed, results are silently degraded without an API-level warning.

The privacy anonymisation uses deterministic SHA-256 pseudonyms scoped by a per-column salt. The code itself documents that this is NOT true anonymisation and is vulnerable to dictionary attack on small domains (employee IDs). The privacy config UI surface does not surface this caveat, which could lead to over-reliance on the feature for compliance.

capabilities.name: Navigation / Information Architecture
capabilities.notes: Sidebar is clean and collapsible with 4 sections (Workspace, Analyze, Govern, Admin) and 18 static nav items for non-admin, 21 for admin. The ActiveLogNav dynamically injects 5 quick-links + 'All analyses' when inside a log. Hover hints on jargon items (Object-Centric, Automations, Process Landscape) are present. However, ~30+ additional pages exist that are only reachable via the Cmd+K palette or within-log navigation — they are completely absent from the sidebar, creating a vast undiscoverable surface. The project detail page adds another 6 tool links (Benchmark, Task Mining, KPIs, Journey Maps, Log Builder, Scheduled Reports). Mission Control, Process Animation, Drift, Root Cause, Rework, Comparison, Dotted Chart, Social Network, Sustainability, Automation ROI, Process Health, Causal Map, Pulse, Cases at Risk, Lineage — 15+ full pages — are absent from the sidebar.

capabilities.name: Onboarding wizard
capabilities.notes: 3-step checklist (Add data, Discover map, Run analysis) with real localStorage-backed completion tracking. Completion celebration fires when all 3 steps done. Three intent cards (Sample, Upload, Connect) plus prebuilt process packs. Checklist items are inline pills in a single row with ChevronRight separators — fine for 3 items but the row can wrap awkwardly. The completion mention of '30+ analyses' with a Cmd+K hint is good. The wizard is dismissible and re-openable. No explicit path back to the wizard once dismissed except from 'Getting started' — but no 'Getting started' sidebar entry exists to re-open it.

capabilities.name: Product tour
capabilities.notes: Per-route tour system with 4 tours (welcome, process-view, variants, ocpm). Longest-prefix route matching is correct. Tours persist per-id to localStorage; kill-switch via ?tours=off. The 'ocpm' tour references selector [data-tour='ocpm-improvements'] but that data attribute does not exist anywhere in OCPMPage.tsx — the tour step will silently spotlight nothing. Tour card positioning is pixel-math (top = spotlight.bottom + 12, bounded by viewport), which can place the card off-screen on small viewports. Clicking the backdrop dismisses the tour, which is an easy accidental trigger.

capabilities.name: Upload / Column mapping flow
capabilities.notes: 3-step wizard (Upload, Map Columns, Complete). Confidence-scored auto-detection with keyword weights. OCEL files skip mapping (self-describing). File summary bar shows row count, column count, and inferred date range. On completion, navigates directly to mission-control/:id rather than a dead-end 'done' screen. Demo mode shows a clean disabled state with docker-compose instructions. Back navigation within the wizard is present. Strong pattern overall.

capabilities.name: Process view / map
capabilities.notes: 6 tabs (Map, City, Happy Path, BPMN, Cases, Analysis). Tab bar + Quality + Export + Analysis Palette crammed into one flex-wrap row — on medium screens this row overflows and wraps, creating a 2-line top bar. The Map tab itself adds a second control strip with Map Options popover, Detail segment group, Clean View toggle, node/edge count, 'What does this map mean?', path search input, Group Activities button, Filter button, and Replay button. That is ~10 interactive controls on the control strip alone before any data is visible. The right panel is always-visible at w-64 even when no node is selected, wasting space. Auto-selects City tab for large logs (>=80 edges, >=30 nodes) and auto-enables Clean View for large graphs — both are good heuristics.

capabilities.name: AnalysisHub (17 sub-tools)
capabilities.notes: 17 analyses across 5 intent groups: Performance (6), Conformance (4), Behavior & Variants (2), Organization (3), Advanced & Data (3). Left sidebar list at w-48 with group headers and lock/star badges. Recommended analyses are starred. Locked analyses (missing resource column, etc.) show a lock icon with tooltip explaining how to unlock — this is good progressive disclosure. On mobile (md breakpoint), the sidebar collapses to max-h-56 scroll, which is usable. The hub header shows analysis description below the label.

capabilities.name: Filter system
capabilities.notes: Three parallel filter mechanisms coexist: (1) FilterPanel sidebar (timeframe, duration, activities, endpoints, resources, edges), (2) FilterChipBar (chip breadcrumb synced to the shared filterStore), (3) FilterExpressionBar (DSL text input). The comment in ProcessViewPage at line 100 explicitly flags this: 'Finding #13 — unify the filter systems.' The sidebar FilterPanel and the chip bar do communicate via useProcessFilters, but having 3 entry points with different mental models adds cognitive load. Duration filter input takes raw seconds with no range slider, requiring users to know that e.g. 86400 = 1 day — the format hint is tiny (9px fg-ghost text).

capabilities.name: Empty states
capabilities.notes: Shared EmptyState component with icon, title, description, action slot, compact variant. Used consistently across OverviewPage, ProjectPickerPage, and others. The 404 page uses inline JSX instead of this component — minor inconsistency.

capabilities.name: Error states
capabilities.notes: Compact and full-page variants. Both include role='alert', an icon, title, message, and optional retry button. Used consistently. The 404 page and a few inline map errors use custom JSX rather than ErrorState — minor inconsistency.

capabilities.name: Loading / progress feedback
capabilities.notes: AnalysisLoading shows elapsed seconds and escalating messages at 10s ('this can be slow') and 30s ('taking longer than expected, will time out at 45s'). LoadingSpinner has sm/md/lg/xl sizes and an optional text label. Skeleton primitives (Skeleton, SkeletonRow) are used on ProjectDetailPage for committed shell skeletons. Page-level Suspense is inside the Layout's <main>, so sidebar and header remain mounted during lazy chunk loading.

capabilities.name: AI chat (FloatingAIChat)
capabilities.notes: Global slide-in panel triggered from the persistent 'Ask AI' button in the header. Auto-detects the current event log from URL patterns across 14 route prefixes. Auto-injects active filter chips into every prompt. Shows a 'navigate to a log first' hint when no log is active. Provides AI-generated contextual suggestions and fallback default suggestions. Not visible or usable on routes without an event log — the button is always shown but the panel renders a 'no log' message, which could confuse users who click it from /projects or /overview.

capabilities.name: Keyboard shortcuts
capabilities.notes: Only 3 shortcuts are listed: '/' focuses search, Esc closes modals, '?' shows the shortcuts help. The modal itself only enumerates these 3. Cmd+K to open the analysis palette is mentioned in tour/onboarding copy but is not in the ShortcutsModal. The '/' shortcut tries to find 'header input[type=text]' — the search input uses type='search', so this shortcut silently fails.

capabilities.name: Mobile / responsive
capabilities.notes: Sidebar collapses to icon-only on desktop (w-[52px]) and slides off-screen on mobile with an overlay. Header has a mobile hamburger. ProcessViewPage uses h-[calc(100vh-7rem)] for the main canvas area; on mobile with a browser address bar this can overflow or clip. AnalysisHub sidebar max-h-56 scrollable on small screens. The multi-control ProcessView toolbar uses flex-wrap and md:gap-3, but no explicit tab-bar scrolling — at narrow widths the 6-tab bar + Quality + Export + Palette buttons likely overflow without scroll affordance. ProcessMap uses touch-action:none and cytoscape pinch-to-zoom, which is explicit and correct.

capabilities.name: Page count / IA sprawl
capabilities.notes: 49 page files registered. Of these, 47 are unique routes registered in App.tsx (Login, Register, SharedDashboard plus 44 protected routes). Of the 44 protected routes, only ~18 are reachable from the sidebar. The remaining ~26 pages are accessible only through within-log navigation, ProjectDetail tool cards, or Cmd+K palette discovery — they are not browsable. This means a new user has no systematic way to discover the full feature set.

capabilities.name: Dashboard system
capabilities.notes: Dashboard list, create modal (name, description, project picker), and a dedicated view page. Public share via /dashboards/shared/:shareToken is supported without authentication. Creation requires a project to be selected, which is good. The list page was only briefly reviewed.

capabilities.name: ProjectPickerPage (intermediate routing)
capabilities.notes: Smart auto-continue: if the user has a lastProjectId in UIStore or there is only one project, it redirects immediately without showing the picker. Only renders the grid when context is genuinely ambiguous. Good UX pattern that reduces navigation friction.

ux_observations.observation: The '/' keyboard shortcut to focus search silently fails. The shortcut handler queries 'header input[type=text]' but the search input in Header.tsx uses type='search', so the selector never matches. Users pressing '/' get no feedback and no focus.

The OCPM product tour step references selector [data-tour='ocpm-improvements'] but that attribute does not exist in OCPMPage.tsx. The step fires with spotlight=null, so the tour card floats in the middle of the screen with no highlighted element. The dev-time console.warn fires but in production it silently misbehaves.

26 of 44 protected pages are not reachable from the sidebar at all — including Drift, Root Cause, Rework, Dotted Chart, Social Network, Process Animation, Sustainability, Automation ROI, Process Health, Causal Map, Process Pulse, Cases at Risk, Lineage, Journey Maps, Task Mining, Mission Control, OCPM (from sidebar shows, but no sub-pages), and others. A user who never opens Cmd+K or navigates to ProjectDetail will never discover most of the product's analytical surface.

The ProcessView top bar contains 6 tabs + 'Quality' + 'Export' dropdown + 'Analysis Palette' button in a single flex-wrap row. On medium-width viewports this wraps to two lines, which visually breaks the layout and pushes map content down. The map control strip immediately below adds another ~10 interactive elements (Map Options, Detail segment, Clean, node/edge count, 'What does this map mean?', path search, Group Activities, Filter, Replay). This is the densest surface in the product and the one new users land on after upload.

Three parallel filter mechanisms coexist on the process map with partially overlapping mental models: FilterPanel sidebar (9 filter categories), FilterChipBar (chip breadcrumbs), and FilterExpressionBar (DSL). The code comment at line 100 itself flags this as 'Finding #13 — unify the filter systems.' Users encounter all three simultaneously on the map tab with no clear hierarchy or guidance about which to use.

The duration filter in FilterPanel takes raw seconds as a number input with only a tiny 9px hint showing the formatted range. Users must know that 86400 = 1 day, 3600 = 1 hour, etc. There is no range slider or formatted input. The placeholder shows formatted values (e.g. '2.3d') but the input itself accepts and stores raw seconds, creating a mismatch between the placeholder format and input format.

The onboarding wizard can be dismissed via the X button, and the tooltip says 'Hide — reopen any time from Getting started.' But there is no 'Getting started' sidebar entry and no visible mechanism to reopen the wizard once dismissed. The only way back is to clear the relevant localStorage key. This creates a one-way door for users who prematurely dismiss the wizard.

The 'Ask AI' button in the header is always visible regardless of page context. When clicked from a non-log page (e.g. /projects, /overview, /settings), the panel opens but renders a 'navigate to a log first' message. Users clicking AI from the home screen get a dead-end panel with no recovery action other than closing it. The button has no contextual tooltip indicating it only works on log pages.

ShortcutsModal only lists 3 shortcuts ('/', Esc, '?'), but the product has many more: Cmd+K for the analysis palette (prominently mentioned in tour and onboarding copy), the tour kill-switch (?tours=off), and the '/' search shortcut (which is broken — see separate observation). The modal is the first place a user would look for available shortcuts, and it severely underrepresents them.

The right panel on the ProcessView map tab is always rendered at w-64 (md:w-64) even when no node is selected. The empty state shows a LogVersionTree component. At smaller viewports (below md) it stacks below the map taking up full width. Users who never click a node pay the layout cost of this panel on every visit. Closing or collapsing the panel is not possible — only selecting then deselecting a node dismisses it.

The AnalysisHub sidebar at mobile breakpoints (below md) renders as a horizontally scrollable list capped at max-h-56. But the sidebar is 48px wide and the analysis names are 11px text — 17 items across 5 groups in 56px height means users see roughly 6-7 items before scrolling, with no visible scroll indicator and no count of hidden items. Discovery of analyses in the non-recommended groups requires active scrolling.

The '404' page uses inline JSX rather than the shared EmptyState and ErrorState components, producing a slightly different visual language (text-5xl font-bold text-fg-ghost for the '404', plain text below, btn-primary to navigate). Minor inconsistency but shows the pattern was not enforced for the shell-level pages.

Clicking the ProductTour backdrop (the dark overlay) immediately dismisses and marks the tour as complete, with no confirmation. A mis-click while reading a step silently ends the entire tour and sets localStorage to never show it again. There is no 'restart tour' option accessible to users.

ProcessViewPage and SimulationPage and SocialNetworkPage all use h-[calc(100vh-7rem)] for their canvas area. On mobile browsers with dynamic address bars (iOS Safari, Chrome Android) the address bar height changes as the user scrolls, causing the canvas to resize or clip. The calculation assumes a fixed browser chrome height which is a known mobile UX anti-pattern.

The ProcessView Map control strip buttons (Map Options, Detail, Clean, path search, Group Activities, Filter, Replay) use title attributes for tooltips but no aria-label on icon-only variants. The detail segment group buttons (Full, Medium, etc.) and algorithm buttons use segment-btn classes and only short labels visible on hover. These are not accessible to screen readers.

maps.summary: FlowMiner's frontend is architecturally mature — lazy-loaded routes, skeleton states, shared error/empty/loading components, a unified filter store, ARIA on the main interactive widgets, and a real multi-step onboarding wizard — but it is significantly over-featured relative to the discoverability surface. Of the 49 pages, only ~18 are reachable from the sidebar; the remaining ~26 analysis pages are invisible unless a user discovers Cmd+K or navigates through the ProjectDetail tool grid. The ProcessView page is the product's most important surface and also its most congested: a tab bar, a quality/export toolbar row, and a multi-control map strip stack on top of each other with up to 18 interactive controls visible simultaneously before any analysis content is shown. Three parallel filter mechanisms (FilterPanel, FilterChipBar, FilterExpressionBar) operate simultaneously with partially overlapping scope, and the codebase itself flags this as an unresolved finding. Several specific bugs exist in the onboarding layer: the '/' search shortcut silently fails (wrong input type selector), the OCPM product tour step has a broken selector (missing data-tour attribute), and the wizard's 'reopen from Getting started' tooltip refers to a sidebar entry that does not exist.

maps.area: New-User Journey: CSV Upload to First Insight

capabilities.name: README first-run guidance
capabilities.notes: Four concrete steps: clone → make init-env → make up → open localhost:3000. First-registration auto-promotion to admin is explicitly called out. The sample CSV path (docs/examples/running-example.csv) and the Settings → AI key setup path are both documented. No ambiguity about the happy path.

capabilities.name: Demo / sample data seeding
capabilities.notes: Five preloaded projects: running-example.csv (tiny/clean), sepsis.csv (1 050 cases, real hospital log), tpch_order_to_cash.csv (multi-table join output), bpic2019_p2p.csv.gz (251 734 cases, real SAP P2P), container_logistics.json (OCEL). The seeder is idempotent, runs on every boot when DEMO_MODE=true, handles OCEL warm-loading across container restarts, and purges + re-seeds on an hourly Celery beat job. Column mappings are pre-populated so logs land as 'ready' immediately — no Celery worker needed at boot. The demo user gets viewer role with an unguessable password so real login can't happen. Missing: the HR_Onboarding.1.csv and HR_Onboarding.2.csv example files exist in docs/examples but are NOT listed in DEMO_PROJECTS — a user who self-hosts and wants a comparison-view demo can't seed them automatically.

capabilities.name: Example files for self-hosted first run
capabilities.notes: Eight files: running-example.csv, sepsis.csv, tpch_order_to_cash.csv, bpic2019_p2p.csv.gz, container_logistics.json, sample-order-management.jsonocel, HR_Onboarding.1.csv, HR_Onboarding.2.csv. README tells you to use running-example.csv. That file uses pm4py's non-obvious column names (case:concept:name, concept:name, time:timestamp) — the auto-detector will catch them, but a newcomer reading the raw CSV would be confused by the duplicate Activity/Resource/Costs columns that appear alongside the XES-style ones.

capabilities.name: File upload UX
capabilities.notes: react-dropzone, drag-and-drop + click-to-browse, fake animated progress bar (random increments up to 90%, jumps to 100% on completion), 500 MB cap displayed. Accepted types shown as pill badges. Accepts .csv, .xes, .xlsx, .parquet at the component level; UploadPage also passes .json/.jsonocel/.xmlocel/.sqlite. Error messages for oversized and wrong-type files. The progress bar is cosmetic/fake — there is no real XHR upload progress. For a 50 MB CSV this still looks fine; for a 250 MB file the bar will sit at 90% for an unknown period.

capabilities.name: Column auto-detection (name-based, in UploadPage)
capabilities.notes: Keyword weight table (case/trace/journey/order → case_id etc.). Scores all columns per target field, picks the highest, stores a confidence float (0–1). Runs only on the SAMPLE preview and only produces a best-score value — it does NOT actually pre-select the dropdown (that is ColumnMapper's job). The two detectors (UploadPage name-scorer and ColumnMapper auto-detect) run in parallel and are reconciled by ColumnMapper's combineDetect(), but the confidence scores passed as props from UploadPage are only used as a display-level fallback when ColumnMapper's own fieldConfidence map has no entry. In practice ColumnMapper always wins because it runs its own detection on mount.

capabilities.name: Column auto-detection (name + content-based, in ColumnMapper)
capabilities.notes: Two-signal system: (1) name-based exact/partial keyword match (HINTS table, exact = 0.9 score); (2) content-based: ISO-8601/epoch ratio >= 0.6 for timestamp, UUID ratio or 100% uniqueness >= 0.5 for case_id, low-cardinality string for activity (capped at 0.7). Agreement between the two signals boosts confidence by 0.15. Confidence displayed as a color-coded percentage pill (green >= 70%, amber >= 40%, red = 'review'). Optional fields (resource, cost) stay name-only at 0.6. Works on anonymised/renamed columns because the content signal fires even when names give nothing. The running-example.csv has redundant column names (Activity and concept:name both present); the name detector will pick 'concept:name' for activity (hits the 'activity' keyword via 'concept:name'? — no, it won't; the hint 'activity' would match the col named 'Activity' via lowercase partial). So auto-detect is correct for that file.

capabilities.name: Column mapper UX — data preview + live stats
capabilities.notes: Split two-column layout: dropdowns on the left, live-highlighted data preview table and Quick Preview stats (cases/events/activities from the sample) on the right. Column headers are colour-coded by role. Duplicate-column validation with inline error messages. Additional-columns chip picker for enrichment attributes. Mapping summary card. 'Start Mining' CTA bottom-right disabled until all three required fields are filled.

capabilities.name: Post-upload navigation — direct to Mission Control
capabilities.notes: On successful mapping save, navigate() goes straight to /mission-control/:eventLogId — no dead-end 'done' screen for the standard flow. The OCEL flow still hits the 'done' step (line 66–74) because mapping is skipped, and shows explicit CTAs (See Insights, View OCPM, Back to Project). The success notification includes a sample-derived '~N cases · M activities' estimate so the user immediately understands what they uploaded.

capabilities.name: Data quality report
capabilities.notes: Overall score (0–100, colour-coded Good/Fair/Poor), issue list with severity (error/warning/info), category badge, affected row count + percentage per issue. Timestamp repair tool: preview mode shows ties/inversions/outliers to fix, then 'Apply repair' applies it. Card only renders on the 'done' step (OCEL excluded) — but the standard flow now navigates away before reaching 'done', so in the current code a new user uploading a CSV will NEVER see the DataQualityCard on the upload flow; they go straight to Mission Control. The card is also available on other analysis pages via useAnalysisData.

capabilities.name: Mission Control — first post-upload view
capabilities.notes: Parallel-loads insights, automation candidates, AI narrative, and case list. Renders: KPI strip (critical/warning/total/top automation ROI), executive briefing (AI narrative in markdown), SLA burn-down bar chart with top-5 slowest cases and a 7d/14d/30d threshold toggle, and a severity-ranked priority feed of all issues. All-failed guard shows a retry button. No 'blank canvas' — if any one of the four calls succeeds, useful content appears. The AI narrative requires a configured LLM provider; without one it simply won't appear (no error shown to user).

capabilities.name: Overview page — cross-project dashboard
capabilities.notes: Stat tiles (projects, event logs, total cases/events, active alerts, initiatives), three value cards (realized savings, throughput density, working capital), recent event logs feed with clickable rows. Empty state when no logs exist — navigates to /projects. Not the first page a new user sees after upload (they land on Mission Control), but is a useful second-level landing page for returning users.

capabilities.name: Floating AI chat panel
capabilities.notes: Slides in from the right on any authenticated page. Detects event-log UUID from 14 recognised route patterns. Auto-focuses input. On open, fetches data-anchored suggestions and top findings from a cached backend endpoint. Injects current page label and active filter chips into every prompt. Shows top findings as clickable cards that prefill the input. Supports tool-use streaming (tool start/result events rendered as inline charts). Prefill API for external components to open chat with a pre-written question. Graceful 'navigate to a log first' hint when not on a log route. Messages are markdown-rendered for assistant turns.

capabilities.name: AskAI panel (AnalysisHub tab)
capabilities.notes: Duplicate chat surface embedded in the Analysis Hub tab. Adds: Chat vs Agent mode toggle (agent mode calls aiApi.agentRun), activity-name-seeded suggestion chips and native datalist autocomplete (?q= deep-link handling from ⌘K palette). Both surfaces share the same aiApi.chatStream/agentRun backend. Having two distinct chat UIs risks confusing users about which to use.

capabilities.name: AI chat tools (backend)
capabilities.notes: Seven tools: show_bottlenecks (bar chart, frequency-filtered), show_rework (bar chart), show_variants (horizontal bar), show_events_over_time (line chart, auto-coarsen if >60 buckets), get_summary (metric card), show_conformance (EMD + severity breakdown + deviating variants chart), propose_filters (validated filter chips with an Apply button). Each returns data/render/summary; LLM only sees summary, frontend sees the full render spec. Tool errors return graceful envelopes. All tools are bounded to <2s latency. Missing: no case-level drill-down tool (e.g. 'show me the 5 slowest cases'), no social-network tool, no simulation tool.

capabilities.name: Onboarding wizard
capabilities.notes: localStorage-backed 3-step checklist (Add data / Discover map / Run deep analysis). Three intent cards: sample data, upload, connect. Surfaces prebuilt process packs if the backend recipe endpoint responds. Progress bar. 100% completion triggers a celebration state with ⌘K hint. The 'map' and 'analysis' onboarding steps are marked by calls to markOnboardingStep() that must exist elsewhere in the codebase; UploadPage marks 'upload' on line 63 but 'map' and 'analysis' are not marked in the files reviewed here — may be in ProcessMap or AnalysisPalette.

capabilities.name: Connector form (SQL + SaaS)
capabilities.notes: 3-step wizard (Choose source → Connect → Finish). Backend-driven connector registry with static fallback. Supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, CSV Watch, REST API, Jira, GitHub, Odoo, Zendesk, Shopify, SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Snowflake, BigQuery, Workday, Coupa, Ariba, Oracle Fusion. Column mapping step on Finish (shows schema-discovered dropdowns if test passed; falls back to free-text). Schedule preset buttons + custom cron. The 'Test Connection' button is disabled until after first save — a significant friction point for new users configuring a DB connector.

capabilities.name: Extraction Copilot
capabilities.notes: Conversational modal for writing SQL from raw table schemas. Two-pane: chat on left, stepwise SQL/pandas code blocks on right with per-step rationale, copy buttons, and a confidence bar. Context inputs for objective and table schema (CREATE TABLE pasted). Resets on open. 'Generated by AI — review before running' disclaimer on every code block. The confidence bar is frontend-only display of the backend's returned score. No ability to run the SQL in-product or pipe it directly to a connector — copy-paste gap.

ux_observations.observation: DataQualityCard is rendered only on the 'done' step of UploadPage, but the standard CSV flow now navigates directly from mapping to Mission Control (navigate() on line 213 of UploadPage.tsx), completely bypassing the 'done' step and thus the quality report. A first-time user uploading a messy CSV with timestamp inversions or null case IDs will never see the data quality warnings.

The 'Test Connection' button in ConnectorForm is disabled for new (unsaved) connectors with the tooltip 'Save the connector first — the test runs against the saved configuration'. This means a user must commit credentials to the database before verifying connectivity — the opposite of what they expect. It also reveals that the test endpoint operates on the stored config, not the form state, which is a backend limitation exposed as UX friction.

Upload progress bar is cosmetic (random increments to 90%, then jumps to 100%). For large files (100–250 MB) the bar will stall at 90% for an indeterminate period with no indication of actual bytes transferred. No time estimate, no 'still uploading' copy, no cancel button.

The running-example.csv referenced in the README has 9 columns including duplicate semantic columns (both 'Activity' and 'concept:name', both 'Resource' and 'org:resource'). A first-time user who opens the file to understand its structure before uploading will be confused by the column names. The README does not warn about this.

The AI chat feature requires a pre-configured LLM provider (Settings → AI key). Mission Control's 'Executive briefing' section silently omits when no provider is configured — there is no call-to-action pointing the new user to Settings. A fresh self-hosted install with no AI key gives a process map and priority feed but no AI narrative, and the user has no in-product hint that the narrative is gated on a key.

Two parallel chat surfaces exist — FloatingAIChat (global slide-in panel, always accessible from the header) and AskAI (embedded in the Analysis Hub tab). They share the same backend but have different affordances (FloatingAIChat shows top-findings cards and filter-chip context; AskAI has Chat/Agent mode toggle and activity-name autocomplete). A new user landing on Mission Control has no reason to know the Analysis Hub tab also contains a chat. There is no explanation of the difference between the two.

The Extraction Copilot produces SQL and pandas snippets but has no path to run the query inside FlowMiner. The user must copy the SQL, run it in their own tool, export to CSV, and re-upload. The copilot is not wired to the connector form at all — there is no 'Use this SQL in a connector' button.

The HR_Onboarding.1.csv and HR_Onboarding.2.csv example files exist in docs/examples and would be ideal for demonstrating the comparison view (a high-value differentiator), but they are absent from DEMO_PROJECTS in demo_seeder.py. A demo-mode visitor cannot see the comparison view with preloaded data.

The ColumnMapper's 'Start Mining' button is right-aligned at the very bottom of a tall two-column form. On a 1024px-height display the button may be below the fold when many additional-columns chips are present, with no sticky CTA or floating action bar.

The onboarding checklist 'map' and 'analysis' steps depend on markOnboardingStep() calls in process map and analysis components, but those calls are not visible in UploadPage or the wizard itself. If any of those components omit the call (e.g., AnalysisPalette may call it, per the grep hit, but it is not confirmed), the checklist will never reach 100% and the celebration state never fires — making the user feel they did something wrong.

maps.summary: The new-user path from CSV to first insight is well-engineered end-to-end. The upload flow (drag-drop → weighted-keyword plus content-based auto-detection → confidence-scored column mapper with live data preview → direct navigation to Mission Control) is clearly the most polished part of the codebase and compares favourably to commercial tools. Mission Control is a strong first-value screen: it never shows a blank canvas, composing insights, automation ROI, SLA burn-down, and an AI narrative from parallel async calls. The demo seeder with five pre-mapped real-world logs (including the full 251 K-case BPIC 2019 dataset) means a self-hosted evaluation can reach insight in under two minutes. The two hardest friction points are: (1) the DataQualityCard is unreachable in the normal upload flow because the navigation to Mission Control bypasses the step that renders it, meaning data quality issues are silently hidden from new users; and (2) the connector 'Test Connection' button requires a prior save, forcing credential commitment before validation. The AI assistant layer is substantive — seven tool-use actions with inline chart rendering, filter proposal, and data-anchored suggestions — but is a silent no-op without a configured API key, with no in-product prompt to set one up.

candidates.title: Data-quality warnings are invisible in the standard upload flow — the worst failure mode for the segment we target
candidates.description: After column mapping, the standard CSV flow navigates straight to /mission-control/:id from handleMappingComplete (UploadPage.tsx line 212), which skips the 'done' step. But DataQualityCard is only rendered inside the step==='done' block (UploadPage.tsx line 466-468, gated behind line 419). So a first-time user uploading a messy CSV with timestamp inversions, null case IDs, or inconsistent activity naming NEVER sees the quality report on the upload path — the most common reason they'd get a wrong process map. This directly undermines our biggest opportunity: open-source/pm4py users hit data-quality blindness as their #1 pain (78% report data quality issues per PMC11646219; 'wrong conclusions because they skip cleaning event logs' per esystems.fi). We built the cure (a real DataQualityCard with severity, affected-row %, and a timestamp-repair tool) and then routed around it.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Open-source segment: 78% of practitioners report data-quality issues as a top challenge (PMC11646219, 41-analyst study); 'many teams run into delays or wrong conclusions because they skip the step of cleaning their event logs' (esystems.fi); CKM Analytix documents timestamp/timezone/DST headaches as a primary cause of bad results. Apromore reviewers also cite 'requires high-quality event logs for the best results' as a con (Nerdisa).

The standard path navigates away at UploadPage.tsx line 212 before 'done' renders.
candidates.recommendation: Surface DataQualityCard on Mission Control (the actual first-value screen) and/or insert a lightweight quality summary banner into the mapping confirmation before navigating away. At minimum, show a non-blocking toast/inline strip on Mission Control when the quality score is Fair/Poor with a one-click jump to the repair tool. This turns a hidden asset into a visible, on-by-default differentiator vs pm4py/Disco/Apromore-CE.
