candidates.title: No write-back / close-the-loop to source systems (the EMS / Action Flows gap)
candidates.description: Celonis's single most-cited differentiator is the insight-to-action loop: detect a deviation, then automatically remediate by creating a ticket, updating a record, or triggering RPA in the SOURCE system (SAP/ServiceNow/Salesforce). FlowMiner's action engine (backend/app/services/action_engine.py) has real dispatch for notify_email, notify_webhook, notify_slack, tag_case, create_task (internal FlowMiner task), escalate, and notify_in_app — all of which keep the user inside FlowMiner or send a generic webhook. There is NO action_type that writes back to a connected system (e.g. create a Jira issue, open a ServiceNow incident, post to a SAP transaction). Verified via grep: no jira/servicenow create-issue or update-record paths exist in action_engine.py. So a 'create_task' from an action rule lands in FlowMiner's own task table, not the system where work actually happens. This is exactly the gap practitioners describe across the research ('the story stays on the dashboard, nothing changes'; 'over 2-in-3 process intelligence initiatives under-delivered'). FlowMiner already HAS authenticated connectors to Jira/ServiceNow/Salesforce with httpx fetch logic, so the write path is a natural extension of existing infrastructure, not a greenfield build.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Celonis EMS/Action Flows is the named core differentiator ('detecting deviations and triggering automated remediation') even critics acknowledge; PeerSpot: 'actions should be able to go via email, task, APIs, and ultimately write back to the source; adding RPA capability would greatly enhance Celonis.' Cross-vendor: 'The story stays on the dashboard' (bpm-d); HFS: '2-in-3 process intelligence initiatives led to disappointing results.' Skan.ai sign: tools that 'only analyze historical data and cannot prevent issues in real-time' underperform.
candidates.flowminer_status: Action engine wires 7 action types (notify_email/webhook/slack, tag_case, create_task, escalate, notify_in_app) in backend/app/services/action_engine.py with CRUD + dry_run + cooldown in backend/app/api/action_rules.py and a dispatch-action-rules Celery beat job every 5 min (backend/app/workers/celery_app.py). create_task inserts into FlowMiner's own task store, not the source system. No write-back action exists despite authenticated Jira/ServiceNow/Salesforce connectors already present (backend/app/services/connectors/jira_connector.py, servicenow_connector.py, salesforce_connector.py).
candidates.recommendation: Add source-system write-back action types that reuse the existing connector adapters: action_type 'create_jira_issue', 'create_servicenow_incident', 'salesforce_update_record', each resolving credentials from the project's saved connector. Surface 'where did my action go?' execution history with the external record ID/link. Frame this as the open-source close-the-loop story Celonis charges EMS-tier money for. Start with Jira + ServiceNow (highest ROI, most-requested in research) before RPA/UiPath bridges.

candidates.title: No analytical query language (PQL/expression-language equivalent) — only a thin case-filter DSL
candidates.description: Power analysts repeatedly praise Celonis PQL (expressive, 150+ operators) and QPR's expression language while hating the lock-in and absence of external help. FlowMiner's nearest equivalent is a case-FILTER DSL (backend/app/services/filter_engine.py): a tokenizer + recursive-descent evaluator supporting case.duration/activity/resource/attr comparisons, and/or/contains, and duration literals (3d, 5m). This selects matching case_ids and pushes a filter chip — it cannot compute, aggregate, define new measures over the process graph, do source/target activity calculations, or express anything PQL/expression-language users actually buy these tools for. custom_kpis.py routes 'process-aware' expressions through this same filter evaluator plus arithmetic on a fixed set of base metrics (avg_case_duration, case_count, rework_rate, etc.) — there is no way to author an arbitrary process metric like 'time between activity A and B per resource group.' This is a genuine capability gap, but it is also an OPPORTUNITY: open-source PQL-without-lock-in (or 'ask in plain English, get the metric' via the existing LLM layer) directly answers the #1 PQL complaint ('a code that only Celonis uses, little help on the internet or through AI').
candidates.competitor_evidence: Celonis PQL loved by analysts who master it ('150+ operators... very versatile') but hated: 'a code that only Celonis uses, so there is little help on the internet or through AI'; debugging 'just a character number in a long code.' QPR: 'Custom Expressions (Expression Language, not very intuitive) ... requires almost always some customer support.' Buyers leave Celonis partly to escape 'proprietary PQL lock-in — every analyst hire requires Celonis-specific training.'
candidates.flowminer_status: Case-filter DSL only: backend/app/services/filter_engine.py (tokenizer + recursive-descent, comparison/and/or/contains/duration literals) returning case_ids; exposed via /competitive/filter-expression (backend/app/api/process_analytics.py:961). custom_kpis.py reuses it for filter-DSL KPIs plus arithmetic over ~7 fixed base metrics. Frontend FilterExpressionBar.tsx is a bare text input — no autocomplete, no syntax reference, no error highlighting, warnings shown only after running.
candidates.recommendation: Do NOT build a 150-operator PQL clone. Instead lean into the existing LLM column-mapper/chat infra: a 'define a metric in plain English -> generated pandas/SQL expression you can save as a Custom KPI' flow (the Extraction Copilot pattern, but for metrics). This converts the PQL strength into FlowMiner's advantage (no proprietary language, AI-native) and reuses backend/app/services/ai/. If a textual DSL is kept, add autocomplete + an in-product operator reference + inline error position to FilterExpressionBar to avoid Celonis's exact debugging complaint.

candidates.title: Real-time streaming exists in the backend but is invisible in the product (no live ops dashboard UI)
candidates.description: Practitioners want forward-looking continuous monitoring, not post-mortem batch analysis ('conformance violations surface in review cycles, not beforehand'). FlowMiner actually HAS a real-time streaming layer that the capability map did not flag: backend/app/api/streaming.py implements authenticated WebSocket live event ingestion + Redis-backed live KPI broadcasting (total_events, active_cases, unique_activities), registered at /api/v1/streaming in main.py:172. But there is no corresponding frontend live-operations dashboard surfaced in the sidebar or palette, and there is no live conformance/SLA-breach alerting wired on top of the stream — alerts run on a 5-min batch beat job against the stored log, not the live stream. So the differentiating capability (live process monitoring, which Microsoft and Disco lack entirely and which is a known open-source gap) is built but completely unsurfaced. This is primarily a wiring/surfacing problem, not a build-from-scratch problem.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Skan.ai sign #5: tools that 'only analyze historical data; cannot prevent issues in real-time' underperform. Open-source gap: 'PM4Py has a streaming module but it is library-only with no UI ... practitioners doing batch-only analysis even when their use case requires continuous monitoring.' Disco/Microsoft offer no streaming. Celonis real-time analysis rated highly (8.7) is a paid strength.
candidates.flowminer_status: Real, registered streaming backend: backend/app/api/streaming.py (WebSocket ingest + Redis live KPIs, JWT-via-query auth, in-process fallback), mounted in backend/app/main.py:172. Alerts (backend/app/services/alert_engine.py) and action rules run on 5-min Celery beat batch jobs against the stored log, not the live stream. No frontend live-ops dashboard is reachable from Sidebar.tsx or the palette.
candidates.recommendation: Build a Live Operations page (sidebar-visible) that subscribes to the existing WebSocket KPI stream and shows active cases, throughput, and live SLA-breach counts. Wire alert/action-rule evaluation to fire on the live stream (not just the nightly/5-min batch) for at-risk cases. This turns a hidden backend asset into a marketable 'real-time process monitoring, self-hosted' differentiator competitors gate behind enterprise tiers.

candidates.title: No external / industry benchmarking — buyers cannot answer 'are we good vs peers?'
candidates.description: SAP Signavio Process Insights' fastest-time-to-value selling point is out-of-the-box KPIs and peer/best-practice BENCHMARKS for P2P/O2C/R2R; Celonis benchmarking is a cited strength. FlowMiner's only benchmarking is a differential-privacy CROSS-TEAM comparison among the user's OWN event logs (backend/app/api/scorecards.py:199 /dp-benchmark, Laplace-noise on avg case duration + case count across the caller's own logs). There is no external/industry baseline, no process-maturity assessment, and no 'your O2C cycle time vs benchmark' framing. For a buyer evaluating FlowMiner against Signavio's 'establish a baseline within weeks' pitch, FlowMiner has nothing to anchor 'is this number good?' — it shows the number but not whether it is healthy relative to anything external.
candidates.competitor_evidence: SAP Signavio Process Insights: 'out-of-the-box KPIs and benchmarks for P2P, O2C, R2R — organizations can establish a baseline within weeks.' Celonis benchmarking is a strength. Gartner Signavio dislike: 'limited drill-down in company benchmarking.' Apromore review: users 'desire pre-built analysis templates for common use cases.' Conversely, hardcoded SAP-best-practice benchmarks are HATED when processes have evolved ('most assumptions and insights are invalid') — so opinionated-but-overridable benchmarks are the safe path.
candidates.flowminer_status: Only cross-team DP benchmark exists: backend/app/api/scorecards.py:199 (/scorecards/dp-benchmark) compares the caller's own event logs with Laplace noise; no external/industry baseline, no maturity scoring. Process templates API (backend/app/api/templates.py) stores reference_model + expected_activities + KPIs + anti_patterns per template but is not used to benchmark a log against an industry standard.
candidates.recommendation: Reuse the existing ProcessTemplate model (reference_model + kpis + anti_patterns) to ship a small set of overridable reference benchmarks for the verticals already covered by recipes (P2P, O2C, incident, returns). On a log mapped to a recipe, show 'your metric vs reference range' with a clear 'edit/override these targets' affordance to avoid Signavio's evolved-process trap. Avoid claiming proprietary peer data you don't have.

candidates.title: Templates/recipes exist but are undiscoverable and narrow (the 'pre-built content pack' gap)
candidates.description: Across every competitor segment, users ask for pre-built industry templates / app packs and praise tools that ship them (UiPath P2P/O2C app templates, Signavio best-practice content, Apromore vertical recipes). FlowMiner HAS this layer: 9 log-builder recipes (backend/app/services/recipes/: sap_p2p, servicenow_incident, salesforce_opportunity, 3 ecommerce, 3 logistics) wired through log_builder_recipes.py (each carrying joins, fixed-activity map, additional_columns, default KPIs and alert rules), plus a ProcessTemplate model. The gap is breadth and discoverability, not existence: the recipe set is e-commerce/logistics-heavy and thin on the highest-value enterprise processes (no O2C, no AP/AR, no HR-to-retire, only one SAP recipe), and recipes/templates are buried in the Log Builder rather than presented as a browsable 'start from a process pack' gallery on the empty-state/home. A new evaluator lands on a blank project with no obvious 'pick your process' path despite the content existing.
candidates.competitor_evidence: UiPath app templates (P2P, O2C) praised though 'rigid.' Apromore: enterprise vertical recipes for banking/insurance/healthcare; community users 'must build everything from scratch.' Open-source gap: 'No open-source tool offers pre-built industry templates.' General: 'without a clear understanding of which processes to focus on, effort becomes scattered'; users 'desire pre-built analysis templates for common use cases.'
candidates.flowminer_status: 9 recipes in backend/app/services/recipes/ + loader backend/app/services/log_builder_recipes.py (joins, fixed-activity map, default KPIs/alerts); ProcessTemplate model + backend/app/api/templates.py CRUD/seed; OnboardingWizard.tsx surfaces packs 'if the backend recipe endpoint responds.' Coverage skews e-commerce/logistics; only one SAP recipe, no O2C/AP/AR/HR. Recipes are reached mainly via the Log Builder, not a prominent gallery.
candidates.recommendation: Promote recipes/templates to a first-class 'Start from a process pack' gallery on the project empty-state and home (not buried in Log Builder), and broaden coverage to the enterprise processes buyers actually evaluate on: O2C, AP/AR, HR onboarding-to-offboarding, a second SAP pack. Each pack should drop in its KPIs, alerts, and (per the benchmarking item) reference targets so time-to-first-insight collapses to minutes.

candidates.title: Collaboration is limited to activity/edge annotations — no shareable narratives, no @mentions, no stakeholder-ready report builder
candidates.description: Buyers leaving Disco cite 'no collaboration, no team sharing'; Apromore is praised for collaboration; the cross-vendor research repeatedly flags 'insights span multiple functions, nobody acts' and 'sharing insights outside the platform requires cumbersome export.' FlowMiner has a genuine but shallow collaboration primitive: threaded annotations pinned to an activity or edge with assign/resolve/reply (backend/app/api/annotations.py + models/annotation.py). What's missing is the layer above it: there are no @mentions/notifications to pull a colleague in, no shareable 'finding' or narrative object that bundles a chart + comment + recommended action for a stakeholder, and dashboard sharing is the only cross-stakeholder surface (public share token). So an analyst can leave a note on a node, but cannot easily hand a COO a stakeholder-ready, self-explaining view — the exact 'translation problem' the research names ('generic views rather than stakeholder-specific configurations').
candidates.competitor_evidence: Disco hated for 'no cloud, no collaboration, no team sharing — desktop-only siloes analysts.' Apromore praised for 'cross-department collaboration without email file transfers.' Cross-vendor: 'insights that span multiple functions fall into a gap between teams ... none taking responsibility'; Skan.ai sign #4: tools deliver 'generic views rather than stakeholder-specific configurations' creating a 'translation problem.'
candidates.flowminer_status: Threaded annotations on activities/edges with reply/resolve/assignee: backend/app/api/annotations.py, backend/app/models/annotation.py (parent_id threading, resolved/assignee fields). Dashboards (backend/app/api/dashboards.py) support public share tokens. No @mention or notification on annotation/assign, no shareable finding/narrative object, no stakeholder-specific report assembly beyond dashboards.
candidates.recommendation: Layer on top of the existing annotation + dashboard infra: (1) @mention with an in-app/email notification when assigned or mentioned (notify channels already exist in alert_engine); (2) a 'shareable finding' object that captures a chart + the AI summary + recommended action and produces a clean stakeholder link/PDF. This closes the multi-function ownership gap without rebuilding collaboration from scratch.

candidates.title: No native task mining / desktop capture beyond an n-gram pattern counter and a bare capture agent
candidates.description: Task mining (desktop/UI event capture) is a named differentiator for Microsoft (bundled Process Advisor), UiPath, and Skan.ai (zero-backend desktop observation), and a cited Celonis weakness. FlowMiner has the skeleton: a capture agent script (tools/capture_agent/agent.py) and an ingest API (backend/app/api/task_mining.py), but the pattern miner (backend/app/services/task_mining.py) is just a windowed n-gram counter (3-8 grams, min_frequency=3) with a simple automatable_score heuristic — no suffix-array/sequence mining, no UI-element-level granularity, no screenshot/OCR, no managed agent rollout. For the buyer segments that pick a tool BECAUSE of task mining (RPA-adjacent, automation-discovery), FlowMiner's offering is a prototype, not a competitive capability. Given the deep desktop-agent governance overhead (HR/works-council buy-in is itself a cited adoption barrier), this is a deliberately-scope-or-defer decision rather than an obvious build.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Microsoft task mining is a 'differentiated bundled capability'; UiPath/Microsoft 'have better task mining than Celonis.' Skan.ai's zero-integration desktop observation is 'the only MQ vendor not requiring backend system connectors.' But desktop agents carry 'HR/privacy governance overhead' and 'significant organizational buy-in' — a real adoption cost.
candidates.flowminer_status: Recording ingest API complete (backend/app/api/task_mining.py); capture agent exists (tools/capture_agent/agent.py); pattern miner is a windowed n-gram counter with a simple automatable_score (backend/app/services/task_mining.py) — no advanced sequence mining, no UI-element granularity, no OCR/screenshots, no managed deployment. Frontend Task Mining page exists but is not in the sidebar.
candidates.recommendation: Do not invest heavily here unless RPA-adjacency becomes a target segment — the governance overhead and depth required (UI-element capture, OCR, managed agent) make it XL with uncertain payoff for a self-hosted OSS tool. If pursued, position as 'privacy-first, self-hosted task mining' (the one angle Microsoft/UiPath SaaS cannot match) rather than competing on feature depth.

candidates.title: No mobile/native experience and known mobile-web clipping — KPI-on-the-go is a competitor gap FlowMiner also has
candidates.description: IBM Process Mining is dinged for 'lack of a functional mobile app' and 'business users who want to monitor KPIs on mobile have no native option.' FlowMiner is responsive web only, and the UX map documents real mobile defects: canvas pages use h-[calc(100vh-7rem)] which clips/resizes with mobile browser address bars (ProcessViewPage/SimulationPage/SocialNetworkPage), and the densest surfaces (ProcessView toolbar, AnalysisHub list) degrade poorly on small screens. There is no lightweight mobile-friendly KPI/alert view for an executive who just wants to glance at process health or respond to an alert. This is a low-severity attract/retain gap (process mining is desk-heavy), but a clean mobile KPI/alert digest would differentiate against the desktop-only incumbents and complement the existing alert/scorecard infra.
candidates.competitor_evidence: IBM Process Mining: 'Lack of a functional mobile app compared to competitors ... business users who want to monitor KPIs on mobile have no native option.' Disco: 'desktop-only means no responsive/mobile access.' Mobile/glanceable health is a recurring small ask for executive stakeholders.
candidates.flowminer_status: Responsive web only; documented mobile issues in the UX map: h-[calc(100vh-7rem)] clipping on iOS Safari/Chrome Android (frontend/src/pages/ProcessViewPage.tsx:426, SimulationPage.tsx:107, SocialNetworkPage.tsx:297); dense ProcessView toolbar and AnalysisHub list degrade on small screens. Alerts/scorecards exist server-side but no mobile-optimized KPI/alert digest view.
candidates.recommendation: Skip a native app. Instead ship one mobile-optimized read-only 'Process Health / My Alerts' route (executive glance + acknowledge-alert) built on existing alert + Overview/Mission-Control data, and fix the calc(100vh-7rem) clipping with dynamic viewport units (100dvh). Low cost, addresses the exact IBM complaint without a mobile codebase.

candidates.title: AI chat tool coverage is narrow — no case drill-down, simulation, social-network, or predictive tools
candidates.description: The AI assistant is one of FlowMiner's strongest differentiators against PQL-bound and consultant-dependent competitors, but its agentic tool catalogue is only 7 tools (show_bottlenecks, show_rework, show_variants, show_events_over_time, get_summary, show_conformance, propose_filters — backend/app/services/ai/chat_tools.py). It cannot answer the most natural follow-ups a business user asks: 'show me the 5 slowest cases' (no case-level drill-down tool), 'what if I add a clerk to approvals' (no simulation tool, despite a full DES backend), 'who hands off to whom' (no SNA tool, despite a Rust-accelerated handover network), or 'which open cases will breach SLA' (no predictive/alarm tool, despite a complete predictive service). The deep analytical backend is largely unreachable through the conversational surface that non-technical users actually use — which undercuts the 'self-service without PQL or consultants' positioning that is FlowMiner's biggest opening against Celonis/Signavio.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Celonis Process Copilot praised for NL querying but limited ('only access to most common activities and variants,' 'degrades on messy data models'). Microsoft Copilot 'only has access to the most common activities and variants.' The recurring buyer demand is 'self-service analytics without PQL or data engineering skill' / 'true no-code analysis' — exactly where a broad AI tool catalogue wins.
candidates.flowminer_status: 7 chat tools in backend/app/services/ai/chat_tools.py (CHAT_TOOL_SCHEMAS): bottlenecks, rework, variants, events-over-time, summary, conformance, propose_filters. Underlying backends exist but are unexposed to chat: predictive (backend/app/services/predictive.py: alarm scoring, remaining-time, outcome), simulation (backend/app/services/simulation_des.py), SNA (backend/app/services/mining/org_mining.py), root cause (backend/app/services/root_cause.py). Two parallel chat UIs (FloatingAIChat + AskAI) share this same thin catalogue.
candidates.recommendation: Expand the chat tool catalogue to expose the analytics that already exist: a case drill-down tool ('slowest/at-risk cases'), a cases-at-risk/SLA-breach tool wrapping predictive alarm scoring, a root-cause tool, and an SNA/handover tool. Each tool reuses an existing service and returns the data/render/summary triple the framework already supports. This is the highest-leverage way to convert FlowMiner's deep backend into the no-PQL, no-consultant self-service experience competitors charge enterprise money for.

candidates.title: No guided 'which analysis / what question' methodology — analysts hit the blank-canvas problem the research names as the hardest unsolved challenge
candidates.description: The cross-vendor practitioner research ranks question formulation / scope selection as the single hardest and least-solved challenge (89% affected, 54% solvability), and 'guided, opinionated methodology for scope selection' is an explicitly requested missing capability. FlowMiner is feature-rich (45+ pages, 17 analyses) but offers no guided path from 'I have data' to 'here is the question worth asking and the analysis that answers it.' Mission Control gives a strong first-value screen and the AnalysisHub stars 'recommended' analyses, but there is no structured methodology wizard ('what outcome do you care about - cost / SLA / compliance / rework? -> here are the 3 analyses + the metric to watch'). For a self-serving mid-market/SMB user without a Celonis-style CoE, this absence means the rich feature set becomes analysis paralysis (a named failure mode: 'buried in dashboards, but nothing changes' / 'abandonment of the project'). This compounds the discoverability problem the UX map already flags (26 of 44 pages not in the sidebar).
candidates.competitor_evidence: Practitioner survey: Question Formulation affected 89% with lowest solvability (54%); 'practitioners want structured 12-step project guidance.' Mavim: 'analysis paralysis can lead to ... abandonment of the project.' Missing capability called out: 'guided, opinionated methodology for scope selection and project setup.' Celonis requires a CoE precisely because the tool does not self-guide.
candidates.flowminer_status: Mission Control (frontend/src/pages/MissionControlPage.tsx) composes a strong first-value screen (KPIs, AI briefing, SLA burn-down, priority feed). AnalysisHub stars 'recommended' analyses and locks unavailable ones with reasons. OnboardingWizard is a 3-step checklist (add data / discover / run analysis). But there is no outcome-driven methodology wizard mapping a business goal to the right analyses + metrics; 26 of 44 pages are not reachable from Sidebar.tsx.
candidates.recommendation: Add an outcome-first 'What do you want to improve?' chooser (cost / cycle time / SLA compliance / rework / capacity) that routes to a curated 2-3 analysis sequence with the metric to watch and a one-line interpretation, reusing the AnalysisHub recommendation logic and the AI narrative. This is the self-serve substitute for a Celonis CoE and directly attacks the #1 practitioner failure mode for the SMB/mid-market segment FlowMiner is positioned to win.

candidates.title: Strong positioning exists in docs but is invisible inside the product
candidates.description: FlowMiner has a genuinely excellent positioning document (docs/why-flowminer.md) — honest comparison table vs Celonis/Apromore CE/Disco/pm4py, the 'depth of Celonis, self-host freedom, no AGPL trap / no open-core paywall / no six-figure contract' line, and a credible 'where FlowMiner is NOT the answer' section. But none of it is reachable in-product. There is no /why, /compare, or /pricing route in App.tsx; the LoginPage and RegisterPage carry only generic 'Open-source process mining, MIT licensed — no lock-in' copy. A frustrated Celonis/Apromore evaluator who installs FlowMiner never encounters the argument for why it solves their specific pain (price shock, consultant dependency, open-core wall). The single best positioning asset in the repo is doing zero conversion work because it lives in a markdown file most evaluators will never open.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Celonis switchers cite price-shock ($286K median, $200K+/business unit) and CoE/consultant dependency as the top leave-drivers; Apromore switchers are stranded by the archived open-core repo; Disco loyalists want simplicity. The whole research corpus is a list of pains that why-flowminer.md already answers — the answer just isn't surfaced where buyers decide.
candidates.flowminer_status: docs/why-flowminer.md (full comparison + honest caveats) and SUPPORT.md (commercial-support story) exist and are high quality. README.md links to why-flowminer.md. But grep of frontend/src/App.tsx shows no /why|/compare|/pricing route, and LoginPage.tsx/RegisterPage.tsx contain only generic one-liner positioning. The doc is not surfaced in-product anywhere.
candidates.recommendation: Add an in-product, lazy-loaded /why (or /compare) page that renders the why-flowminer.md argument as a polished comparison view, linked from the LoginPage, the empty-project state, and a sidebar 'Why FlowMiner' / 'Compare' entry. Mirror it on a public marketing route so it is the first thing a Celonis/Apromore searcher hits. The content is already written — this is surfacing, not authoring.

candidates.title: No migration path from competitor exports (Disco .dsc, Celonis, Apromore) — the switching-cost lever is unaddressed
candidates.description: Switching cost is the single most-repeated reason buyers STAY on an incumbent (sunk pipelines, dashboards, trained CoE). FlowMiner's strongest GTM moment is the Apromore community-edition exodus (ApromoreCore archived Aug 2025, ApromoreDocker Sept 2025 — those users are actively stranded and shopping) and Disco users who want a server tool. Yet there is no importer for any competitor's native format: no Disco .dsc handler, no Celonis/Signavio export adapter, no Apromore project importer in backend/app/services/connectors/. A stranded Apromore CE user or a Disco shop has to re-do their column mapping and rebuild from raw CSV, which feels exactly like the migration pain the research says blocks switches. FlowMiner already advertises 'leaving is always cheap' for its OWN data (JSON export by SHA-256) but offers no cheap way IN from a competitor.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Apromore's own migration press release warns of 'rebuilding dashboards, connectors, filters when switching' as a major switching cost — now ironically applicable to stranded Apromore CE users post-Salesforce. Disco exports XES/MXML only ('closed data'); Disco users 'graduate' when they need conformance/collaboration. Research: 'organizations stay due to sunk-cost investment in pipelines.'
candidates.flowminer_status: ls of backend/app/services/connectors/ shows CSV, XES, OCEL, SAP, SaaS connectors but NO Disco/.dsc, Celonis, or Apromore importers. XES import exists (xes_connector.py) which partially covers Disco/ProM export, but there is no first-class 'Migrate from X' flow, no Disco .dsc parser, and no mapping-preservation. why-flowminer.md sells cheap EXIT (project export) but says nothing about cheap ENTRY from a competitor.
candidates.recommendation: Build a 'Switch to FlowMiner' import flow: (1) a Disco .dsc / XES importer that auto-carries the column mapping (FlowMiner already auto-detects, so this is mostly UX framing + a .dsc parser), (2) a documented Apromore-CE / Celonis CSV-export recipe in the Log Builder. Then position it loudly: 'Stranded on Apromore Community? Import your logs in 60 seconds.' This converts an externally-created wave of displaced users.

candidates.title: No public hosted demo or 'try without installing' path — highest-friction top-of-funnel for a self-host tool
candidates.description: FlowMiner has a genuinely excellent demo seeder (5 pre-mapped real logs incl. the full 251K-case BPIC2019, idempotent, OCEL warm-loading, DEMO_MODE gating, demo-guard middleware) — but it is only reachable by someone who already cloned the repo and ran docker compose. There is no public hosted demo URL, and the README has no 'try it online' link (grep found none). For a self-hostable tool competing against SaaS incumbents that offer instant cloud trials, requiring 'clone + make init-env + make up' before a buyer sees a single process map is the biggest top-of-funnel leak. The asset to remove this friction is already built; the distribution of it is missing.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Research repeatedly faults incumbents for the OPPOSITE failure (Celonis/Signavio/Apromore: 'no instant trial with real data... multiple sales calls before any access'). ProcessMind/Mindzie win specifically on 'instant onboarding, no consultant.' Disco wins on 'value virtually immediately after downloading.' A frictionless demo is table stakes that FlowMiner can beat incumbents on but currently doesn't expose.
candidates.flowminer_status: backend/app/services/demo_seeder.py is full (5 DEMO_PROJECTS pre-mapped, hourly re-seed, OCEL warm-load) and demo_guard.py middleware exists — DEMO_MODE is production-ready. But README.md has no hosted-demo link; grep for demo.flowminer/app.flowminer/try-online found nothing. The capability exists; there is no public deployment of it referenced anywhere.
candidates.recommendation: Stand up a public read-only DEMO_MODE instance at a stable URL and make 'Try the live demo (no install)' the first CTA in the README and on the /why page. This is mostly ops (deploy the already-built demo mode behind the existing Dokploy/Traefik topology) plus one README line — disproportionate funnel impact for low effort.

candidates.title: Trust-proof trifecta is absent: no tagged releases, no public roadmap link, no reference/credibility signals
candidates.description: Risk-averse buyers (the exact ones leaving Celonis/Apromore over vendor-stability fear) need proof a tool is real and maintained. FlowMiner has a CHANGELOG.md but ZERO git tags (git tag returns empty) — so there is no versioned release a buyer can pin to, no '1.0', no release cadence to demonstrate momentum. The README honestly says 'pre-1.0, UI still evolving,' which is good honesty but, combined with no releases and no public proof points, reads as 'unproven' to a procurement team. Apromore's thin independent review base is explicitly called out as a trust failure ('enterprises can't find peer proof'); FlowMiner currently has even less external signal. There is no SBOM, no public security advisory history, and no reference deployments.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Apromore hated point: '0 reviews on PeerSpot/Capterra/Slashdot — this thinness itself is a trust signal, enterprises can't find peer proof.' Gartner MQ Leader status repeatedly cited as 'procurement cover.' ARIS/Apromore buyers actively fleeing over 'vendor stability / roadmap continuity' fears. Buyers need a credibility anchor FlowMiner does not yet provide.
candidates.flowminer_status: CHANGELOG.md exists but git tag is empty (no tagged releases). SECURITY.md exists (72h ack, coordinated disclosure). SUPPORT.md describes governance + roadmap in docs/roadmap/. No SBOM, no public reference customers, no analyst presence, no review-site listing. README status badge says 'pre-1.0' with no release link.
candidates.recommendation: Cut tagged, semver releases with a maintained CHANGELOG (immediate, S); publish an SBOM and a one-page architecture/security overview; cultivate 2-3 named or anonymized reference deployments and a handful of independent reviews (G2/SourceForge/AlternativeTo). For an open-source tool the GitHub equivalent of MQ-cover is stars + release cadence + visible CI/test-pass badges — make the passing test suite and Rust-accel benchmarks visible as trust proof.

candidates.title: Cost-savings / ROI value-realization layer is built but silent at the positioning level
candidates.description: The single most damaging incumbent critique is 'over 2-in-3 process intelligence initiatives under-delivered' and 'the story stays on the dashboard, nothing changes' (insight-to-action gap). FlowMiner has actually built the answer — Initiatives/ROI tracker with baseline+target+/measure recompute, a value-calculator library, scorecards with cost-of-quality FTE-hour quantification, AutomationRoiPage, OverviewPage value cards (realized savings, working capital), Mission Control automation-ROI strip, and action rules that close the loop to Tasks. But the POSITIONING never leads with this. why-flowminer.md sells license/sovereignty/depth; it does not say 'FlowMiner quantifies and tracks the dollar value you realize, so you don't end up in the 2/3 that fail.' The strongest counter-positioning against the industry's worst pain is buried as a feature rather than led as a message.

Baseline → action → measured savings, all in the open product'). Lead the /why page and Mission Control empty state with the ROI tracker. candidates.title: No published pricing / packaging model for the commercial-support tier — the exact transparency buyers crave
candidates.description: Across EVERY competitor profile, opaque 'contact sales' pricing is a top hated item, and transparent published pricing is repeatedly named as the thing buyers want (IBM and ProcessMind win partly on transparency alone). A buyer evaluating 'can I get a name to call when this breaks' has no idea if that costs $2K or $200K, so they default to assuming enterprise-scary or, worse, assume there's no real support and rule it out.
candidates.competitor_evidence: Universal hated theme: 'No public rate card' (Celonis 4.1/5 Evaluation-and-Contracting, lowest dim), Apromore/Disco/Signavio all 'contact sales.' candidates.flowminer_status: Product is genuinely free under MIT (LICENSE confirmed). No /pricing page in App.tsx. The placeholder email/org (flowminer.io, github.com/flowminer/flowminer) also signal pre-launch.
candidates.recommendation: Publish a simple, transparent commercial-support packaging table (e.g. Community free / Supported flat annual / Managed-hosting per-instance) with at least ranges, mirroring the transparency FlowMiner positions against. Even 'starts at $X/year, no per-GB, no per-process, no per-seat data tax' is a wedge against Celonis APC and per-process licensing. candidate.title: Data-quality warnings are invisible in the standard upload flow — the worst failure mode for the segment we target

The standard path navigates away at UploadPage.tsx line 212 before 'done' renders.
candidate.recommendation: Surface DataQualityCard on Mission Control (the actual first-value screen) and/or insert a lightweight quality summary banner into the mapping confirmation before navigating away. At minimum, show a non-blocking toast/inline strip on Mission Control when the quality score is Fair/Poor with a one-click jump to the repair tool. This turns a hidden asset into a visible, on-by-default differentiator vs pm4py/Disco/Apromore-CE.

verdict.title: Data-quality warnings are invisible in the standard CSV upload flow
verdict.original_claim: After column mapping, handleMappingComplete (UploadPage.tsx line 212) navigates straight to /mission-control/:id, skipping the 'done' step. DataQualityCard is only rendered inside step==='done' (lines 419/466-468), so a first-time CSV user uploading a messy log never sees the quality report.
verdict.evidence:
CONFIRMED via code:

1. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/pages/UploadPage.tsx line 212: handleMappingComplete ends with navigate(`/mission-control/${eventLogId}`) — setStep('done') is never called on the standard CSV path. The only setStep('done') call (line 72) is in the OCEL branch, which skips mapping entirely.

2. UploadPage.tsx line 419: DataQualityCard is inside {step === 'done' && (...)} — it only renders at line 466-467 when that gate is true, which is unreachable for CSV uploads.

3. Developer comment at lines 199-201 confirms the bypass is intentional: "take the user straight to the first-value view instead of a dead-end 'done' screen with manual CTAs" — the quality report was collateral damage.

4. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/pages/MissionControlPage.tsx: zero references to DataQualityCard, quality, or any data-quality surface. The landing page after CSV upload shows no quality warnings at all.

5. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/pages/ProcessViewPage.tsx line 573-584: DataQualityCard exists here, behind a qualityOpen toggle button — accessible but not proactively surfaced. Users must know to click "Quality" to see it.
verdict.adjusted: The UX issue is real and the severity is accurately described. The fix has two valid options: (a) On MissionControlPage, auto-fetch quality stats on mount and show a dismissible inline banner or card if severity is 'high' or 'critical' — zero navigation change required; (b) In handleMappingComplete, call setStep('done') instead of navigating, then add a prominent CTA to go to mission-control from the done screen (restoring the quality report as a first-class step). Option (a) is lower risk. ProcessViewPage already has a working toggle-based quality panel as a fallback, but it requires users to discover and click "Quality" — too much friction for first-time users arriving from a messy CSV.

verdict.title: Massive feature surface is undiscoverable: analysis pages absent from sidebar navigation
verdict.original_claim: Of 49 page files (~44 protected routes), only ~18 appear in the sidebar (Sidebar.tsx navSections + ActiveLogNav). The remaining ~26 are reachable only via ⌘K palette or ProjectDetail tool cards. A user who never discovers ⌘K cannot browse most of the product.
verdict.evidence:
Confirmed by reading all four relevant files:

1. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/components/Layout/Sidebar.tsx — navSections contains exactly 18 paths: /overview, /projects, /inbox, /alerts, /action-rules, /dashboards, /benchmark (picker), /initiatives (picker), /kpis, /ocpm, /governance, /capability-map, /connectors, /templates, /admin/usage, /admin/audit, /admin/users, /settings.

3. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/App.tsx — 49 Route path declarations total. Removing login/register/shared/redirect leaves ~46 protected routes. Many are parametric variants of the same page (e.g. /kpis and /kpis/:projectId both count as one feature). Distinct analysis features: ~30 unique analysis destinations beyond admin/utility pages.

4. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/components/ProcessMap/AnalysisPalette.tsx — PALETTE_GROUPS confirms these routes are palette-only (not in sidebar navSections or ActiveLogNav): /animation/:id, /automation-roi/:id, /causal-map/:id, /comparison/:id, /dotted-chart/:id, /drift/:id (only appears on event-log cards in ProjectDetailPage, not sidebar), /health/:id, /lineage/:id, /mission-control/:id (explicitly commented out of sidebar at line 111-115 with "no bare /mission-control route"), /process-city/:id, /pulse/:id, /rework/:id, /root-cause/:id (only in event-log cards), /simulate/:id, /social-network/:id, /sustainability/:id.

5. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/pages/ProjectDetailPage.tsx — tool cards at lines 82-90 expose: Benchmark, Task Mining, KPIs, Journey Maps (analyze group), Log Builder, Scheduled Reports (configure group). Event-log action links at lines 478-487 expose: Process Map, Variants, Bottlenecks, Concept Drift, Conformance, Root Cause (+ OCPM if ocel log). These are per-log-card links, not persistent sidebar entries.

The count is roughly 16 distinct analysis pages that are palette-only or only reachable via ProjectDetail drill-down (not persistently visible in the sidebar from any route): Animation, Automation ROI, Causal Map, Comparison, Dotted Chart, Drift, Process Health, Lineage, Mission Control, Process City, Process Pulse, Rework, Root Cause, Simulate, Social Network, Sustainability. The claim's number (~26) is slightly inflated because it counts parametric siblings (/ocpm and /ocpm/:id) as separate invisible items, but the structural problem is real. The sidebar has a deliberate comment at line 111-115 explicitly excluding Mission Control with a note that "it must be reached from an event-log detail page."
verdict.adjusted:
The UX issue is real and confirmed by code. Approximately 16 distinct analysis pages (Animation Theater, Automation ROI, Causal Map, Comparison, Concept Drift, Dotted Chart, Process Health, Data Lineage, Mission Control, Process City, Process Pulse, Rework, Root Cause, Simulate, Social Network, Sustainability) are reachable exclusively via the ⌘K palette or by drilling into a specific project/event-log card. The sidebar's ⌘K "Search analyses…" button (Sidebar.tsx lines 202-230) and ActiveLogNav's "All analyses" button partially mitigate this — they are persistent and visible — but they are search-first surfaces, not a browsable catalog. A first-time user who does not know what analyses exist has no way to discover them by browsing.

Recommended fix: Add a persistent "Analyses" nav section in Sidebar.tsx with collapsible or paginated groups matching PALETTE_GROUPS, so the full catalog is scannable without knowing what to search for. Alternatively, promote a "Browse all analyses" link in ActiveLogNav that opens a full-page grid (like the AnalysisHub tab in ProcessViewPage) rather than just re-opening ⌘K. The claim's number (~26) overstates by conflating parametric route siblings, but ~16 high-value analysis pages being palette-only is still a material discoverability gap, particularly for the competitive differentiators (Causal Map, Cases at Risk, Automation ROI, Process Health, Drift) that the product strategy relies on.

verdict.evidence:
Confirmed at all three layers:

1. Frontend gate — /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/components/Connectors/ConnectorForm.tsx line 663: `disabled={testStatus === 'testing' || !connector?.id}`. Lines 664-668 show the tooltip "Save the connector first — the test runs against the saved configuration". Lines 684-688 add a secondary explanatory line "Available after the first save — then you can validate connectivity here."

2. Parent no-op handler — /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/pages/ConnectorsPage.tsx lines 169-175: `handleTestNewConnector` is wired as `onTest` on the create-modal ConnectorForm. It does not call the API at all — it fires an info notification telling the user to save first and test later. The `onTest` prop in ConnectorForm (line 300) calls this no-op with the live form state, so even if the disable guard were removed, no real test would occur.

3. Backend architecture confirms the root cause — /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/api/connectors.py lines 281-301: `POST /{connector_id}/test` fetches the connector row by ID from the DB, decrypts `connector.config` from stored state, and passes that to `service.test_connection()`. There is no endpoint accepting raw config from form state. A connector_id is mandatory — the endpoint structurally cannot be called before a record exists.
verdict.adjusted: The UX issue is real and fully confirmed at every layer. The save-before-test inversion is not a UI oversight — it is load-bearing: the backend test endpoint is ID-keyed and reads only persisted, encrypted config; there is no "test with raw payload" variant. Fixing this requires a new backend endpoint (e.g. `POST /connectors/test-config` accepting a raw config body) plus decryption of any already-stored secrets client-side or via a partial-save flow. Until that endpoint exists, the frontend gate is the honest choice over a fake success. The strategist's framing is correct: this is the highest-friction moment in the connector wizard and worth prioritizing a speculative-test endpoint that accepts form state directly without persisting it.

candidate.title: No analytical query language (PQL/expression-language equivalent) — only a thin case-filter DSL
candidate.description: Power analysts repeatedly praise Celonis PQL (expressive, 150+ operators) and QPR's expression language while hating the lock-in and absence of external help. FlowMiner's nearest equivalent is a case-FILTER DSL (backend/app/services/filter_engine.py): a tokenizer + recursive-descent evaluator supporting case.duration/activity/resource/attr comparisons, and/or/contains, and duration literals (3d, 5m). This selects matching case_ids and pushes a filter chip — it cannot compute, aggregate, define new measures over the process graph, do source/target activity calculations, or express anything PQL/expression-language users actually buy these tools for. custom_kpis.py routes 'process-aware' expressions through this same filter evaluator plus arithmetic on a fixed set of base metrics (avg_case_duration, case_count, rework_rate, etc.) — there is no way to author an arbitrary process metric like 'time between activity A and B per resource group.' This is a genuine capability gap, but it is also an OPPORTUNITY: open-source PQL-without-lock-in (or 'ask in plain English, get the metric' via the existing LLM layer) directly answers the #1 PQL complaint ('a code that only Celonis uses, little help on the internet or through AI').
candidate.competitor_evidence: Celonis PQL loved by analysts who master it ('150+ operators... very versatile') but hated: 'a code that only Celonis uses, so there is little help on the internet or through AI'; debugging 'just a character number in a long code.' verdict.adjusted: The claim is mostly correct but overstates one point: the frontend is NOT entirely disconnected from the streaming backend — useDashboardCollab.ts wires the dashboard-collaboration WebSocket channel. However, the live KPI stream (/ws/{eventLogId}, /live-kpis/{eventLogId}, /ingest/{eventLogId}) is entirely unwired in the frontend. ProcessPulsePage.tsx looks like the intended live-ops view but explicitly uses only historical data ("No streaming infra required") — it is a simulation, not a live feed. The corrected recommendation: wire ProcessPulsePage (or a new LiveOpsDashboard component) to /api/v1/streaming/ws/{eventLogId} to consume real live_metrics KPIs; add a top-level sidebar entry (currently absent) for real-time monitoring reachable without first navigating into an event-log detail; and replace the 5-min batch alert evaluation with an event-triggered path that calls alert_engine.evaluate_alert on each ingested event payload arriving at the streaming WebSocket — this is a wiring task, not a build-from-scratch task.

candidate.title: No external / industry benchmarking — buyers cannot answer 'are we good vs peers?'
candidate.description: SAP Signavio Process Insights' fastest-time-to-value selling point is out-of-the-box KPIs and peer/best-practice BENCHMARKS for P2P/O2C/R2R; Celonis benchmarking is a cited strength. FlowMiner's only benchmarking is a differential-privacy CROSS-TEAM comparison among the user's OWN event logs (backend/app/api/scorecards.py:199 /dp-benchmark, Laplace-noise on avg case duration + case count across the caller's own logs). There is no external/industry baseline, no process-maturity assessment, and no 'your O2C cycle time vs benchmark' framing. For a buyer evaluating FlowMiner against Signavio's 'establish a baseline within weeks' pitch, FlowMiner has nothing to anchor 'is this number good?' — it shows the number but not whether it is healthy relative to anything external.
candidate.competitor_evidence: SAP Signavio Process Insights: 'out-of-the-box KPIs and benchmarks for P2P, O2C, R2R — organizations can establish a baseline within weeks.' Celonis benchmarking is a strength. Gartner Signavio dislike: 'limited drill-down in company benchmarking.' Apromore review: users 'desire pre-built analysis templates for common use cases.' Conversely, hardcoded SAP-best-practice benchmarks are HATED when processes have evolved ('most assumptions and insights are invalid') — so opinionated-but-overridable benchmarks are the safe path.
candidate.flowminer_status: Only cross-team DP benchmark exists: backend/app/api/scorecards.py:199 (/scorecards/dp-benchmark) compares the caller's own event logs with Laplace noise; no external/industry baseline, no maturity scoring. Process templates API (backend/app/api/templates.py) stores reference_model + expected_activities + KPIs + anti_patterns per template but is not used to benchmark a log against an industry standard.
candidate.recommendation: Reuse the existing ProcessTemplate model (reference_model + kpis + anti_patterns) to ship a small set of overridable reference benchmarks for the verticals already covered by recipes (P2P, O2C, incident, returns). On a log mapped to a recipe, show 'your metric vs reference range' with a clear 'edit/override these targets' affordance to avoid Signavio's evolved-process trap. Avoid claiming proprietary peer data you don't have.

verdict.title: No external / industry benchmarking — buyers cannot answer 'are we good vs peers?'
verdict.original_claim: FlowMiner's only benchmarking is a differential-privacy cross-team comparison among the user's OWN event logs (/scorecards/dp-benchmark). There is no external/industry baseline, no process-maturity assessment, and no 'your O2C cycle time vs benchmark' framing.
verdict.evidence:
Three benchmarking mechanisms confirmed, none of which provide external/industry data:

1. /backend/app/api/analytics.py:163 — POST /benchmark: computes KPIs (avg/median/p95 duration, variants, top-variant share, percentile rank) across the caller's OWN event logs. Percentile rank is computed purely within the caller's selected set — no external reference pool.

2. /backend/app/api/scorecards.py:199 — POST /dp-benchmark: Laplace-noised avg duration + case count, also only across the caller's own logs.

3. /backend/app/api/templates.py:116 — 20+ process templates (O2C, P2P, ITSM, Logistics, Healthcare, Banking, etc.) each carry KPI targets (e.g., O2C avg_cycle_time target: 72 hours, P2P: 168 hours, ITSM MTTR: 8 hours). These targets are hardcoded internal defaults (authored by the FlowMiner team) and are NOT wired into any benchmark comparison endpoint. They are only used for conformance template matching and KPI creation pre-fill in /frontend/src/pages/KpisPage.tsx (users pick a template to pre-fill their own threshold, then set their own values). No endpoint compares a measured log KPI against a template target.

4. /backend/app/api/ai.py:729-750 — _BEST_PRACTICES is a 10-item internal list used for LLM suggestions; not an external dataset.

5. No files found referencing industry_data, industry_avg, peer_kpi, APQC, Gartner, or any external benchmark database across the entire backend/app and frontend/src trees.

The claim that only the DP-benchmark endpoint exists is slightly understated — there is also a non-DP federated benchmark (POST /analytics/benchmark with a full BenchmarkPage.tsx UI) and templates with KPI targets — but the core claim stands: none of these provide external/industry reference data. The template KPI targets (e.g., O2C 72-hour target) are the closest thing to an 'industry baseline', but they are: (a) static developer-authored numbers, (b) not labeled as industry benchmarks in the UI, and (c) not connected to the benchmark comparison flow.
verdict.adjusted: The gap is confirmed but slightly larger than described. FlowMiner has TWO cross-log benchmark features (the non-DP /analytics/benchmark with a full UI page at BenchmarkPage.tsx, plus the DP /scorecards/dp-benchmark) — both compare the user's own logs only. The process templates in /backend/app/api/templates.py contain hardcoded KPI targets for O2C/P2P/ITSM/Healthcare/Logistics processes (authored by the FlowMiner team) that could serve as a lightweight 'industry baseline', but they are currently siloed from the benchmark UI and not surfaced as 'industry standard' comparators. The missing piece: wire template KPI targets into the BenchmarkPage as a 'best-practice reference' row, label them as 'FlowMiner reference target (based on industry practice)', and add a "vs. target" column in the benchmark table. That alone would give buyers the Signavio-style anchoring ('your O2C is 110h vs. the 72h reference target') without requiring a live industry data feed. For a full Celonis-grade offering, a licensed APQC/benchmarking dataset would be needed — that is genuinely absent.

candidate.title: Templates/recipes exist but are undiscoverable and narrow (the 'pre-built content pack' gap)
candidate.description: Across every competitor segment, users ask for pre-built industry templates / app packs and praise tools that ship them (UiPath P2P/O2C app templates, Signavio best-practice content, Apromore vertical recipes). FlowMiner HAS this layer: 9 log-builder recipes (backend/app/services/recipes/: sap_p2p, servicenow_incident, salesforce_opportunity, 3 ecommerce, 3 logistics) wired through log_builder_recipes.py (each carrying joins, fixed-activity map, additional_columns, default KPIs and alert rules), plus a ProcessTemplate model. The gap is breadth and discoverability, not existence: the recipe set is e-commerce/logistics-heavy and thin on the highest-value enterprise processes (no O2C, no AP/AR, no HR-to-retire, only one SAP recipe), and recipes/templates are buried in the Log Builder rather than presented as a browsable 'start from a process pack' gallery on the empty-state/home. A new evaluator lands on a blank project with no obvious 'pick your process' path despite the content existing.
candidate.competitor_evidence: UiPath app templates (P2P, O2C) praised though 'rigid.' Apromore: enterprise vertical recipes for banking/insurance/healthcare; community users 'must build everything from scratch.' Open-source gap: 'No open-source tool offers pre-built industry templates.' General: 'without a clear understanding of which processes to focus on, effort becomes scattered'; users 'desire pre-built analysis templates for common use cases.'
candidate.flowminer_status: 9 recipes in backend/app/services/recipes/ + loader backend/app/services/log_builder_recipes.py (joins, fixed-activity map, default KPIs/alerts); ProcessTemplate model + backend/app/api/templates.py CRUD/seed; OnboardingWizard.tsx surfaces packs 'if the backend recipe endpoint responds.' Coverage skews e-commerce/logistics; only one SAP recipe, no O2C/AP/AR/HR. Recipes are reached mainly via the Log Builder, not a prominent gallery.
candidate.recommendation: Promote recipes/templates to a first-class 'Start from a process pack' gallery on the project empty-state and home (not buried in Log Builder), and broaden coverage to the enterprise processes buyers actually evaluate on: O2C, AP/AR, HR onboarding-to-offboarding, a second SAP pack. Each pack should drop in its KPIs, alerts, and (per the benchmarking item) reference targets so time-to-first-insight collapses to minutes.

verdict.title: Templates/recipes exist but are undiscoverable and narrow (the 'pre-built content pack' gap)
verdict.original_claim: FlowMiner HAS 9 log-builder recipes (sap_p2p, servicenow_incident, salesforce_opportunity, 3 ecommerce, 3 logistics) wired through log_builder_recipes.py, plus a ProcessTemplate model. The gap is breadth and discoverability: skews e-commerce/logistics-heavy, thin on enterprise processes (no O2C, no AP/AR, no HR-to-retire, only one SAP recipe), and recipes are buried in the Log Builder rather than a browsable gallery on the empty-state/home.
verdict.evidence:
CONFIRMED PRESENT — exactly as claimed:
- /backend/app/services/recipes/: 9 JSON files (sap_p2p, servicenow_incident, salesforce_opportunity, ecommerce_order_fulfillment, ecommerce_returns_reverse_logistics, ecommerce_subscription_dunning, logistics_carrier_scorecard, logistics_otif_root_cause, logistics_p2p_three_way_match)
- /backend/app/services/log_builder_recipes.py: full ProcessRecipe schema with joins, events, default_kpis, default_alert_rules, reference_model sidecar persistence
- /backend/app/models/process_template.py + /backend/app/api/templates.py: ProcessTemplate CRUD + /seed (19 built-in templates, not just mirroring recipes — covers O2C, P2P, ITSM, HR Onboarding, Insurance, Patient Journey, Loan Origination, Mortgage, Clinical Trial, Sales Opportunity, etc.) + /install-from-url endpoint
- /frontend/src/pages/TemplatesPage.tsx: a full browsable gallery with category grouping, detail modals, KPI/anti-pattern display — IS in the sidebar nav

CONFIRMED PARTIALLY WEAK:
- 3 system-specific recipes (sap_p2p, salesforce_opportunity, servicenow_incident) have default_kpis=0, default_alert_rules=0 — unlike the 6 ecommerce/logistics recipes which each have 3 KPIs and 2–3 alert rules
- No O2C *recipe* JSON exists (salesforce_opportunity is category 'o2c' but maps Opportunity-to-Close, not billing cycle); ProcessTemplate seed DOES include O2C/AP-adjacent templates but those are conformance models, not ETL packs
- Two parallel template systems exist (log-builder recipes vs ProcessTemplates) with no cross-linking UI

DISCOVERABILITY — CLAIM IS PARTIALLY OVERSTATED:
- OnboardingWizard.tsx (ProjectsPage empty-state, lines 219–252) DOES render recipe cards conditionally on recipes.length > 0, labeled 'Or start from a prebuilt process pack'
- Recipe picker IS visible in EventLogBuilderPage as a labeled section ('Start from a content pack', line 725), not just a buried dropdown — but it appears mid-page after file upload
- TemplatesPage IS in the sidebar (Sidebar.tsx: { label: 'Templates', path: '/templates', icon: BookTemplate }) and shows a gallery — BUT templates require clicking 'Load Built-in Templates' seed button before any appear (empty state on first visit)
- Recipe cards in OnboardingWizard navigate to /projects?new=1 rather than deep-linking to the builder with pack pre-applied — the connection between the wizard discovery and actual recipe use is indirect
verdict.adjusted: The claim's core facts are correct but overstated in two directions. On breadth: the seed template set (19 entries in /backend/app/api/templates.py) already covers O2C, HR, banking, insurance — the real gap is that these are conformance-model templates, not ETL recipes, and the two systems are siloed. The 3 enterprise-system recipes (SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow) lack the default KPI/alert enrichment the ecommerce/logistics recipes have, which is a genuine asymmetry worth fixing. On discoverability: recipes ARE surfaced in the OnboardingWizard empty-state and in TemplatesPage (sidebar nav), so the claim that they are entirely buried is wrong — but two real UX gaps remain: (1) TemplatesPage shows a blank empty-state until an admin manually clicks the seed button; (2) the OnboardingWizard recipe cards link to /projects?new=1 rather than the Log Builder with the pack pre-selected, breaking the 'pick your process' flow. Recommendation: merge the two template surfaces (add a recipe section to TemplatesPage), auto-seed on first visit instead of requiring a manual admin action, and add deep-link CTAs from recipe cards directly into the Log Builder with the pack pre-applied. Add default_kpis/default_alert_rules to sap_p2p, salesforce_opportunity, and servicenow_incident to match the ecommerce/logistics recipe quality.

candidate.title: Collaboration is limited to activity/edge annotations — no shareable narratives, no @mentions, no stakeholder-ready report builder
candidate.description: Buyers leaving Disco cite 'no collaboration, no team sharing'; Apromore is praised for collaboration; the cross-vendor research repeatedly flags 'insights span multiple functions, nobody acts' and 'sharing insights outside the platform requires cumbersome export.' FlowMiner has a genuine but shallow collaboration primitive: threaded annotations pinned to an activity or edge with assign/resolve/reply (backend/app/api/annotations.py + models/annotation.py). What's missing is the layer above it: there are no @mentions/notifications to pull a colleague in, no shareable 'finding' or narrative object that bundles a chart + comment + recommended action for a stakeholder, and dashboard sharing is the only cross-stakeholder surface (public share token). So an analyst can leave a note on a node, but cannot easily hand a COO a stakeholder-ready, self-explaining view — the exact 'translation problem' the research names ('generic views rather than stakeholder-specific configurations').
candidate.competitor_evidence: Disco hated for 'no cloud, no collaboration, no team sharing — desktop-only siloes analysts.' Apromore praised for 'cross-department collaboration without email file transfers.' Cross-vendor: 'insights that span multiple functions fall into a gap between teams ... none taking responsibility'; Skan.ai sign #4: tools deliver 'generic views rather than stakeholder-specific configurations' creating a 'translation problem.'
candidate.flowminer_status: Threaded annotations on activities/edges with reply/resolve/assignee: backend/app/api/annotations.py, backend/app/models/annotation.py (parent_id threading, resolved/assignee fields). Dashboards (backend/app/api/dashboards.py) support public share tokens. No @mention or notification on annotation/assign, no shareable finding/narrative object, no stakeholder-specific report assembly beyond dashboards.
candidate.recommendation: Layer on top of the existing annotation + dashboard infra: (1) @mention with an in-app/email notification when assigned or mentioned (notify channels already exist in alert_engine); (2) a 'shareable finding' object that captures a chart + the AI summary + recommended action and produces a clean stakeholder link/PDF. This closes the multi-function ownership gap without rebuilding collaboration from scratch.

verdict.title: Collaboration: shallow annotation primitive, @mentions are placeholder-only, no shareable finding/narrative object
verdict.original_claim: FlowMiner has genuine but shallow collaboration via threaded annotations on activities/edges with assign/resolve/reply. Missing: @mentions/notifications on assignment, shareable 'finding' or narrative object bundling chart+comment+recommended action for a stakeholder, and dashboard sharing is the only cross-stakeholder surface.
verdict.evidence:
CONFIRMED PRESENT — Annotation primitive: backend/app/models/annotation.py has parent_id (threading), resolved/resolved_by/resolved_at, assignee_id fields. backend/app/api/annotations.py implements POST /annotations, POST /{id}/replies, POST /{id}/resolve, POST /{id}/unresolve, PATCH /{id}/assign, DELETE /{id}. Frontend API client at frontend/src/api/annotations.ts exposes all six operations. CommentThread.tsx renders annotations per activity/edge in the ProcessMap sidebar (ProcessViewPage.tsx line 1320). Dashboard public share confirmed: models/dashboard.py has share_token + is_shared; api/dashboards.py exposes GET /dashboards/shared/{share_token} (no auth); SharedDashboardPage.tsx routes /dashboards/shared/:shareToken.

CONFIRMED ABSENT — @mentions: CommentThread.tsx line 123 has placeholder text 'Add a comment — @mentions supported' but the input is a plain <input type='text'> with no @ parsing, no user-lookup dropdown, no mention extraction in post(). Zero backend handling of mentions in annotations.py or any model. The placeholder is purely cosmetic. Notification on assign: assign_annotation() in annotations.py writes assignee_id but never imports or calls Notifier; notifier.py (services/infra/notifier.py) only routes Alert notifications, not annotation events. Shareable finding/narrative object: no Finding, Narrative, or StakeholderReport model exists anywhere in backend/app/models/ or schemas/. No endpoint bundles chart + annotation + recommended_action into a sharable payload. mining_reports.py has PDF/HTML conformance export; scheduled_reports.py has email-deliverable scheduled reports — neither is a stakeholder-targeted finding narrative. Notification table: action_engine.py comment (line 580) explicitly notes 'there is no separate notifications table.'
verdict.adjusted: The claim is accurate and the status 'present_but_weak' is correct. The annotation layer (threading, resolve, assign) exists end-to-end in backend and frontend. However: (1) @mentions are a UI lie — the placeholder text implies the feature but zero parsing or notification logic exists; this should be called out as a missing feature, not a weak one. (2) No notification fires when an annotation is assigned, making the assignee field functionally inert from a collaboration standpoint. (3) There is no shareable 'finding' object — no model, no endpoint, no UI — that bundles a chart + annotation + recommended action for a stakeholder audience. (4) Dashboard share tokens are the only authenticated-to-public sharing primitive. Worth building in priority order: (a) remove or implement the @mention placeholder (b) fire a notification on annotation assignment (c) add a lightweight Finding model that pins a chart snapshot + annotation + action to a shareable URL separate from dashboards.

candidate.title: No native task mining / desktop capture beyond an n-gram pattern counter and a bare capture agent
candidate.description: Task mining (desktop/UI event capture) is a named differentiator for Microsoft (bundled Process Advisor), UiPath, and Skan.ai (zero-backend desktop observation), and a cited Celonis weakness. FlowMiner has the skeleton: a capture agent script (tools/capture_agent/agent.py) and an ingest API (backend/app/api/task_mining.py), but the pattern miner (backend/app/services/task_mining.py) is just a windowed n-gram counter (3-8 grams, min_frequency=3) with a simple automatable_score heuristic — no suffix-array/sequence mining, no UI-element-level granularity, no screenshot/OCR, no managed agent rollout. For the buyer segments that pick a tool BECAUSE of task mining (RPA-adjacent, automation-discovery), FlowMiner's offering is a prototype, not a competitive capability. Given the deep desktop-agent governance overhead (HR/works-council buy-in is itself a cited adoption barrier), this is a deliberately-scope-or-defer decision rather than an obvious build.
candidate.competitor_evidence: Microsoft task mining is a 'differentiated bundled capability'; UiPath/Microsoft 'have better task mining than Celonis.' Skan.ai's zero-integration desktop observation is 'the only MQ vendor not requiring backend system connectors.' But desktop agents carry 'HR/privacy governance overhead' and 'significant organizational buy-in' — a real adoption cost.
candidate.flowminer_status: Recording ingest API complete (backend/app/api/task_mining.py); capture agent exists (tools/capture_agent/agent.py); pattern miner is a windowed n-gram counter with a simple automatable_score (backend/app/services/task_mining.py) — no advanced sequence mining, no UI-element granularity, no OCR/screenshots, no managed deployment. Frontend Task Mining page exists but is not in the sidebar.
candidate.recommendation: Do not invest heavily here unless RPA-adjacency becomes a target segment — the governance overhead and depth required (UI-element capture, OCR, managed agent) make it XL with uncertain payoff for a self-hosted OSS tool. If pursued, position as 'privacy-first, self-hosted task mining' (the one angle Microsoft/UiPath SaaS cannot match) rather than competing on feature depth.

verdict.title: Task Mining: Present but weak — cross-link differentiator omitted from claim
verdict.original_claim: Task mining is a skeleton: capture agent + ingest API + a windowed n-gram pattern counter with a simple automatable_score heuristic — no suffix-array/sequence mining, no UI-element granularity, no screenshot/OCR, no managed agent rollout. Frontend Task Mining page exists but is not in the sidebar.
verdict.evidence: Pattern miner confirmed as windowed n-gram counter (3-8 grams, min_frequency=3) at /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/services/task_mining.py lines 34-151; the file itself labels it "intentionally simple" and names suffix-array counting as the upgrade path (line 10). Capture agent at /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/tools/capture_agent/agent.py only polls active window titles via pygetwindow/AppKit/ewmh/xdotool — no UI-element capture, no screenshots, no OCR. automatable_score heuristic is `1.0 - (len(users) / max(count, 1))` (lines 137-139). No managed rollout infrastructure found anywhere. The cross-link endpoint (POST /task-mining/cross-link) at /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/api/task_mining.py lines 287-425 — which the claim entirely omits — joins task patterns to process activities via SequenceMatcher and is fully wired in the frontend at /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/pages/TaskMiningPage.tsx and /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/api/taskMining.ts. Task Mining page is NOT in the global Sidebar.tsx navSections (confirmed by reading the full file), but IS reachable from ProjectDetailPage.tsx line 83 as a project-level card link. The TaskEvent model at /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/models/task_mining.py has url, window_title, application, and a JSON details blob — structurally ready for richer capture — but the agent only populates window_title/application today.
verdict.adjusted: The claim is substantially correct on the miner's limitations (n-gram only, no OCR/screenshots, no UI-element granularity, no managed rollout) but materially omits the cross-link feature, which is the only genuinely differentiated capability in the stack — it joins desktop task sequences to discovered process activities, a join no competitor currently ships in-product. The sidebar absence claim is technically correct (no entry in navSections) but misleading: the page is reachable from the project detail card. Recommended framing: the task mining stack is a working but shallow prototype whose ceiling is the capture agent (window-title polling only) and a bag-of-ngrams miner. The one asset worth keeping and surfacing is the cross-link endpoint; it should be prominently positioned rather than buried. For a competitive offering, the gaps to close in priority order are: (1) richer capture agent with click/keystroke/URL events (the model already has the fields), (2) suffix-array or PrefixSpan sequence mining for larger datasets, (3) sidebar entry so the feature is discoverable. Managed agent rollout is correctly identified as a deliberate defer given HR/works-council overhead.

candidate.title: No mobile/native experience and known mobile-web clipping — KPI-on-the-go is a competitor gap FlowMiner also has
candidate.description: IBM Process Mining is dinged for 'lack of a functional mobile app' and 'business users who want to monitor KPIs on mobile have no native option.' candidate.competitor_evidence: IBM Process Mining: 'Lack of a functional mobile app compared to competitors ... business users who want to monitor KPIs on mobile have no native option.' candidate.flowminer_status: Responsive web only; documented mobile issues in the UX map: h-[calc(100vh-7rem)] clipping on iOS Safari/Chrome Android (frontend/src/pages/ProcessViewPage.tsx:426, SimulationPage.tsx:107, SocialNetworkPage.tsx:297); dense ProcessView toolbar and AnalysisHub list degrade on small screens. candidate.title: AI chat tool coverage is narrow — no case drill-down, simulation, social-network, or predictive tools
candidate.description: The AI assistant is one of FlowMiner's strongest differentiators against PQL-bound and consultant-dependent competitors, but its agentic tool catalogue is only 7 tools (show_bottlenecks, show_rework, show_variants, show_events_over_time, get_summary, show_conformance, propose_filters — backend/app/services/ai/chat_tools.py). The deep analytical backend is largely unreachable through the conversational surface that non-technical users actually use — which undercuts the 'self-service without PQL or consultants' positioning that is FlowMiner's biggest opening against Celonis/Signavio.
candidate.competitor_evidence: Celonis Process Copilot praised for NL querying but limited ('only access to most common activities and variants,' 'degrades on messy data models'). Microsoft Copilot 'only has access to the most common activities and variants.' FlowMiner has actually built the answer — Initiatives/ROI tracker with baseline+target+/measure recompute, a value-calculator library, scorecards with cost-of-quality FTE-hour quantification, AutomationRoiPage, OverviewPage value cards (realized savings, working capital), Mission Control automation-ROI strip, and action rules that close the loop to Tasks. But the POSITIONING never leads with this. why-flowminer.md sells license/sovereignty/depth; it does not say 'FlowMiner quantifies and tracks the dollar value you realize, so you don't end up in the 2/3 that fail.' The strongest counter-positioning against the industry's worst pain is buried as a feature rather than led as a message.
candidate.competitor_evidence: HFS: 'over 2-in-3 process intelligence initiatives under-delivered.' BPM-d: 'insight generated, acknowledged, then left at observation.' Mavim: 'buried in dashboards, but nothing changes.' Celonis's own pitch is value-realization but Glassdoor calls it 'overhyped value realization story.' This is the open flank — a tool that PROVES realized value wins the argument incumbents keep losing.
candidate.flowminer_status: Built and wired: backend/app/api/initiatives.py (baseline/target/current + /measure live recompute + get_calculators), api/scorecards.py (cost-of-quality FTE quantification), frontend AutomationRoiPage.tsx, OverviewPage.tsx (realized-savings/working-capital cards), MissionControlPage.tsx (automation ROI). Mature feature layer. why-flowminer.md and README features list do NOT lead with value-realization/ROI as a positioning pillar.
candidate.recommendation: Add a value-realization pillar to why-flowminer.md and the README ('Close the loop — track the dollars, not just the diagrams. Baseline → action → measured savings, all in the open product'). Lead the /why page and Mission Control empty state with the ROI tracker. This is messaging on top of shipped capability — pure S-effort leverage against the industry's #1 failure narrative.
