candidate.title: No published pricing / packaging model for the commercial-support tier — the exact transparency buyers crave
candidate.description: Across EVERY competitor profile, opaque 'contact sales' pricing is a top hated item, and transparent published pricing is repeatedly named as the thing buyers want (IBM and ProcessMind win partly on transparency alone). FlowMiner's product is free (MIT), which is a huge advantage — but its commercial offering (priority SLA support, managed hosting, deployment/ERP-extraction help) in SUPPORT.md is itself 'email hello@flowminer.io' with no tiers, no price ranges, no packaging. FlowMiner is reproducing the exact opacity it criticizes incumbents for, on the one thing it does charge for. A buyer evaluating 'can I get a name to call when this breaks' has no idea if that costs $2K or $200K, so they default to assuming enterprise-scary or, worse, assume there's no real support and rule it out.
candidate.competitor_evidence: Universal hated theme: 'No public rate card' (Celonis 4.1/5 Evaluation-and-Contracting, lowest dim), Apromore/Disco/Signavio all 'contact sales.' Buyers explicitly want: 'Published, transparent pricing so buyers can build a business case without a sales call' and 'Flat-rate/per-seat pricing that does not scale with data volume.' IBM/ProcessMind/Mindzie win on transparent published tiers.
candidate.flowminer_status: Product is genuinely free under MIT (LICENSE confirmed). SUPPORT.md lists commercial services (priority SLA, managed hosting, deployment/SAP-extraction help, custom dev) but with NO pricing, NO tiers — just 'email hello@flowminer.io.' No /pricing page in App.tsx. The placeholder email/org (flowminer.io, github.com/flowminer/flowminer) also signal pre-launch.
candidate.recommendation: Publish a simple, transparent commercial-support packaging table (e.g. Community free / Supported flat annual / Managed-hosting per-instance) with at least ranges, mirroring the transparency FlowMiner positions against. Even 'starts at $X/year, no per-GB, no per-process, no per-seat data tax' is a wedge against Celonis APC and per-process licensing. Make 'unlimited processes, unlimited data volume, flat fee' an explicit anti-Celonis pricing message.

verdict.title: No published pricing or packaging for the commercial-support tier
verdict.original_claim: SUPPORT.md lists commercial services (priority SLA, managed hosting, deployment/SAP-extraction help, custom dev) but with NO pricing, NO tiers — just 'email hello@flowminer.io.' No /pricing page in App.tsx. FlowMiner is reproducing the exact opacity it criticizes incumbents for on the one thing it charges for.
verdict.evidence: /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/SUPPORT.md lines 20-34: four commercial service categories listed (priority SLA, managed hosting, deployment/ERP extraction, custom dev), contact method is solely "email hello@flowminer.io" — no pricing, no tiers, no ranges. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/LICENSE: confirms MIT. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/App.tsx: full route tree has no /pricing, /plans, or /commercial route. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/frontend/src/pages/: 47 page files enumerated — none are a pricing page. grep across all non-node_modules .md files finds no FlowMiner-side price figures anywhere. The "tier" hits in frontend source (ProcessCityCanvas.tsx, AutomationRoiPage.tsx, ProcessPulsePage.tsx) are all data-visualization tiers (duration/ROI quantiles), not commercial plan tiers.
verdict.adjusted: Confirmed valid and worth fixing. The gap is real: SUPPORT.md names four service lines but publishes zero pricing signal. The minimum viable fix is adding rough anchoring ranges (e.g. "priority SLA from $X/month", "managed hosting from $Y/month") and named tiers (Community / Pro / Enterprise) directly in SUPPORT.md, so a buyer can self-qualify before emailing. A /pricing page in the app is optional but lower priority — SUPPORT.md is the natural entry point since the product is self-hosted. The irony the strategist flags is legitimate: docs/why-flowminer.md criticizes competitors for "six-figure" opaque pricing, while the one paid offering FlowMiner has is itself opaque. Adding even ballpark ranges resolves the contradiction and removes the "enterprise-scary or no real support" evaluation risk.

candidate.title: No vertical / use-case packaging despite shipped recipes — buyers can't self-identify
candidate.description: Incumbents win SAP shops with P2P/O2C/R2R out-of-the-box benchmarks, and the open-source pain is 'community users must build everything from scratch — no pre-built templates for common processes.' FlowMiner has actually shipped 6 vertical recipes and content-pack recipes (log_builder_recipes.py, demo content packs, the close-the-loop branch's vertical packs), plus prebuilt process packs surfaced in onboarding. But positioning is entirely horizontal: README and why-flowminer.md describe ALGORITHMS (inductive miner, OCEL, conformance) not OUTCOMES (cut P2P maverick spend, hit O2C SLAs, audit four-eyes compliance). A P2P analyst leaving Celonis cannot tell from FlowMiner's positioning that it does their job; they see a generalist toolkit. The vertical recipes exist but the GTM doesn't package them as 'FlowMiner for Procure-to-Pay / Order-to-Cash / IT Service Management.'
candidate.competitor_evidence: Celonis/Signavio loved for out-of-box P2P/O2C/R2R KPIs and 'fastest time-to-value for SAP best-practice benchmarking.' Apromore CE hated: 'community users must build everything from scratch, no pre-built templates.' Open-source missing: 'pre-built industry templates.' Buyers self-identify by process area, not algorithm.
candidate.flowminer_status: Shipped: backend/app/services/log_builder_recipes.py, demo content-pack recipes (per connection-journey memory: 3 process content-pack recipes), close-the-loop branch added 6 vertical recipes, onboarding wizard surfaces prebuilt process packs. The recipes exist. README/why-flowminer.md positioning is algorithm-centric, not vertical/outcome-centric. No 'FlowMiner for P2P/O2C/ITSM' framing anywhere.
candidate.recommendation: Repackage the existing recipes as named vertical solution pages ('FlowMiner for Procure-to-Pay', 'for Order-to-Cash', 'for IT Service Management / Jira', 'for Healthcare pathways via state-aware OCPM'), each with the demo log, the recipe, and the relevant ROI calculator pre-wired. Lead with outcomes. This is packaging shipped capability, so most cost is content + a recipe-gallery page.

candidate.title: Sovereignty / data-residency moat is real and well-argued but not aimed at the named regulated segment that no incumbent can serve
candidate.description: why-flowminer.md section 5 makes the on-prem/sovereign case well and honestly (Fernet-at-rest, local Ollama option, honest pseudonymisation-not-anonymisation framing, RBAC+audit). This is FlowMiner's most defensible moat: EVERY major competitor (Celonis, Signavio, Microsoft, UiPath, IBM-mostly) is cloud-only and structurally CANNOT serve EU banking / healthcare / government / defence. But the positioning is generic ('on-prem and sovereign by default') rather than segment-targeted at the buyers who are STRUCTURALLY DISQUALIFIED from the incumbents. There is no 'For regulated industries' / 'For the public sector' / 'For air-gapped deployments' landing that names GDPR, data-residency, and the Celonis-SAP data-toll risk as the wedge. The strongest moat is pitched as a feature bullet instead of a go-to-market beachhead.
candidate.competitor_evidence: Repeated across all profiles: 'SaaS-only deployment — regulated industries cannot send ERP data to US cloud.' 'CPM not compatible with country cybersecurity policy.' Celonis-SAP antitrust: data-access can become a mid-contract 'toll booth.' Both Microsoft and SAP 'explicitly abandon' the sovereignty/SMB segment. This is an uncontested beachhead.
candidate.flowminer_status: why-flowminer.md section 5 covers it well with honest caveats (pseudonymisation vs anonymisation, RBAC as the real boundary). Backend has privacy.py/anonymizer.py, audit_logs.py, encrypted-at-rest secrets, local-Ollama support. Capability is real. Positioning is a generic section, not a named-segment GTM beachhead; no regulated-industry/public-sector landing or messaging.
candidate.recommendation: Carve a 'For regulated / sovereign deployments' positioning beachhead that names the segment (EU banking, healthcare, public sector, defence), the disqualifier (cloud-only incumbents can't serve you), and the proof (air-gapped, local-LLM, encrypted-at-rest, RBAC+audit, honest privacy framing). This is the wettest, least-contested wedge — make it a primary message, not a section 5 bullet.

candidate.title: 'Cheaper + sovereign' pitch risks reading as 'budget tool' — under-claims the depth that actually beats incumbents
candidate.description: An earlier internal audit found the cheaper+sovereign pitch is INVERTED — the product is deep, but cheap-positioning makes risk-averse enterprise buyers discount it. The research corroborates the danger: open-source tools are dismissed as lacking 'performance, support, polish,' and 'budget' framing pushes you toward the SMB segment where willingness-to-pay is lowest. FlowMiner's true differentiator is that it has Celonis-CLASS depth (OCEL 2.0 + state-aware OCPM, stochastic conformance JSD/EMD, queue mining Erlang-C, causal LiNGAM, DES simulation, predictive+SHAP, Rust acceleration) that NO other open/affordable tool has — pm4py is a library, Disco is discovery-only, Apromore CE is gutted. Surface copy leads with what it COSTS (free/MIT) before what it IS (the only self-hostable tool with enterprise-grade depth). Leading on price anchors low.
candidate.competitor_evidence: Open-source dismissed for 'lack performance, support, advanced features.' Glassdoor (Celonis): 'competitors catching up at a discount' — discount framing invites the 'cheap imitation' read. Buyers leaving Celonis still want DEPTH (variant explorer, conformance, OCPM); they want to NOT overpay, not to downgrade. The winning frame is 'same depth, your terms,' not 'cheaper.'
candidate.flowminer_status: README headline leads with 'depth of Celonis, self-host freedom... without the six-figure contract' — depth-first, which is correct. But LoginPage/RegisterPage and much surface copy lead with 'open-source / MIT / no lock-in' (cost/freedom framing). Capability map confirms the depth is real (stochastic conformance, OCEL+state-aware OCPM, queue/causal/DES/predictive+SHAP, Rust accel). The pitch ordering is partly inverted on the high-traffic surfaces.
candidate.recommendation: Reorder every positioning surface to lead with DEPTH and uniqueness ('The only self-hostable platform with OCEL 2.0 object-centric mining, stochastic conformance, queue mining, causal discovery, and DES simulation — the depth enterprises pay six figures for'), and treat 'free/MIT/sovereign' as the closer, not the headline. Add a one-line proof: 'No other open or affordable tool ships this depth — pm4py is a library, Disco is discovery-only, Apromore CE locks conformance and simulation behind sales.'

candidate.title: AI assistant + MCP server is a category-defining wedge that positioning treats as just another feature
candidate.description: FlowMiner ships a data-grounded AI chat (tool-use, inline chart/filter rendering), an Extraction Copilot that writes the ETL SQL, an LLM column-mapper, and — uniquely — an MCP server so Claude Desktop/Cursor/Zed can query a FlowMiner instance as a tool, provider-agnostic incl. local Ollama. This directly neutralizes TWO of the biggest incumbent pains at once: PQL lock-in ('a proprietary language no AI is trained on, every analyst needs Celonis-specific training') and the ETL/data-prep tax (60-80% of project time). No incumbent offers an open, self-hostable, no-query-language, MCP-native AI layer — Celonis Copilot is cloud-only and degrades on messy Knowledge Models; Microsoft Copilot 'can't do ETL' and only sees common variants. The roadmap even notes the 'first open-source process-mining MCP' blog angle. Yet positioning lists AI as one feature pillar among many rather than as the wedge that makes FlowMiner self-serviceable by a single analyst (no CoE, no PQL).
candidate.competitor_evidence: Celonis: 'PQL only Celonis uses, little help online or via AI'; 'every analyst hire needs Celonis-specific training.' Microsoft Copilot: 'isn't equipped with ETL... only common activities/variants.' Universal: ETL is 60-80% of project time and the #1 frustration. 'No mature open-source web app wraps pm4py for non-coders.' This is a true open-flank.
candidate.flowminer_status: Shipped and mature: backend/app/api/ai.py + services/ai/chat_tools.py (7 tool-use actions, inline charts), mapping_suggester.py (LLM column mapping), ExtractionCopilot, mcp/server.py (8 tools, MCP stdio), llm.py (Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter/DeepSeek/Ollama). why-flowminer.md section 3 uses it well as the anti-PQL/anti-CoE argument. README lists AI as a feature pillar. The MCP / no-query-language angle is under-amplified as the headline wedge.
candidate.recommendation: Elevate 'No query language. No CoE. Ask in plain English, or point your own AI agent at it via MCP' to a top-line message, explicitly contrasted with PQL lock-in. Ship the 'first open-source process-mining MCP server' blog post already in the roadmap as a distribution play to the AI-agent/dev-tool audience (Cursor/Zed/Claude Desktop users), a channel no incumbent is reaching. Pair with the Extraction Copilot as the 'we do the ETL the SI bills you for' message.

2. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/services/ai/chat_tools.py — 7 tool schemas (show_bottlenecks, show_rework, show_variants, show_events_over_time, get_summary, show_conformance, propose_filters) with render envelopes (bar_chart, line_chart, metric_card, conformance_chart, filter_proposal).

3. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/api/ai_tools.py — POST /ai/extract-log (ExtractionCopilot): multi-turn conversational SQL-generation copilot with rationale-before-SQL discipline, ANSI SQL/PostgreSQL scoping, and JSON-structured response with sql/step/confidence fields.

4. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/services/ai/mapping_suggester.py — LLM column mapper (suggest_mapping), forces gpt-4.1-nano for this task, validates LLM output against real columns, back-fills from heuristic.

5. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/mcp/server.py — 9 MCP tools (not 8 as claimed): list_event_logs, get_log_summary, get_bottlenecks, get_variants, get_rework, get_conformance, get_dfg, get_insights, ask_natural_language. stdio mode, FLOWMINER_MCP_USER_EMAIL auth, real mcp SDK import.

6. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/backend/app/services/ai/llm.py — 5 providers: anthropic, openai, openrouter, ollama, null. Tool-use loop for anthropic + openai/openrouter. DeepSeek mentioned only as an OpenRouter-proxied model, not a standalone provider.

7. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/docs/roadmap/ai-phases.md line 121-122 — explicit blog positioning note: "The first open-source process-mining MCP server — ask Claude Desktop about your process in one click."

8. README.md structure: AI appears as one named section ("AI, grounded in your data") among four sections (Process mining, AI, Collaboration, Operational) — coordinated, not foregrounded.

9. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/docs/why-flowminer.md — Section 3 ("No Center of Excellence, no SI engagement, no proprietary query language") does make the anti-PQL/anti-CoE argument and covers all four AI features (auto column-mapping, data-anchored chat, Extraction Copilot, MCP server). However it is section 3 of 6 and framed as a cost/friction argument, not as a category-defining positioning statement or headline wedge.
verdict.adjusted: The UX/positioning issue is real and confirmed by the code. All four AI components the strategist names are shipped and mature. The positioning gap is also real: README lists AI as one of four feature-pillar sections with no special prominence; why-flowminer.md buries the anti-PQL/MCP argument in section 3 under a cost-friction framing rather than leading with it. The roadmap itself knows this is the differentiation story (ai-phases.md line 85-88: "Being first in open source gives us a real moat with developer-tool buyers and with the Ollama / local-LLM crowd that Celonis structurally cannot serve") — but that insight has not propagated to the README or the why-flowminer.md headline. One correction to the claim: DeepSeek is not an independent provider in llm.py; it is accessed only through OpenRouter. The MCP server has 9 tools, not 8. Otherwise the evidence matches. Recommended fix: restructure README to open with the AI/MCP/no-CoE wedge, make why-flowminer.md section 3 the headline section (or move it to section 1 after MIT), and publish the 'first open-source process-mining MCP' blog post the roadmap already wrote the headline for.

candidate.title: Placeholder org/email/URLs and absent distribution signal a pre-launch project, undercutting every trust message
candidate.description: All public touchpoints reference unclaimed placeholders: README clone URL is github.com/<you>/flowminer.git, SUPPORT.md points to github.com/flowminer/flowminer and hello@flowminer.io, SECURITY.md to security@flowminer.io — and there are no git tags, no review-site presence, no demo URL. For a category where buyers are explicitly fleeing vendors over STABILITY and CONTINUITY fears, presenting as an unlaunched repo with placeholder coordinates is self-defeating regardless of how good the code is. There is no distribution surface (no marketing site referenced, no blog despite roadmap blog plans, no review listings) — the product is invisible to the searchers who are right now Googling 'Celonis alternative,' 'Apromore community edition replacement,' 'self-hosted process mining,' and 'open source process mining.' Distribution, not capability, is the binding constraint.
candidate.competitor_evidence: Apromore's fatal trust signal is thin external proof ('0 reviews... enterprises can't find peer proof'). Buyers actively search for alternatives (the research is full of 'Celonis alternatives' / 'Signavio alternatives' comparison articles) — FlowMiner appears in none of them. Switch-driver lists name ProcessMind/Mindzie precisely because they show up in comparison content; FlowMiner doesn't.
candidate.flowminer_status: README.md clone URL is literal '<you>/flowminer.git'; SUPPORT.md/SECURITY.md use flowminer.io + github.com/flowminer/flowminer (ownership unverified); git tag empty; no demo URL referenced; roadmap mentions a planned blog post but none shipped. No evidence of any review-site listing or comparison-article presence. The product is functionally complete but distribution-absent.
candidate.recommendation: Claim the org/domain/handles, replace all placeholder URLs/emails, cut a tagged v0.x release, stand up a minimal docs+demo site, and seed distribution where the buyers search: get listed in 'Celonis/Apromore/Signavio alternative' comparison content and on G2/SourceForge/AlternativeTo, and publish the roadmap's 'first open-source process-mining MCP' and 'stranded on Apromore CE?' posts. Capability is done; the remaining ROI is almost entirely in being findable.

verdict.title: Placeholder org/email/URLs and absent distribution signal a pre-launch project
verdict.original_claim: README clone URL is literal '<you>/flowminer.git'; SUPPORT.md/SECURITY.md use flowminer.io + github.com/flowminer/flowminer (ownership unverified); git tag empty; no demo URL referenced; roadmap mentions a planned blog post but none shipped. No evidence of any review-site listing or comparison-article presence.
verdict.evidence: CONFIRMED REAL: (1) `<you>` placeholder clone URL is literally present at README.md:83, CONTRIBUTING.md:24, and docs/why-flowminer.md:169 — `git clone https://github.com/<you>/flowminer.git`. (2) `git tag --list` returns empty — no tags have been pushed; CHANGELOG.md references a v0.1.0 tag and release.yml fires on `v*` tags, but the tag does not exist locally. (3) FUNDING.yml contains the comment "Replace the placeholder handles with real ones before publishing." (4) No marketing site, blog, G2/Capterra/Product Hunt references exist anywhere in the codebase. OVERSTATED OR WRONG: (5) The claim says "no demo URL referenced" — this is false. /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/deploy/demo/README.md is a full, production-grade demo deployment guide for `demo.flowminer.io`, including Caddy TLS, systemd unit, hourly seeder reset, write-guard middleware, and anonymous JWT login. The URL is explicitly referenced multiple times. (6) The flowminer.io emails and github.com/flowminer/flowminer URLs are internally consistent org coordinates used across SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CHANGELOG.md, FUNDING.yml, and deploy/demo/README.md — they are a chosen org identity, not random placeholders (though whether the GitHub org is live is unverifiable locally). The demo-deploy README even uses a distinct org `flowminer-stack` for the VPS clone path, showing deliberate naming decisions.
verdict.adjusted: The claim is substantially correct on the three highest-signal items: the `<you>` clone URL placeholder appears in three files (README, CONTRIBUTING, why-flowminer.md) and is the most glaring trust signal failure for anyone cloning; zero git tags exist despite the CHANGELOG and release workflow referencing v0.1.0; and there is zero distribution surface (no marketing site, no blog, no review listings). These are real problems to fix. However, the claim is wrong that "no demo URL is referenced" — a complete, engineering-quality demo deployment for demo.flowminer.io exists at /home/josh/Documents/Projects/flowminer/deploy/demo/README.md, meaning the demo infrastructure is designed and coded but not yet deployed. Corrected action: (a) Replace `<you>` with the real org in README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and docs/why-flowminer.md — this is a three-line fix with outsized credibility impact; (b) Push the v0.1.0 tag to make the release pipeline fire and produce GHCR images + a GitHub release; (c) Deploy demo.flowminer.io — the code is entirely ready, it just needs a VPS and DNS; (d) The distribution gap (no blog, no review-site listings) is real and unaddressed by any existing code or roadmap item.

positioning.title: Strong positioning exists in docs but is invisible inside the product
positioning.description: FlowMiner has a genuinely excellent positioning document (docs/why-flowminer.md) — honest comparison table vs Celonis/Apromore CE/Disco/pm4py, the 'depth of Celonis, self-host freedom, no AGPL trap / no open-core paywall / no six-figure contract' line, and a credible 'where FlowMiner is NOT the answer' section. But none of it is reachable in-product. There is no /why, /compare, or /pricing route in App.tsx; the LoginPage and RegisterPage carry only generic 'Open-source process mining, MIT licensed — no lock-in' copy. A frustrated Celonis/Apromore evaluator who installs FlowMiner never encounters the argument for why it solves their specific pain (price shock, consultant dependency, open-core wall). The single best positioning asset in the repo is doing zero conversion work because it lives in a markdown file most evaluators will never open.
positioning.competitor_evidence: Celonis switchers cite price-shock ($286K median, $200K+/business unit) and CoE/consultant dependency as the top leave-drivers; Apromore switchers are stranded by the archived open-core repo; Disco loyalists want simplicity. The whole research corpus is a list of pains that why-flowminer.md already answers — the answer just isn't surfaced where buyers decide.
positioning.flowminer_status: docs/why-flowminer.md (full comparison + honest caveats) and SUPPORT.md (commercial-support story) exist and are high quality. README.md links to why-flowminer.md. But grep of frontend/src/App.tsx shows no /why|/compare|/pricing route, and LoginPage.tsx/RegisterPage.tsx contain only generic one-liner positioning. The doc is not surfaced in-product anywhere.
positioning.recommendation: Add an in-product, lazy-loaded /why (or /compare) page that renders the why-flowminer.md argument as a polished comparison view, linked from the LoginPage, the empty-project state, and a sidebar 'Why FlowMiner' / 'Compare' entry. Mirror it on a public marketing route so it is the first thing a Celonis/Apromore searcher hits. The content is already written — this is surfacing, not authoring.

positioning.title: No migration path from competitor exports (Disco .dsc, Celonis, Apromore) — the switching-cost lever is unaddressed
positioning.description: Switching cost is the single most-repeated reason buyers STAY on an incumbent (sunk pipelines, dashboards, trained CoE). FlowMiner's strongest GTM moment is the Apromore community-edition exodus (ApromoreCore archived Aug 2025, ApromoreDocker Sept 2025 — those users are actively stranded and shopping) and Disco users who want a server tool. Yet there is no importer for any competitor's native format: no Disco .dsc handler, no Celonis/Signavio export adapter, no Apromore project importer in backend/app/services/connectors/. A stranded Apromore CE user or a Disco shop has to re-do their column mapping and rebuild from raw CSV, which feels exactly like the migration pain the research says blocks switches. FlowMiner already advertises 'leaving is always cheap' for its OWN data (JSON export by SHA-256) but offers no cheap way IN from a competitor.
positioning.competitor_evidence: Apromore's own migration press release warns of 'rebuilding dashboards, connectors, filters when switching' as a major switching cost — now ironically applicable to stranded Apromore CE users post-Salesforce. Disco exports XES/MXML only ('closed data'); Disco users 'graduate' when they need conformance/collaboration. Research: 'organizations stay due to sunk-cost investment in pipelines.'
positioning.flowminer_status: ls of backend/app/services/connectors/ shows CSV, XES, OCEL, SAP, SaaS connectors but NO Disco/.dsc, Celonis, or Apromore importers. XES import exists (xes_connector.py) which partially covers Disco/ProM export, but there is no first-class 'Migrate from X' flow, no Disco .dsc parser, and no mapping-preservation. why-flowminer.md sells cheap EXIT (project export) but says nothing about cheap ENTRY from a competitor.
positioning.recommendation: Build a 'Switch to FlowMiner' import flow: (1) a Disco .dsc / XES importer that auto-carries the column mapping (FlowMiner already auto-detects, so this is mostly UX framing + a .dsc parser), (2) a documented Apromore-CE / Celonis CSV-export recipe in the Log Builder. Then position it loudly: 'Stranded on Apromore Community? Import your logs in 60 seconds.' This converts an externally-created wave of displaced users.

positioning.title: No public hosted demo or 'try without installing' path — highest-friction top-of-funnel for a self-host tool
positioning.description: FlowMiner has a genuinely excellent demo seeder (5 pre-mapped real logs incl. the full 251K-case BPIC2019, idempotent, OCEL warm-loading, DEMO_MODE gating, demo-guard middleware) — but it is only reachable by someone who already cloned the repo and ran docker compose. There is no public hosted demo URL, and the README has no 'try it online' link (grep found none). For a self-hostable tool competing against SaaS incumbents that offer instant cloud trials, requiring 'clone + make init-env + make up' before a buyer sees a single process map is the biggest top-of-funnel leak. The asset to remove this friction is already built; the distribution of it is missing.
positioning.competitor_evidence: Research repeatedly faults incumbents for the OPPOSITE failure (Celonis/Signavio/Apromore: 'no instant trial with real data... multiple sales calls before any access'). ProcessMind/Mindzie win specifically on 'instant onboarding, no consultant.' Disco wins on 'value virtually immediately after downloading.' A frictionless demo is table stakes that FlowMiner can beat incumbents on but currently doesn't expose.
positioning.flowminer_status: backend/app/services/demo_seeder.py is full (5 DEMO_PROJECTS pre-mapped, hourly re-seed, OCEL warm-load) and demo_guard.py middleware exists — DEMO_MODE is production-ready. But README.md has no hosted-demo link; grep for demo.flowminer/app.flowminer/try-online found nothing. The capability exists; there is no public deployment of it referenced anywhere.
positioning.recommendation: Stand up a public read-only DEMO_MODE instance at a stable URL and make 'Try the live demo (no install)' the first CTA in the README and on the /why page. This is mostly ops (deploy the already-built demo mode behind the existing Dokploy/Traefik topology) plus one README line — disproportionate funnel impact for low effort.

positioning.title: Trust-proof trifecta is absent: no tagged releases, no public roadmap link, no reference/credibility signals
positioning.description: Risk-averse buyers (the exact ones leaving Celonis/Apromore over vendor-stability fear) need proof a tool is real and maintained. FlowMiner has a CHANGELOG.md but ZERO git tags (git tag returns empty) — so there is no versioned release a buyer can pin to, no '1.0', no release cadence to demonstrate momentum. The README honestly says 'pre-1.0, UI still evolving,' which is good honesty but, combined with no releases and no public proof points, reads as 'unproven' to a procurement team. Apromore's thin independent review base is explicitly called out as a trust failure ('enterprises can't find peer proof'); FlowMiner currently has even less external signal. There is no SBOM, no public security advisory history, and no reference deployments.
positioning.competitor_evidence: Apromore hated point: '0 reviews on PeerSpot/Capterra/Slashdot — this thinness itself is a trust signal, enterprises can't find peer proof.' Gartner MQ Leader status repeatedly cited as 'procurement cover.' ARIS/Apromore buyers actively fleeing over 'vendor stability / roadmap continuity' fears. Buyers need a credibility anchor FlowMiner does not yet provide.
positioning.flowminer_status: CHANGELOG.md exists but git tag is empty (no tagged releases). SECURITY.md exists (72h ack, coordinated disclosure). SUPPORT.md describes governance + roadmap in docs/roadmap/. No SBOM, no public reference customers, no analyst presence, no review-site listing. README status badge says 'pre-1.0' with no release link.
positioning.recommendation: Cut tagged, semver releases with a maintained CHANGELOG (immediate, S); publish an SBOM and a one-page architecture/security overview; cultivate 2-3 named or anonymized reference deployments and a handful of independent reviews (G2/SourceForge/AlternativeTo). For an open-source tool the GitHub equivalent of MQ-cover is stars + release cadence + visible CI/test-pass badges — make the passing test suite and Rust-accel benchmarks visible as trust proof.

positioning.title: Cost-savings / ROI value-realization layer is built but silent at the positioning level
positioning.description: The single most damaging incumbent critique is 'over 2-in-3 process intelligence initiatives under-delivered' and 'the story stays on the dashboard, nothing changes' (insight-to-action gap). FlowMiner has actually built the answer — Initiatives/ROI tracker with baseline+target+/measure recompute, a value-calculator library, scorecards with cost-of-quality FTE-hour quantification, AutomationRoiPage, OverviewPage value cards (realized savings, working capital), Mission Control automation-ROI strip, and action rules that close the loop to Tasks. But the POSITIONING never leads with this. why-flowminer.md sells license/sovereignty/depth; it does not say 'FlowMiner quantifies and tracks the dollar value you realize, so you don't end up in the 2/3 that fail.' The strongest counter-positioning against the industry's worst pain is buried as a feature rather than led as a message.
positioning.competitor_evidence: HFS: 'over 2-in-3 process intelligence initiatives under-delivered.' BPM-d: 'insight generated, acknowledged, then left at observation.' Mavim: 'buried in dashboards, but nothing changes.' Celonis's own pitch is value-realization but Glassdoor calls it 'overhyped value realization story.' This is the open flank — a tool that PROVES realized value wins the argument incumbents keep losing.
positioning.flowminer_status: Built and wired: backend/app/api/initiatives.py (baseline/target/current + /measure live recompute + get_calculators), api/scorecards.py (cost-of-quality FTE quantification), frontend AutomationRoiPage.tsx, OverviewPage.tsx (realized-savings/working-capital cards), MissionControlPage.tsx (automation ROI). Mature feature layer. why-flowminer.md and README features list do NOT lead with value-realization/ROI as a positioning pillar.
positioning.recommendation: Add a value-realization pillar to why-flowminer.md and the README ('Close the loop — track the dollars, not just the diagrams. Baseline → action → measured savings, all in the open product'). Lead the /why page and Mission Control empty state with the ROI tracker. This is messaging on top of shipped capability — pure S-effort leverage against the industry's #1 failure narrative.

positioning.title: No published pricing / packaging model for the commercial-support tier — the exact transparency buyers crave
positioning.description: Across EVERY competitor profile, opaque 'contact sales' pricing is a top hated item, and transparent published pricing is repeatedly named as the thing buyers want (IBM and ProcessMind win partly on transparency alone). FlowMiner's product is free (MIT), which is a huge advantage — but its commercial offering (priority SLA support, managed hosting, deployment/ERP-extraction help) in SUPPORT.md is itself 'email hello@flowminer.io' with no tiers, no price ranges, no packaging. FlowMiner is reproducing the exact opacity it criticizes incumbents for, on the one thing it does charge for. A buyer evaluating 'can I get a name to call when this breaks' has no idea if that costs $2K or $200K, so they default to assuming enterprise-scary or, worse, assume there's no real support and rule it out.
positioning.competitor_evidence: Universal hated theme: 'No public rate card' (Celonis 4.1/5 Evaluation-and-Contracting, lowest dim), Apromore/Disco/Signavio all 'contact sales.' Buyers explicitly want: 'Published, transparent pricing so buyers can build a business case without a sales call' and 'Flat-rate/per-seat pricing that does not scale with data volume.' IBM/ProcessMind/Mindzie win on transparent published tiers.
positioning.flowminer_status: Product is genuinely free under MIT (LICENSE confirmed). SUPPORT.md lists commercial services (priority SLA, managed hosting, deployment/SAP-extraction help, custom dev) but with NO pricing, NO tiers — just 'email hello@flowminer.io.' No /pricing page in App.tsx. The placeholder email/org (flowminer.io, github.com/flowminer/flowminer) also signal pre-launch.
positioning.recommendation: Publish a simple, transparent commercial-support packaging table (e.g. Community free / Supported flat annual / Managed-hosting per-instance) with at least ranges, mirroring the transparency FlowMiner positions against. Even 'starts at $X/year, no per-GB, no per-process, no per-seat data tax' is a wedge against Celonis APC and per-process licensing. Make 'unlimited processes, unlimited data volume, flat fee' an explicit anti-Celonis pricing message.

positioning.title: No vertical / use-case packaging despite shipped recipes — buyers can't self-identify
positioning.description: Incumbents win SAP shops with P2P/O2C/R2R out-of-the-box benchmarks, and the open-source pain is 'community users must build everything from scratch — no pre-built templates for common processes.' FlowMiner has actually shipped 6 vertical recipes and content-pack recipes (log_builder_recipes.py, demo content packs, the close-the-loop branch's vertical packs), plus prebuilt process packs surfaced in onboarding. But positioning is entirely horizontal: README and why-flowminer.md describe ALGORITHMS (inductive miner, OCEL, conformance) not OUTCOMES (cut P2P maverick spend, hit O2C SLAs, audit four-eyes compliance). A P2P analyst leaving Celonis cannot tell from FlowMiner's positioning that it does their job; they see a generalist toolkit. The vertical recipes exist but the GTM doesn't package them as 'FlowMiner for Procure-to-Pay / Order-to-Cash / IT Service Management.'
positioning.competitor_evidence: Celonis/Signavio loved for out-of-box P2P/O2C/R2R KPIs and 'fastest time-to-value for SAP best-practice benchmarking.' Apromore CE hated: 'community users must build everything from scratch, no pre-built templates.' Open-source missing: 'pre-built industry templates.' Buyers self-identify by process area, not algorithm.
positioning.flowminer_status: Shipped: backend/app/services/log_builder_recipes.py, demo content-pack recipes (per connection-journey memory: 3 process content-pack recipes), close-the-loop branch added 6 vertical recipes, onboarding wizard surfaces prebuilt process packs. The recipes exist. README/why-flowminer.md positioning is algorithm-centric, not vertical/outcome-centric. No 'FlowMiner for P2P/O2C/ITSM' framing anywhere.
positioning.recommendation: Repackage the existing recipes as named vertical solution pages ('FlowMiner for Procure-to-Pay', 'for Order-to-Cash', 'for IT Service Management / Jira', 'for Healthcare pathways via state-aware OCPM'), each with the demo log, the recipe, and the relevant ROI calculator pre-wired. Lead with outcomes. This is packaging shipped capability, so most cost is content + a recipe-gallery page.

positioning.title: Sovereignty / data-residency moat is real and well-argued but not aimed at the named regulated segment that no incumbent can serve
positioning.description: why-flowminer.md section 5 makes the on-prem/sovereign case well and honestly (Fernet-at-rest, local Ollama option, honest pseudonymisation-not-anonymisation framing, RBAC+audit). This is FlowMiner's most defensible moat: EVERY major competitor (Celonis, Signavio, Microsoft, UiPath, IBM-mostly) is cloud-only and structurally CANNOT serve EU banking / healthcare / government / defence. But the positioning is generic ('on-prem and sovereign by default') rather than segment-targeted at the buyers who are STRUCTURALLY DISQUALIFIED from the incumbents. There is no 'For regulated industries' / 'For the public sector' / 'For air-gapped deployments' landing that names GDPR, data-residency, and the Celonis-SAP data-toll risk as the wedge. The strongest moat is pitched as a feature bullet instead of a go-to-market beachhead.
positioning.competitor_evidence: Repeated across all profiles: 'SaaS-only deployment — regulated industries cannot send ERP data to US cloud.' 'CPM not compatible with country cybersecurity policy.' Celonis-SAP antitrust: data-access can become a mid-contract 'toll booth.' Both Microsoft and SAP 'explicitly abandon' the sovereignty/SMB segment. This is an uncontested beachhead.
positioning.flowminer_status: why-flowminer.md section 5 covers it well with honest caveats (pseudonymisation vs anonymisation, RBAC as the real boundary). Backend has privacy.py/anonymizer.py, audit_logs.py, encrypted-at-rest secrets, local-Ollama support. Capability is real. Positioning is a generic section, not a named-segment GTM beachhead; no regulated-industry/public-sector landing or messaging.
positioning.recommendation: Carve a 'For regulated / sovereign deployments' positioning beachhead that names the segment (EU banking, healthcare, public sector, defence), the disqualifier (cloud-only incumbents can't serve you), and the proof (air-gapped, local-LLM, encrypted-at-rest, RBAC+audit, honest privacy framing). This is the wettest, least-contested wedge — make it a primary message, not a section 5 bullet.

positioning.title: 'Cheaper + sovereign' pitch risks reading as 'budget tool' — under-claims the depth that actually beats incumbents
positioning.description: An earlier internal audit found the cheaper+sovereign pitch is INVERTED — the product is deep, but cheap-positioning makes risk-averse enterprise buyers discount it. The research corroborates the danger: open-source tools are dismissed as lacking 'performance, support, polish,' and 'budget' framing pushes you toward the SMB segment where willingness-to-pay is lowest. FlowMiner's true differentiator is that it has Celonis-CLASS depth (OCEL 2.0 + state-aware OCPM, stochastic conformance JSD/EMD, queue mining Erlang-C, causal LiNGAM, DES simulation, predictive+SHAP, Rust acceleration) that NO other open/affordable tool has — pm4py is a library, Disco is discovery-only, Apromore CE is gutted. Surface copy leads with what it COSTS (free/MIT) before what it IS (the only self-hostable tool with enterprise-grade depth). Leading on price anchors low.
positioning.competitor_evidence: Open-source dismissed for 'lack performance, support, advanced features.' Glassdoor (Celonis): 'competitors catching up at a discount' — discount framing invites the 'cheap imitation' read. Buyers leaving Celonis still want DEPTH (variant explorer, conformance, OCPM); they want to NOT overpay, not to downgrade. The winning frame is 'same depth, your terms,' not 'cheaper.'
positioning.flowminer_status: README headline leads with 'depth of Celonis, self-host freedom... without the six-figure contract' — depth-first, which is correct. But LoginPage/RegisterPage and much surface copy lead with 'open-source / MIT / no lock-in' (cost/freedom framing). Capability map confirms the depth is real (stochastic conformance, OCEL+state-aware OCPM, queue/causal/DES/predictive+SHAP, Rust accel). The pitch ordering is partly inverted on the high-traffic surfaces.
positioning.recommendation: Reorder every positioning surface to lead with DEPTH and uniqueness ('The only self-hostable platform with OCEL 2.0 object-centric mining, stochastic conformance, queue mining, causal discovery, and DES simulation — the depth enterprises pay six figures for'), and treat 'free/MIT/sovereign' as the closer, not the headline. Add a one-line proof: 'No other open or affordable tool ships this depth — pm4py is a library, Disco is discovery-only, Apromore CE locks conformance and simulation behind sales.'

positioning.title: AI assistant + MCP server is a category-defining wedge that positioning treats as just another feature
positioning.description: FlowMiner ships a data-grounded AI chat (tool-use, inline chart/filter rendering), an Extraction Copilot that writes the ETL SQL, an LLM column-mapper, and — uniquely — an MCP server so Claude Desktop/Cursor/Zed can query a FlowMiner instance as a tool, provider-agnostic incl. local Ollama. This directly neutralizes TWO of the biggest incumbent pains at once: PQL lock-in ('a proprietary language no AI is trained on, every analyst needs Celonis-specific training') and the ETL/data-prep tax (60-80% of project time). No incumbent offers an open, self-hostable, no-query-language, MCP-native AI layer — Celonis Copilot is cloud-only and degrades on messy Knowledge Models; Microsoft Copilot 'can't do ETL' and only sees common variants. The roadmap even notes the 'first open-source process-mining MCP' blog angle. Yet positioning lists AI as one feature pillar among many rather than as the wedge that makes FlowMiner self-serviceable by a single analyst (no CoE, no PQL).
positioning.competitor_evidence: Celonis: 'PQL only Celonis uses, little help online or via AI'; 'every analyst hire needs Celonis-specific training.' 'No mature open-source web app wraps pm4py for non-coders.' This is a true open-flank.

# FlowMiner Competitive UX & Feature Audit
**Date: 2026-06-10**

## 1. Executive Summary

FlowMiner is, on the evidence of its own codebase, the deepest self-hostable process mining platform in existence. It ships capabilities that the entire open-source ecosystem lacks and that commercial incumbents charge six figures for: stochastic conformance (JSD/EMD), queue mining (Erlang-C), causal discovery (LiNGAM), discrete-event simulation, predictive monitoring with SHAP, OCEL 2.0 with state-aware OCPM, and a Rust acceleration layer that makes large-log analysis tractable. Layered on top is an AI assistant with tool-use, an Extraction Copilot that writes the ETL SQL, an LLM column-mapper, and — uniquely in this market — an MCP server that lets Claude Desktop/Cursor/Zed query a FlowMiner instance directly. pm4py is a library, Disco is discovery-only, Apromore Community Edition is gutted and now archived. FlowMiner is none of those things. The product is genuinely good.

**The single biggest thing holding it back is not capability — it is that almost nobody can find the capability, and almost nobody knows the product exists.** Two binding constraints dominate everything else. First, *discoverability*: roughly 16 of the most differentiating analysis pages (Causal Map, Cases-at-Risk, Automation ROI, Process Health, Drift, Root Cause, Social Network, Simulation) are reachable only via the ⌘K palette or by drilling into a project card — they appear nowhere a browsing user would look. The AI layer renders a raw error dump instead of a setup prompt when no key is configured. The post-upload landing screen is the most control-dense surface in the product. The deep backend is largely unreachable through the conversational interface non-technical users actually use. Second, *distribution*: there are no git tags, the README clone URL is literally `github.com/<you>/flowminer.git`, there is no public demo link (despite a fully-built demo deployment kit sitting in the repo), and FlowMiner appears in zero "Celonis alternative" comparison articles where buyers are actively searching right now.

The competitive opening is enormous and time-sensitive. Celonis is bleeding mid-market and regulated buyers over price ($286K median enterprise contract), mandatory Centers of Excellence, proprietary PQL lock-in, and cloud-only architecture. SAP Signavio jacked prices post-acquisition and treats non-SAP data as second-class. **Apromore's open-source Community Edition was archived in August–September 2025 after the Salesforce acquisition — those self-hosting users are stranded and shopping right now**, and FlowMiner has no importer to catch them. Every major incumbent is structurally cloud-only and cannot serve EU banking, healthcare, government, or defence — an uncontested beachhead FlowMiner owns by architecture.

**The top five moves, in order:**

1. **Make depth discoverable.** Add a browsable "Analyses" catalog to the sidebar, fix the AI-no-key dead-ends, surface the data-quality report on the landing screen, and expand the AI chat tool catalogue to expose the cases-at-risk / simulation / SNA backends that already exist. These are mostly S/M-effort fixes that convert a hidden asset into a visible one.
2. **Win the distribution war.** Push a `v0.1.0` tag (the release pipeline is already wired), deploy the already-built `demo.flowminer.io`, replace the `<you>` placeholder, and seed "Celonis/Apromore alternative" comparison content. Capability is done; ROI is now almost entirely in being findable.
3. **Catch the Apromore exodus.** Ship a "Migrate from Disco/Apromore" XES importer with mapping auto-carry (≈1 day on existing infrastructure) and market it loudly to stranded CE users.
4. **Reposition around depth + sovereignty + AI/MCP, not "cheap."** Lead every surface with "the depth of Celonis, your infrastructure, no query language, no CoE." Carve an explicit regulated/sovereign beachhead. The positioning doc already says all this — it just isn't surfaced in-product.
5. **Build the close-the-loop write-back** (Jira/ServiceNow issue creation) to neutralize Celonis's single most-cited differentiator (EMS/Action Flows) — the connectors are already authenticated, the write path is an extension, not a greenfield build.

The rest of this report grounds each of these in competitor evidence and verified code.

---

## 2. The Competitive Landscape — what users actually say

### Celonis — the market leader users love to leave

**Loved:** best-in-class variant explorer and visualization ("excelling at the process mining part and showing event logs and process variants" — Gartner Peer Insights); the deepest SAP connector library; PQL's expressiveness for analysts who master it; and the EMS/Action Flows insight-to-action loop, which even critics concede is conceptually unmatched.

**Hated:** Pricing is the dominant complaint. No public rate card; enterprise median of **$286,356/year** (SpendHound, 160 contracts); a consultant quoting the jump from "$15,000 entry-level to $200,000+ when scaling across business units" (PeerSpot). Gartner rates Celonis 4.1/5 on Evaluation & Contracting, its *lowest* dimension. PQL is proprietary lock-in: *"a code that only Celonis uses, so there is little help on the internet or through AI beyond the Celonis documentation"* (Gartner). The platform "cannot be self-served" — it requires a 5–20 FTE Center of Excellence (Celonis' own research, via Diginomica). And it is SaaS-only, structurally excluding regulated industries.

**The switching opening:** Cost, consultant dependency, PQL lock-in, and cloud-only deployment are all things FlowMiner inverts by design. The strongest single quote for FlowMiner's pitch is the Glassdoor employee review: *"Overpriced complicated products with overhyped value realization story — customers do not need all the bells and whistles to do decent process mining; competitors are catching up at a discount."*

### Apromore & the open-source ecosystem — the stranded segment

**Loved:** academic-grade simulation, Gartner Leader recognition, application-neutrality, and a free Community/Core edition that gave researchers and PoC teams a real starting point.

**Hated (and now fatal):** **ApromoreCore was archived read-only on 29 August 2025; ApromoreDocker on 1 September 2025** — *"The source code available in this repository is now deprecated."* The Salesforce acquisition broke the neutrality promise that was the entire reason non-Salesforce shops chose it. The free tier was always gutted (conformance, dashboards, filters, simulation all enterprise-only), and now there is no maintained self-host path at all.

For the broader OSS world the pains are structural: ProM crashes on non-trivial logs and overwhelms users with "200+ plugins with no guidance on which to use"; pm4py "is just a library" with no UI, single-threaded performance, and graphviz dependency hell; and across all of them **ETL is non-existent** — *"ETL functionality in process mining tools is lacking... you are on your own there"* (PMC11646219, 41-analyst study).

**The switching opening:** This is FlowMiner's most direct audience and its most time-sensitive one. Stranded Apromore CE users are *actively shopping* and need a maintained, self-hostable tool with the depth they had — exactly FlowMiner's profile.

### Microsoft & SAP — the suite-bundled hyperscalers

**Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining** wins on M365/Azure gravity and task mining, but is a **$5,000/tenant/month add-on** on top of Power Automate Premium, is "best suited for process discovery" (not conformance or continuous monitoring), cannot do ETL ("isn't equipped with transforming or preparing any ETL work" — its own Copilot FAQ), and degrades sharply on non-Microsoft data.

**SAP Signavio** is frictionless for SAP shops but *"After SAP acquired Signavio, the prices increased significantly, making it too expensive for our small company"* (PeerSpot). Non-SAP data is a "second-class citizen," Process Insights "hardcodes SAP best-practice assumptions" that are "invalid" for evolved processes, and the Celonis-SAP antitrust suit (data-extraction "toll booth") is actively shaping buyer decisions.

**The switching opening:** Both explicitly abandon the SMB, sovereignty, and non-suite segments. Both are cloud-only. FlowMiner's hardcoded-benchmark *avoidance* (overridable reference targets, not SAP-best-practice lock-in) is the safe counter-position.

### UiPath / IBM / ARIS — the second tier

UiPath wins on the RPA-mining loop but has a thin connector library (~10–12 vs Celonis's 100+), "congested" process maps, no drag-and-drop dashboards, and a 30%-of-project SQL data-prep tax. IBM is "too high" priced for SMBs with "thin onboarding documentation." ARIS owns the BPM-to-mining conformance loop but suffers Citrix slowness, multi-day maintenance windows, split modeling/mining environments, and — critically — **vendor-stability fear after the 2025 Software AG divestiture**. All three lose to self-hostable options on cost transparency, data sovereignty, and per-seat/per-event pricing.

### Disco & the simple tools — the UX benchmark

Disco is the cautionary tale FlowMiner must respect. It is beloved for **near-zero time-to-value** ("value virtually immediately after downloading"), **calm intuitive UX** ("a pleasant look and feel, without unnecessary bells and whistles"), and **local-execution privacy**. Its limits — discovery-only, closed data, desktop-only, no collaboration — are exactly where FlowMiner is stronger. But Disco's *feel* is the bar: the moment FlowMiner's first-touch screen feels denser or more intimidating than Disco, it loses the very "fleeing the steep curve" buyers it targets. **This is the most important UX lesson in the entire research corpus.**

---

## 3. What FlowMiner Has Today (grounded in code)

**Genuinely strong (full maturity, verified in code):**

- **Core mining.** Discovery (DFG, Alpha, Heuristic, Inductive IM/IMf, Split Miner v2, ILP) with Rust acceleration (`backend/app/services/discovery.py`, `rust_accel.py` — DFG ~400x, Inductive ~95x byte-identical to pm4py). Conformance across six methods including alignment-based, decomposed SESE, and stochastic JSD/EMD (`conformance.py`). Bottleneck/DBSM scoring (`bottleneck.py`), queue mining (`queue_mining.py`), drift detection (`drift.py`).
- **Predictive/causal/simulation.** Remaining-time GBR, outcome RF, next-activity, suffix prediction, and SLA-breach alarm scoring with proper OOF cross-validation and model persistence (`predictive.py`); DES simulation with resource pools and scenario deltas (`simulation_des.py`); causal LiNGAM DAG (`causal.py`).
- **Operational layer.** Alerts with live `/test` (`alert_engine.py`), action rules with dry-run/cooldown (`action_engine.py`), initiatives/ROI tracker with live `/measure` recompute and 19 value-calculator formulas (`initiatives.py`, `value_calculators.py`), scorecards with cost-of-quality FTE quantification (`scorecards.py`), governance lifecycle (`governance.py`), audit logs, privacy/anonymization.
- **AI/MCP.** Streaming tool-use chat (`ai.py`, `chat_tools.py`), Extraction Copilot (`ai_tools.py`), LLM column-mapper (`mapping_suggester.py`), 9-tool MCP server (`mcp/server.py`), 5-provider abstraction incl. local Ollama (`llm.py`).
- **Onboarding/upload flow.** The CSV → confidence-scored auto-mapping → live-preview ColumnMapper → direct-to-Mission-Control path is the most polished part of the product and beats most commercial tools. The demo seeder (`demo_seeder.py`) ships 5 pre-mapped real logs including the full 251K-case BPIC2019.

**Exists but weak:**

- **OCEL/OCPM.** OC-DFG and summary ship, but OPerA performance metrics require the optional `ocpa` package and error out if absent (`ocel_improvements.py`).
- **Analytical query layer.** Only a case-*filter* DSL (`filter_engine.py`) plus arithmetic over 9 fixed scalar metrics (`custom_kpis.py`). No graph-aware computation (e.g. "avg time A→B per resource group").
- **Streaming.** A real WebSocket live-KPI backend exists (`streaming.py`) but is entirely unwired in the frontend; `ProcessPulsePage` only animates the *static* map.
- **Collaboration.** Threaded annotations on activities/edges work end-to-end, but `@mentions` are a cosmetic placeholder, assignment fires no notification, and there is no shareable "finding" object.
- **Benchmarking.** Two cross-log benchmarks exist but compare only the user's own logs; template KPI targets exist but aren't wired into the benchmark UI as reference baselines.

**Stub:**

- **Task mining.** Capture agent polls window titles only; pattern miner is a bag-of-ngrams counter. The one genuinely differentiated piece — the task→process cross-link endpoint — is buried.

---

## 4. The Gaps That Matter (verified)

### 4A. UX / Usability Gaps

#### G1 — Deep features are undiscoverable (HIGH / M)
**Evidence:** Celonis Community ("the basic 2D process map feels almost like a hidden feature"); ProM ("you don't know what plugins to use"). **Verified state:** ~16 distinct, high-value analysis pages — Causal Map, Cases-at-Risk, Automation ROI, Process Health, Drift, Root Cause, Social Network, Simulation, Dotted Chart, Process City, Lineage, Comparison, Rework, Animation, Pulse, Mission Control — are reachable *only* via ⌘K or project-card drill-down; none appear in the sidebar (`Sidebar.tsx` confirmed; Mission Control is *explicitly* commented out at lines 111–115). The ⌘K button helps but is a *search*, not a *browse*, surface. **This is the inverse of the competitive story:** the deep backend that should win deals is invisible. **Recommendation:** add a persistent browsable "Analyses" catalog grouped by intent (reuse `AnalysisPalette` groups), with one-line descriptions and recommended/locked badges.

#### G2 — Data-quality warnings are invisible in the standard upload flow (HIGH / S)
**Evidence:** 78% of practitioners report data-quality issues as a top challenge (PMC11646219); "wrong conclusions because they skip cleaning event logs" (esystems.fi). **Verified state:** `DataQualityCard` is built and good, but the standard CSV path navigates straight to Mission Control (`UploadPage.tsx` line 212), bypassing the `step==='done'` block (line 466) where the card renders. A first-time user with a messy CSV — the exact target segment — *never sees the quality report.* **Recommendation (option A, low-risk):** on Mission Control, auto-fetch quality stats and show a dismissible banner when severity is high, with one-click jump to the repair tool. This turns a hidden cure into an on-by-default differentiator vs pm4py/Disco/Apromore-CE.

#### G3 — The post-upload landing screen is the densest in the product (HIGH / M)
**Evidence:** Disco loved for "no unnecessary bells and whistles"; UiPath maps hated as "congested." **Verified state:** ProcessView stacks **~21 interactive controls** (9 top-bar + 12 map-strip) before any insight, both rows `flex-wrap` to two lines on medium viewports, and a `w-64` right panel renders even with no node selected. Auto-Clean View only triggers above 80 edges, so small/medium logs land on the full unconstrained surface. **Recommendation:** lower the auto-simplify threshold to ~40 edges; collapse Detail/Clean/count/"what does this mean" into a single "Simplify" control; make the right panel opt-in. Lead new users with a calm view and a one-click "Advanced" reveal.

#### G4 — Three parallel filter mechanisms, self-flagged in code (HIGH / M)
**Evidence:** Celonis "overly cumbersome steps to apply filters" + 15-filter cap; Disco loved for intuitive sliders. **Verified state:** FilterPanel (6 categories), FilterChipBar, and FilterExpressionBar coexist; the code itself flags "Finding #13 — unify the filter systems" in two files. **Recommendation:** make the FilterChipBar the single source of truth (its own tooltip already claims this), demote FilterPanel to a popover editor, and hide the DSL bar behind a power-user toggle.

#### G5 — AI is a silent (worse: error-dumping) no-op without a key (HIGH / S)
**Evidence:** Celonis Copilot is a *loved* differentiator; OSS has no AI-guided analysis at all. **Verified state — worse than feared:** with no LLM key, Mission Control renders the null-provider's raw fallback string (env-var instructions + context dump) *as if it were the executive briefing* — it looks broken. Chat panels stream the same text. The `llm_configured` flag is returned by the API but consumed by only 2 of 5+ AI surfaces. **Recommendation:** read `llm_configured`; render an "Enable AI insights — add a key in Settings → AI" card instead of the dump; repoint existing env-var banners to `/settings?tab=ai`.

#### G6 — AI chat tool catalogue is too narrow (HIGH / M)
**Evidence:** the recurring buyer demand is "self-service analytics without PQL." **Verified state:** only 7 chat tools exist (`chat_tools.py`); the LLM cannot answer "show me the 5 slowest cases," "which cases will breach SLA," "who hands off to whom," or "what if I add a clerk" — despite complete `case_explorer`, `predictive`, `org_mining`, and `simulation_des` backends. The deep analytics are unreachable through the conversational surface non-technical users use, undercutting the no-PQL positioning. **Recommendation:** add `show_slowest_cases`, `show_sna`, `predict_sla_risk`, `simulate_what_if` (each wraps an existing service + a frontend render type). Tools 1–2 are sub-second; 3–4 use the existing model-cache. **This is the single highest-leverage way to convert backend depth into a self-service experience.**

#### G7 — Connector "Test Connection" requires saving credentials first (MEDIUM / M)
**Verified state — confirmed at all three layers:** the test endpoint is ID-keyed and reads only persisted config (`connectors.py` lines 281–301); the frontend gate and a no-op parent handler enforce save-before-test. Data-in is the make-or-break moment; a save-before-validate flow reads as broken. **Recommendation:** add a `POST /connectors/test-config` endpoint accepting raw form-state config without persisting.

#### G8 — Smaller papercuts (MEDIUM–LOW / mostly S)
- **Duration filter** takes raw seconds with a format-mismatched placeholder (`FilterPanel.tsx` 170–197) — replace with a range slider or unit-aware input.
- **Broken `/` shortcut** (`useKeyboardShortcuts.ts` line 12 selects `input[type=text]`; header uses `type="search"`) and **ShortcutsModal omits ⌘K** — two trivial fixes; ⌘K is the entry point to ~30 pages.
- **Product tour** has a broken `ocpm-improvements` selector (spotlights nothing in production) and a backdrop-click that permanently completes the tour with no restart path.
- **Canvas pages** use `calc(100vh-7rem)` (4 pages) which clips on mobile browsers — switch to `100dvh`. Fix before any shared link goes external.
- **Two AI chat surfaces** (FloatingAIChat + AskAI) with no explanation of which to use — add one-line cross-references or consolidate.

### 4B. Missing / Weak Features

#### G9 — No write-back / close-the-loop to source systems (HIGH / L)
**Evidence:** Celonis EMS/Action Flows is the *named core differentiator*; "the story stays on the dashboard, nothing changes" (bpm-d); "2-in-3 initiatives under-delivered" (HFS). **Verified absent:** `dispatch_action()` handles 7 action types, all internal/generic-webhook; `create_task` lands in FlowMiner's *own* task table. No Jira/ServiceNow/Salesforce *write* path exists — but those connectors already hold authenticated httpx clients. **Recommendation:** add `create_jira_issue` / `create_servicenow_incident` action types reusing existing connector auth; surface "where did my action go?" with the external record link. Start Jira + ServiceNow.

#### G10 — Real-time streaming is built but invisible (MEDIUM / M)
**Verified state:** a real WebSocket live-KPI backend exists and is registered (`streaming.py`, `main.py:172`); alerts run on a 5-min batch beat against the stored log; the frontend never connects to the live-KPI stream and `ProcessPulsePage` only animates static data. This is a *wiring* problem, not a build. **Recommendation:** wire a Live-Ops page (sidebar-visible) to the existing stream; fire alert evaluation on ingested events. Market as "real-time process monitoring, self-hosted" — a capability Microsoft and Disco lack entirely.

#### G11 — No analytical query language / graph-aware metrics (MEDIUM / XL)
**Verified state:** only a case-filter DSL + arithmetic over 9 scalars. No "time A→B per resource group." **Recommendation — do NOT build a 150-operator PQL clone.** Lean into the LLM layer: "define a metric in plain English → generated, saveable expression" (the Extraction-Copilot pattern for metrics). This converts Celonis's PQL *strength* into FlowMiner's advantage (no proprietary language, AI-native), directly answering the #1 PQL complaint. Optionally extend the existing `safe_eval` AST with named graph builtins.

#### G12 — Templates/recipes exist but are siloed and uneven (MEDIUM / M)
**Verified state:** 9 log-builder recipes + 19 seed templates exist and *are* surfaced in onboarding and a sidebar Templates page — but TemplatesPage shows blank until an admin clicks "seed," recipe cards link to `/projects?new=1` instead of the builder with the pack pre-applied, and the 3 enterprise recipes (SAP/Salesforce/ServiceNow) lack the default KPIs/alerts the ecommerce/logistics ones have. **Recommendation:** auto-seed on first visit, deep-link recipe cards into the builder, and enrich the enterprise recipes to match.

#### G13 — No external benchmarking; collaboration shallow; task mining a prototype (MEDIUM–LOW)
- **Benchmarking:** wire existing template KPI targets into BenchmarkPage as a labelled "reference target" row — gives Signavio-style "your O2C is 110h vs the 72h reference" anchoring without a licensed dataset.
- **Collaboration:** implement (or remove) the `@mention` placeholder, fire a notification on annotation assignment, add a lightweight shareable "Finding" object.
- **Task mining:** keep and surface the differentiated cross-link endpoint; otherwise defer — the governance overhead (HR/works-council buy-in) makes depth investment XL with uncertain payoff.

#### G14 — A positioning win to bank: most "feared gaps" are already solved
Several capabilities a competitor audit would assume missing are **present and verified** — this is itself a story to tell: a real ROI/value-realization layer, a streaming backend, OCEL 2.0 + state-aware OCPM, stochastic conformance, an MCP server, and a robust onboarding/upload flow. The onboarding-wizard "one-way door" gap was *disproven* (a "Getting started" reopen button exists on the Projects page). The public-demo "missing" gap was *disproven* (a full `deploy/demo/` kit exists — only the README link is missing). These are surfacing problems, not build problems.

---

## 5. Positioning, Pricing & Go-to-Market

FlowMiner has an excellent positioning doc (`docs/why-flowminer.md`) doing **zero conversion work** because it lives in a markdown file no evaluator opens. There is no `/why`, `/compare`, or `/pricing` route, and the Login/Register pages carry generic "MIT licensed, no lock-in" copy with a *commodity* feature list (upload, discover, bottleneck, dashboards) — anything a competitor could write. Fix the surfacing first; the content already exists.

**Reframe the core pitch — depth first, price last.** The internal "cheaper + sovereign" framing is inverted and risks the "budget tool" read that anchors low (Glassdoor: competitors "catching up at a discount"). Buyers leaving Celonis want to *stop overpaying*, not to *downgrade*. Lead with: *"The only self-hostable platform with OCEL 2.0 object-centric mining, stochastic conformance, queue mining, causal discovery, and DES simulation — the depth enterprises pay six figures for, on your infrastructure."* Treat free/MIT/sovereign as the closer. Add the one-line proof: "pm4py is a library, Disco is discovery-only, Apromore CE is archived and gutted."

**Make the AI/MCP wedge the headline, not a feature bullet.** "No query language. No CoE. Ask in plain English — or point your own AI agent at it via MCP" neutralizes *two* incumbent pains at once (PQL lock-in + ETL tax). Ship the roadmap's already-titled "first open-source process-mining MCP server" blog post to reach the Cursor/Zed/Claude-Desktop audience no incumbent is courting.

**Carve the sovereignty beachhead explicitly.** Every major incumbent is cloud-only and *structurally cannot* serve EU banking, healthcare, public sector, or defence. Name the segment, name the disqualifier, name the proof (air-gapped, local Ollama, Fernet-at-rest, RBAC+audit) — and preserve the honest pseudonymisation-not-anonymisation caveat to avoid overclaiming GDPR compliance.

**Lead the value-realization story against the industry's #1 failure narrative.** "Over 2-in-3 process intelligence initiatives under-deliver" is the most damaging incumbent critique — and FlowMiner has *built* the answer (Initiatives tracker, 19 value calculators, cost-of-quality scorecards, Automation ROI). Add a value-realization pillar: "Close the loop — track the dollars, not just the diagrams. Baseline → action → measured savings, in the open product." Pure S-effort messaging on shipped capability.

**Pricing model.** The product is free (MIT) — a real advantage — but the commercial-support tier in SUPPORT.md is itself opaque ("email us," no tiers), reproducing the exact opacity FlowMiner criticizes. Publish a simple table: **Community (free) / Supported (flat annual) / Managed hosting (per-instance)** with at least ranges. Make "unlimited processes, unlimited data volume, flat fee — no per-GB, no per-process, no per-seat data tax" an explicit anti-Celonis-APC message.

**Vertical packaging.** Reframe the 9 shipped recipes as outcome-led solution pages — "FlowMiner for Procure-to-Pay," "for Order-to-Cash," "for IT Service Management / Jira," "for Healthcare pathways" — each pre-wiring the demo log, recipe, KPIs, and ROI calculator. Buyers self-identify by process area, not algorithm.

---

## 6. Prioritized Roadmap

|---|------|-----|--------|-----------------|
| **NOW — quick wins, mostly days** | | | | |
| 1 | Push `v0.1.0` tag + replace `<you>` placeholder URLs | High | S | Materializes GHCR release + GitHub Releases page; removes the single most damaging trust signal |
| 2 | Deploy `demo.flowminer.io` (kit already built) + add "Try live" CTA to README | High | S | Removes the biggest top-of-funnel leak for a self-host tool |
